plan.title: How this course takes you from band 4 to 8+
paras: Five levels: Foundation (4.0 → 5.0), Developing (5.0 → 6.0), Competent (6.0 → 7.0), Advanced (7.0 → 7.5) and Expert (7.5 → 8.0+). Every unit trains all four skills around one common IELTS topic: academic vocabulary, Speaking Parts 1–3, a reading passage with True / False / Not Given, two grammar structures and a timed Writing task with a model answer.

Pace: one unit every 3–4 days, about 45–60 minutes a day, plus the outside practice listed under each level. From band 4.0, reaching 8.0 usually takes 18–24 months of steady work. Moving up one full band generally needs a few hundred hours of focused practice in total.

Honest note: no website can guarantee a band score. This course builds the vocabulary, grammar, speaking fluency and essay structure that high bands need. To reach 8.0–9.0 you must also do timed Cambridge IELTS practice tests, read long academic texts, listen to native-speed English every day, and get your Writing and Speaking marked by a qualified teacher.
Model answers and their band labels are written by desktopchill as study references. They are not official, examiner-marked scripts.
weeks: Everyday topics. Answer Part 1 questions with a reason and an example; describe simple tables; write a clear four-paragraph opinion essay.
Society topics. Extend Part 3 answers; describe trends accurately; plan discussion and problem–solution essays; reduce basic grammar errors.
Abstract topics. Use less common vocabulary and complex sentences with control; handle every Task 1 chart type; build cohesive arguments.
Precision. Collocations, hedging and nuance; Part 3 speculation and evaluation; essays with fully developed, well-supported ideas.
Exam conditions. A full mock test every week, teacher feedback on Writing and Speaking, and fixing the last error patterns.
When you score 8.0 or higher on three Cambridge practice tests in a row under real timing, and a teacher rates your Writing and Speaking at 7.5 or above.

levels.name: Band 4→5
levels.title: Foundation: everyday topics
levels.desc: Hometown, study and work, routines, family, food, shopping, travel, technology, transport and sport — the topics of Speaking Part 1.
goals: Answer Part 1 questions in 2–3 sentences with a reason and an example
Speak for 1–2 minutes about a familiar person, place or object
Describe a simple table or bar chart in about 150 words
Write a four-paragraph opinion essay with a clear position
Use present, past and future tenses, comparatives and basic linkers correctly
extra: Cambridge IELTS 10–12: one Listening section a day, checking the transcript
Read one short news article a day (BBC Learning English, News in Levels level 3)
Record yourself answering three Part 1 questions every day and listen back
Write one essay a week and ask a teacher to mark the most common error

lines.t: Let’s talk about your hometown. Where is it?

lines.t: My hometown is Hai Phong, a port city about two hours from Hanoi. It’s famous for seafood.

lines.t: Has it changed much in recent years?

Suburbs have fewer parks than the city centre.

gram.title: Present simple vs present continuous
gram.rule: Present simple: facts and habits (I live, it rains) · Present continuous: now / temporary / changing (I am living, it is growing)
gram.note: Use the present simple for permanent facts and routines: My city has two universities. Use the present continuous for actions happening now, temporary situations and trends: More people are moving to the suburbs. Verbs like know, like, want are rarely continuous.

lines.t: Why do young people move from rural areas to cities?

lines.t: Mainly for jobs and education. Cities have more universities and better-paid work, so young people see more opportunities there.
lines.vi: Chủ yếu vì việc làm và học tập. Thành phố có nhiều trường đại học và việc lương cao hơn, nên người trẻ thấy nhiều cơ hội hơn.

lines.t: It depends. Cities are more convenient, but the countryside is cleaner and more peaceful. For older people, I think rural life is often healthier.
lines.vi: Còn tuỳ. Thành phố tiện hơn, nhưng nông thôn sạch và yên bình hơn. Với người lớn tuổi, tôi nghĩ sống ở nông thôn thường tốt cho sức khoẻ hơn.

gram2.title: Comparatives and superlatives
gram2.rule: short adj + -er / the -est (cheaper, the cheapest) · more / the most + long adj (more convenient) · not as … as · much / a lot + comparative
gram2.note: Use -er/-est for one-syllable adjectives and more/most for longer ones. Irregular: good–better–best, bad–worse–worst. To make a comparison stronger, add much or far: much cheaper. not as … as is a polite way to say “less”: It isn’t as crowded as Hanoi.

cue.card: Describe a place in your hometown that you like.
points: and explain why you like it
model: I’d like to talk about West Lake Park, which is only ten minutes from my house. It’s a large park with a lake in the middle, lots of old trees and a path that goes all the way around the water.

In the early morning it’s full of local residents. Older people do tai chi, some people go jogging, and in the evening families come to walk and buy ice cream. At weekends there are often small music performances near the gate.

I like it for two reasons. First, it’s the most peaceful place in my neighbourhood. The streets around it are crowded and noisy, but once you are inside, you can hear birds. Second, it has a lot of memories for me, because my grandfather taught me to ride a bike there. Whenever I feel stressed, I go there for a walk and I always feel better afterwards.

write.prompt: The table below shows the population of three cities in 2000 and 2020. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
write.data:
City        2000 (millions)   2020 (millions)
City A      2.1               4.0
City B      3.5               3.9
City C      1.2               1.0
plan: Introduction: paraphrase the task (shows → illustrates; population → number of residents)
Overview: two main features — A grew fastest; C was the only city to shrink
Body 1: City A and City B with exact figures
Body 2: City C, and one comparison across all three
model: The table illustrates how many people lived in three cities, A, B and C, in 2000 and 2020.
Overall, the populations of City A and City B increased over the period, with City A showing by far the biggest rise. City C was the only city whose population fell.

In 2000, City A had 2.1 million residents, which was fewer than City B. However, over the next twenty years its population almost doubled to 4 million, making it the largest of the three cities by 2020. City B started with the highest figure, 3.5 million, and grew only slightly, reaching 3.9 million in 2020.

City C was the smallest city in both years. Its population went down from 1.2 million to 1 million, a drop of around 17 per cent. As a result, by 2020 City A was four times bigger than City C, whereas in 2000 the difference between them had been much smaller.

gram.title: Past simple vs present perfect
gram.rule: Past simple: finished time (I graduated in 2020) · Present perfect: life experience / up to now (I have worked here for three years)
gram.note: Use the past simple with a finished time: yesterday, last year, in 2019, two years ago. Use the present perfect when the time is not finished or not stated, often with for, since, already, ever, yet: I have worked here since 2021. Don’t say “I have graduated in 2020”.

cue.card: Describe a job you would like to do in the future.
points: how you could get this job
and explain why you would like to do it
model: In the future, I’d really like to work as a project manager for large construction projects, such as bridges or hospitals.

This job needs a mix of technical and people skills. You need engineering knowledge to understand the drawings, but you also need to communicate clearly, plan schedules and solve problems quickly when something goes wrong on site.

To get this job, I think I need two or three more years of experience as an engineer first. I’m also planning to take a project management qualification, and of course my English has to be much better, because many big projects involve foreign partners.

The main reason I’d like to do it is that I enjoy seeing the whole picture. At the moment I only work on one part of a building. As a project manager, I could lead a team and see a project from the first drawing to the opening day, which I think would give me a lot of satisfaction.

write.prompt: Some people think that universities should focus on practical skills for work. Others believe that the main purpose of university is to give students knowledge. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
plan: Introduction: paraphrase both views and give your opinion (both matter, but knowledge comes first)
Body 1: why practical skills matter — employers, internships, example
Body 2: why knowledge matters — deep understanding, changing jobs, example
Conclusion: restate your opinion in one or two sentences
model: Some people argue that universities should mainly prepare students for the workplace, while others think their key role is to provide knowledge. In my view, both are important, but a strong foundation of knowledge should come first.

On the one hand, practical skills help graduates find jobs. Many employers complain that new graduates know a lot of theory but cannot use software, write a clear report or work in a team. If universities include internships and real projects, students can gain experience before they graduate. For example, engineering students who spend a semester at a construction company often get job offers from the same company.

On the other hand, the main value of a degree is deep knowledge that lasts for a long time. Practical skills change quickly; a computer program that students learn today may be out of date in five years. However, a student who really understands the principles of physics or economics can learn new tools easily. In addition, universities are places for research and critical thinking, not only for job training.

In conclusion, although practical skills are clearly useful, I believe universities should focus first on giving students solid knowledge, and then add practical training on top of it. This combination will prepare graduates not only for their first job but for a whole career.

cue.card: Describe a hobby you enjoy.
points: when and how you started it
and explain why you enjoy it
model: I’d like to talk about photography, which I took up about three years ago. At first I just used my phone, but last year I saved up and bought a second-hand camera.

I usually go out to take photos on Sunday mornings, when the streets are still quiet. I especially like taking pictures of old buildings and local markets in Hanoi. Occasionally I join a small photography club, and we go on trips to the countryside together.

I enjoy it for a few reasons. First of all, it helps me relax. During the week my job is quite stressful, but when I’m looking for a good photo, I forget about work completely. Secondly, it makes me notice details that I used to ignore, like the light on a wall or the faces of people in the market. Finally, it’s a great way to socialise, because I have met lots of interesting people through the club.

write.prompt: The bar chart below shows how many hours per week people in four age groups spent on three leisure activities. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
write.data:
Hours per week   16–24   25–39   40–59   60+
Social media      14      9       5       2
Sport             5       3       2       2
Reading           2       3       4       7
plan: Introduction: paraphrase (bar chart, hours per week, age groups)
Overview: social media falls with age, reading rises with age
Body 1: social media and sport across the groups
Body 2: reading, and the over-60s compared with the youngest group
model: The bar chart compares the number of hours per week that people in four age groups spent on social media, sport and reading.
Overall, time spent on social media fell sharply as people got older, while reading showed the opposite pattern. Sport was the least time-consuming activity for every group except the oldest.

The 16–24 group spent 14 hours a week on social media, which was the highest figure in the chart. This dropped to 9 hours for people aged 25–39, 5 hours for those aged 40–59 and only 2 hours for the over-60s. Young people also did the most sport, at 5 hours a week, compared with 2 or 3 hours in the other groups.

In contrast, reading increased steadily with age. The youngest group read for just 2 hours a week, but this rose to 4 hours for people in their forties and fifties and reached 7 hours among the over-60s. In fact, people over 60 spent more than three times as long reading as they did on social media.

cue.card: Describe a person in your family you admire.
points: what he or she is like
what he or she has done
and explain why you admire this person
model: The person I admire most in my family is my grandmother on my mother’s side. She’s eighty now and still lives in our hometown.

She is a very calm and patient person. I have never heard her shout, even when we were naughty children. She’s also incredibly hard-working. When she was young, she used to run a small shop and look after five children at the same time, because my grandfather worked far away.

What I admire most is how she brought up her children. She didn’t have much education herself, but she saved every bit of money so that all five of them could go to university. Three of them became teachers.

I think she had a big influence on me. Whenever I feel that my job is too stressful, I remember how much harder her life was, and how she never complained. I take after her a little, I think, because people say I’m patient too.

write.prompt: In many countries, young adults now live independently instead of with their parents. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase and state your view (advantages outweigh disadvantages)
Body 1: disadvantages — cost, loneliness, less support for parents
Body 2: advantages — independence, skills, relationships; stronger point
Conclusion: restate your view
model: In many parts of the world, it is becoming more common for young adults to move out of their parents’ home and live on their own. Although this trend has some drawbacks, I believe its benefits are greater.

There are certainly some disadvantages. Firstly, living alone is expensive. Young people have to pay rent and bills, so they may save less money than if they stayed at home. Secondly, some young adults feel lonely, especially if they move to a new city for work. Finally, when children leave home, their parents may receive less help, which can be a problem as they get older.

However, the advantages are more significant. The most important one is personal development. When young people live independently, they have to cook, manage a budget and solve problems by themselves, and these skills make them more confident adults. In addition, living apart can actually improve family relationships. Many people find that they get on better with their parents when they visit at weekends instead of arguing about small things every day. Moreover, with modern technology, it is easy to keep in touch and support each other from a distance.

In conclusion, while living independently costs more and can be lonely at first, I believe the advantages, especially the chance to become a mature and responsible adult, clearly outweigh the disadvantages.

cue.card: Describe a healthy habit you have.
points: and explain why you think it is healthy
model: One healthy habit I have is walking to work instead of taking a motorbike. I started it about a year ago, when my company moved to an office about two kilometres from my apartment.

At first I only did it because parking was expensive, but now I really enjoy it. It takes me about twenty-five minutes each way, so I walk almost an hour a day without having to find extra time for exercise.

It has affected my life in several positive ways. I sleep better, I have more energy in the morning, and I’ve lost about four kilos without changing my diet much. It also gives me time to think about my day or listen to English podcasts, which helps my listening skills.

I think it’s healthy because doctors recommend at least thirty minutes of physical activity every day, and most office workers sit for eight or nine hours. Walking is free, easy and safe, so I believe more people should try it, especially in cities with terrible traffic jams.

write.prompt: Fast food is becoming more and more popular. Why is this happening? What can be done to encourage people to eat healthier food?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase and outline the answer (causes + solutions)
Body 1: causes — busy lifestyles, price, advertising
Body 2: solutions — education in schools, labels and taxes, cheaper healthy options
Conclusion: summarise
model: In many countries, fast food is now part of everyday life. This essay will explain the main reasons for this trend and suggest some ways to encourage healthier eating.

There are several reasons why fast food is so popular. The first is the busy modern lifestyle. Many people work long hours and spend a lot of time commuting, so they do not have the time or energy to cook. Fast food is quick and available almost everywhere. Secondly, it is often cheap, which makes it attractive to students and young workers. Finally, fast-food companies spend huge amounts of money on advertising, especially on social media, and children are strongly influenced by these adverts.

However, there are a number of things that could be done. To begin with, schools should teach children how to cook simple, nutritious meals and explain the health risks of junk food. In addition, governments could make clear labels compulsory, so that people can see how much sugar, salt and fat a product contains. A tax on sugary drinks, like the ones introduced in several countries, could also reduce consumption. At the same time, cities could support small restaurants that sell healthy food at a fair price.
In conclusion, fast food is popular mainly because it is fast, cheap and heavily advertised. Better education, clearer information and financial measures could help people make healthier choices.

cue.card: Describe something you bought that you were happy with.
points: where and when you bought it
and explain why you were happy with it
model: I’d like to talk about a second-hand bicycle that I bought about six months ago.

I found it on an online marketplace. The seller was a university student who was moving abroad, so she wanted to sell it quickly. I went to her apartment, checked the brakes and the gears, and rode it around the street before deciding.
It cost me one and a half million dong, which is less than a third of the price of a new one. It was a few years old, but it was clearly good quality and she had looked after it well.

I was happy with it for several reasons. Firstly, it was great value for money. Secondly, it changed my routine: now I cycle to the market and to the park, which keeps me fit. And finally, buying second-hand felt better for the environment than buying something new. I think it’s the best purchase I’ve made in years.

write.prompt: The table below shows the average monthly spending of a household in one city in 2010 and 2020. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
write.data:
Category        2010 ($)   2020 ($)
Housing         300        520
Food            250        280
Transport       120        110
Entertainment    40        130
plan: Introduction: paraphrase (average monthly household spending, two years)
Overview: housing was the biggest cost and rose most; entertainment grew fastest in relative terms; transport was stable
Body 1: housing and food
Body 2: transport and entertainment, with a comparison
model: The table compares how much an average household in one city spent per month on four categories in 2010 and 2020.
Overall, housing was the largest expense in both years and saw the biggest increase in dollar terms. Spending on entertainment more than tripled, while transport costs changed very little.

In 2010, a household spent $300 a month on housing, but by 2020 this had risen to $520, an increase of more than 70 per cent. Food was the second largest category. It went up only slightly, from $250 to $280, so by 2020 households were spending almost twice as much on housing as on food.

Transport was the only category that fell, dropping from $120 to $110 a month. In contrast, spending on entertainment grew dramatically, from just $40 to $130. As a result, in 2020 households spent more on entertainment than on transport, whereas ten years earlier the opposite had been true.

sents.t: Some famous destinations now receive more visitors than they can handle.

lines.vi: Có. Những nơi nổi tiếng có thể bị quá tải và ô nhiễm, và giá cả tăng với người dân địa phương.

gram2.title: Future plans: going to, present continuous, will
gram2.rule: be going to (plans and intentions) · present continuous (fixed arrangements) · will (decisions now, predictions)
gram2.note: Use going to for plans you have already decided: I’m going to visit Japan next year. Use the present continuous for arrangements with a time and place: We’re flying to Da Nang on Friday. Use will for quick decisions and predictions: I think tourism will grow.

drill.vi: Tôi nghĩ du lịch sẽ phát triển trong mười năm tới.

cue.card: Describe a memorable trip you took.
points: and explain why it was memorable
model: I’d like to describe a trip to Ha Giang, in the far north of Vietnam, which I took with three university friends two years ago.

We rented motorbikes in Ha Giang city and spent four days riding along the mountain roads. Our itinerary was quite simple: we rode in the morning, stopped at small villages for lunch, and stayed in family homestays at night, so the accommodation was very cheap.

The scenery was absolutely breathtaking, especially the Ma Pi Leng Pass, where the road runs along the edge of a deep valley. We also visited a local market where people from different ethnic groups came to buy and sell animals and food.

It was memorable for two reasons. First, it was the first long trip I planned completely by myself, without a package holiday. Second, something went wrong: on the third day it was raining heavily and one of the bikes broke down. A family let us stay in their house and cooked dinner for us. That kindness is the thing I remember most.

write.prompt: Tourism brings many benefits to a country, but it also causes problems. Do you think the advantages of tourism outweigh the disadvantages?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase and give your opinion (advantages outweigh, if managed)
Body 1: disadvantages — overcrowding, pollution, rising prices
Body 2: advantages — jobs and income, culture and infrastructure
Conclusion: restate and add the condition (good management)
model: Tourism has become one of the world’s largest industries. Although it can create serious problems, I believe its advantages are greater, as long as it is managed carefully.

There is no doubt that tourism can have negative effects. Famous destinations often become overcrowded, especially in the peak season, which damages the experience for both visitors and residents. Large numbers of tourists also produce rubbish and pollution, and beaches and forests can be harmed. Moreover, when many visitors arrive, the prices of food and housing tend to rise, so local people may struggle to afford them.

Nevertheless, the benefits of tourism are more significant. Above all, it creates jobs, not only in hotels and restaurants but also for farmers, drivers and craftspeople. In poor rural areas, money from tourism can be the main source of income for whole villages. In addition, tourism encourages governments to build better roads, airports and other facilities that local people also use. Finally, it promotes cultural exchange, as visitors learn about local traditions and residents meet people from around the world.

In conclusion, while tourism can lead to overcrowding, pollution and higher prices, I believe these problems can be reduced through good planning, such as limiting visitor numbers at sensitive sites. Therefore, the economic and cultural advantages of tourism outweigh its disadvantages.

lines.t: How often do you use your phone?

gram.title: Present perfect with for, since, already, yet, just
gram.rule: have/has + past participle · for + period · since + starting point · already / just (positive) · yet (negative and questions)
gram.note: The present perfect connects the past and now: I have had this phone for two years. since gives the starting point: since 2022. just = very recently; already = earlier than expected; yet goes at the end of negatives and questions: Have you updated it yet?

ex.t: I have used this app since January.

gram2.note: but joins two clauses in one sentence. However starts a new sentence and is followed by a comma. Although and while introduce a contrasting clause: Although phones are useful, they can be a distraction. Don’t use although and but together.

cue.card: Describe a piece of technology you find useful.
points: and explain why it is useful to you
model: The piece of technology I find most useful is actually quite simple: a pair of wireless headphones with noise cancelling. I got them as a birthday present from my sister about a year ago.

I use them every single day. In the morning I listen to podcasts while I’m commuting on the bus, and at work I use them for video calls with clients. In the evening I sometimes wear them just to have some silence while I read, because my street is very noisy.

They are useful to me for three reasons. First, they help me concentrate. Our office is open-plan, and before I had them the noise was a real distraction. Second, they have improved my English, since I now listen to about an hour of English podcasts a day. And third, they make my commute much more relaxing.
The only drawback is that I sometimes forget to charge them. But overall, I think they were the best present I’ve ever received, and I can’t imagine my daily routine without them now.

write.prompt: Some people think that the internet has brought people closer together. Others think it has made people more isolated. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
plan: Introduction: paraphrase both views; opinion — closer, if used carefully
Body 1: isolation — screen time replaces real contact, comparison and loneliness
Body 2: closer — distance, communities, families abroad
Conclusion: balanced but clear opinion
model: The internet has changed the way people communicate. While some believe it has brought people closer, others argue that it has made them more isolated. In my opinion, it mostly connects people, but only if it is used sensibly.

On the one hand, there are good reasons to think that the internet makes people lonely. Many people spend hours scrolling through social media instead of meeting friends face to face. Even when families eat together, everyone may be looking at a screen. Furthermore, social media often shows perfect versions of other people’s lives, which can make users feel that they are missing out. Some studies have linked heavy social media use with loneliness, especially among teenagers.

On the other hand, the internet allows people to stay in touch in ways that were impossible before. Millions of Vietnamese workers and students live abroad, and video calls let them see their families every day for free. The internet also helps people with the same interests find each other, for example in online groups for new parents or for people with rare illnesses. For many people, these online communities lead to real friendships.

In conclusion, I believe the internet has brought people closer together overall, because it removes distance as a barrier to communication. However, it should support face-to-face relationships rather than replace them.

cue.card: Describe a journey you often make.
points: what you see or do on the way
and explain how you feel about this journey
model: The journey I make most often is my commute from home to the office, which is about eight kilometres across Hanoi.

I usually go by motorbike, and it takes about thirty minutes, although during rush hour it can take almost an hour. Twice a week, when I have meetings in the city centre, I ride to the nearest metro station instead and take the metro.

On the way I pass West Lake, which is the nicest part of the trip, especially early in the morning when the light is soft. After that the road gets very crowded, and I have to concentrate because motorbikes, cars and buses are all fighting for space. On the metro, I usually listen to podcasts or read the news.

To be honest, I have mixed feelings about it. The traffic and the pollution are stressful, and I often arrive at work a bit tired. But the metro part is relaxing, and I’m happy to see the city investing in better public transport. If a metro line opened near my house, I would definitely stop riding my motorbike.

write.prompt: The bar chart below shows the main ways people travelled to work in one city in 2005 and 2025. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
write.data:
% of commuters     2005    2025
Motorbike          65      48
Car                 5      14
Bus/Metro          10      24
Walking/Cycling    20      14
plan: Introduction: paraphrase (percentage of commuters, four modes, two years)
Overview: motorbikes most popular both years but fell; public transport and cars rose
Body 1: motorbikes and walking/cycling (falls)
Body 2: bus/metro and car (rises), with a comparison
model: The bar chart shows the percentage of commuters in one city who used four different types of transport to get to work in 2005 and 2025.

Overall, the motorbike was the most common way to travel to work in both years, although its share fell considerably. By contrast, public transport and cars became much more popular over the twenty-year period.

In 2005, almost two thirds of commuters (65%) travelled by motorbike, but this figure had dropped to less than half (48%) by 2025. Walking and cycling also became less popular, falling from 20% to 14% of journeys.

At the same time, the proportion of people using buses or the metro more than doubled, from 10% to 24%, which made public transport the second most popular option in 2025. The share of commuters who drove a car also rose sharply, from just 5% to 14%. As a result, in 2025 cars were used as often as walking and cycling combined had been used in the past for short commutes, which suggests that the city’s roads became busier with larger vehicles.

cue.card: Describe a sports event you watched.
points: and explain how you felt about it
model: I’d like to talk about the final of a regional football tournament between Vietnam and Thailand, which I watched a couple of years ago.

I didn’t have a ticket to the stadium, so I watched it with about twenty colleagues on a big screen at a café near our office. The atmosphere was incredible. Everyone was wearing red shirts, and the spectators in the café were shouting and singing as if they were in the stadium.

The match was very tense. Thailand scored first, and for a long time it looked like we would lose. Then, about ten minutes before the end, Vietnam scored twice in five minutes. When the final whistle blew, people ran out into the street, waving flags and riding their motorbikes around the city.

I felt really proud and happy, and also a bit surprised at how emotional I was, because I don’t normally care that much about football. I think the reason it was so memorable is that sport brings people together. For one evening, everyone in that café felt like one big team.

write.prompt: Some people believe that children should spend more time doing sports at school, while others think academic subjects are more important. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
plan: Introduction: paraphrase both views; opinion — more sport, without cutting core subjects
Body 1: academic subjects — exams, careers, limited time
Body 2: sport — health, concentration, teamwork
Conclusion: restate opinion
model: There is an ongoing debate about whether schools should give more time to sport or concentrate on academic subjects. Although academic study is clearly essential, I believe children should do more sport at school.

Those who prefer academic subjects argue that school time is limited and that maths, languages and science are the key to future success. Students must pass important exams, and their results often decide which university or job they can get. From this point of view, extra hours of sport might mean less time for the subjects that really count.

However, there are strong arguments for more physical education. Firstly, many children today have a sedentary lifestyle, spending hours in front of screens, and childhood obesity is rising in many countries. Regular sport at school is the only exercise some children get. Secondly, research suggests that physical activity improves concentration and memory, so it may actually help academic performance. Finally, team sports teach skills that classrooms cannot easily teach, such as teamwork, leadership and how to deal with failure.

In conclusion, while academic subjects must remain the main focus of education, I believe schools should provide at least one hour of physical activity every day. Healthy, active children are likely to learn better and become more well-rounded adults.

gram2.note: affect is the verb: Pollution affects our health. effect is the noun: Pollution has a serious effect on our health. Learning word families (verb, noun, adjective) helps you paraphrase in Writing and is rewarded under Lexical Resource.

cue.card: Describe a time when the weather changed your plans.
points: and explain how you felt about it
model: I’d like to talk about a weekend last October, when a storm completely changed my plans.
My friends and I had planned a camping trip to a lake about two hours from Hanoi. We had booked a campsite, bought food and borrowed tents. The forecast earlier in the week said it would be sunny.

However, on Friday evening the forecast suddenly changed. A tropical storm was moving towards the coast, and heavy rain was expected across the north. By Saturday morning it was pouring, and the wind was so strong that some trees in my street fell down. Parts of the road to the lake were flooded, so we had no choice but to cancel.

At first I felt really disappointed, because we had been looking forward to it for weeks. But in the end we had a great time anyway. We moved the “camping trip” to my apartment, cooked the barbecue food in the kitchen and watched films all evening. Looking back, I’m glad we stayed home, because the storm caused a lot of damage that weekend.

write.prompt: The table below shows the amount of household waste recycled in four countries in 2012 and 2022 (as a percentage of all household waste). Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
write.data:
Country     2012    2022
Country A   45%     62%
Country B   30%     35%
Country C   12%     28%
Country D   20%     18%
plan: Introduction: paraphrase (proportion of household waste recycled, four countries, two years)
Overview: three countries improved; A highest; D the only fall
Body 1: A and B
Body 2: C and D, with comparisons
model: The table shows what proportion of household waste was recycled in four countries in 2012 and 2022.
Overall, recycling rates rose in three of the four countries, and Country A recycled the largest share of its waste in both years. Country D was the only country where the rate fell.

In 2012, Country A already recycled 45% of its household waste, and this figure increased to 62% ten years later, meaning that almost two thirds of its waste was recycled. Country B started at 30%, but it improved only slightly, reaching 35% in 2022.

The most dramatic change was in Country C, where the recycling rate more than doubled, from just 12% to 28%. As a result, it moved from last place to third. Country D, by contrast, recycled 20% of its waste in 2012, but this dropped slightly to 18% in 2022, so by the end of the period it had the lowest rate of the four countries.

gram.title: Relative clauses: who, which, that, where
gram.rule: person + who / that · thing + which / that · place + where · whose (possession)
gram.note: Relative clauses add information about a noun: a film which won many awards, the actor who plays the doctor. In defining clauses you can use that for both people and things. where refers to places: the cinema where we met. These clauses help you build longer, more complex sentences for Grammatical Range.

cue.card: Describe a film you enjoyed watching.
points: when and where you watched it
and explain why you enjoyed it
model: I’d like to talk about a documentary called “My Octopus Teacher”, which I watched on a streaming service about two years ago.

I watched it at home on a rainy Sunday afternoon with my younger sister. Neither of us expected much, because it was recommended by an algorithm, not by a friend, but it turned out to be one of the most memorable films I’ve seen.

It’s about a man in South Africa who was going through a difficult time in his life. He started diving every day in a kelp forest near his home, and he slowly built a relationship with a wild octopus. The film follows the octopus for about a year, showing how it hunts, hides from sharks and finally grows old.

I enjoyed it for two reasons. First, the photography was breathtaking. I had never realised how intelligent octopuses are. Second, the story was inspiring. It showed how spending time in nature helped the man recover from stress. After watching it, I started going for walks in the park more often, so I guess it had a real effect on me.

write.prompt: Many people now get their news from social media rather than from newspapers or television. Is this a positive or negative development?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase; position — mainly negative
Body 1: positives — speed, free, different voices (concede)
Body 2: negatives — fake news, headlines only, filter bubbles (main argument)
Conclusion: restate and suggest media literacy
model: Nowadays, a growing number of people read the news on social media instead of in newspapers or on television. Although this development has some benefits, I believe it is mainly negative.

It is true that social media has made news faster and more accessible. Important stories can reach millions of people within minutes, and most of this information is free. In addition, social media allows ordinary people to share what is happening around them, so we can hear voices that traditional media may ignore. For example, during floods, local residents often post useful updates before journalists arrive.

However, the disadvantages are more serious. The biggest problem is fake news. On social media, anyone can publish a story, and false information often spreads faster than the truth because it is more shocking. Secondly, many users only read headlines or watch short videos, so they get a very simple picture of complicated issues. Finally, social media platforms show people content that matches what they already like, which means users rarely see different opinions. Over time, this can make society more divided.

In conclusion, although getting news from social media is fast and convenient, I believe it is a negative trend overall because it encourages misinformation and shallow understanding. Schools should therefore teach young people how to check sources and think critically about what they read online.

lines.t: Do you know your neighbours well?

lines.t: Not very well, to be honest. I live in an apartment block, and most people keep to themselves. We usually just say hello in the lift.
lines.vi: Thật lòng thì không rõ lắm. Tôi sống ở chung cư, hầu hết mọi người sống khép kín. Chúng tôi thường chỉ chào nhau trong thang máy.

lines.t: Yes, I do. If you have an emergency, your neighbours are the closest people who can help you, even before your family.
lines.vi: Có. Nếu có chuyện khẩn cấp, hàng xóm là người gần nhất có thể giúp bạn, thậm chí trước cả gia đình.

lines.t: In my hometown, they help a lot. For example, they look after each other’s children and share food during Tết.
lines.vi: Ở quê tôi, họ giúp nhau nhiều lắm. Ví dụ họ trông con giúp nhau và chia sẻ đồ ăn dịp Tết.

sents.t: In many big cities, people live close together but do not know their neighbours.
sents.vi: Ở nhiều thành phố lớn, người ta sống gần nhau nhưng không biết hàng xóm.

sents.t: To change this, some apartment blocks now organise small events, such as shared dinners or clean-up days.
sents.vi: Để thay đổi điều này, một số toà chung cư giờ tổ chức các sự kiện nhỏ như bữa tối chung hay ngày dọn dẹp.

sents.vi: Cư dân tham gia những sự kiện này nói họ thấy an toàn hơn và bớt cô đơn.

lines.vi: Còn tuỳ. Ở làng ai cũng biết nhau và giúp nhau, nhưng ít việc làm. Ở thành phố cuộc sống tiện hơn nhưng có thể cô đơn.

lines.t: How can people build a stronger community?
lines.vi: Làm sao để xây dựng cộng đồng gắn bó hơn?

lines.t: Small things can help, like local festivals, sports clubs or a residents’ group online. When people meet regularly, they start to trust each other.
lines.vi: Những điều nhỏ có thể giúp, như lễ hội địa phương, câu lạc bộ thể thao hay nhóm cư dân online. Khi gặp nhau thường xuyên, mọi người bắt đầu tin nhau.

gram2.title: Comparing past and present: used to vs these days
gram2.rule: used to + verb (past habit) · these days / nowadays + present simple
gram2.note: To compare past and present, use used to for the past and these days or nowadays with the present simple: People used to sit outside in the evening. These days they stay inside and watch TV. This is useful in Part 3 answers.

ex.t: People used to know everyone on their street.
ex.vi: Trước đây người ta biết hết mọi người trong phố.

ex.t: These days, many people live in apartment blocks.
ex.vi: Ngày nay nhiều người sống ở chung cư.

ex.t: Children used to play outside together.
ex.vi: Trẻ con từng chơi cùng nhau ngoài trời.

ex.t: Nowadays they usually play on their phones.
ex.vi: Ngày nay chúng thường chơi điện thoại.

drill.t: ___, people are much busier.
drill.vi: Ngày nay mọi người bận hơn nhiều.

drill.t: Did you ___ to live in a village?
drill.vi: Bạn từng sống ở làng à?

drill.vi: Ngày nay hàng xóm tôi sống khép kín.

cue.card: Describe a neighbour you know well.
points: how long you have known them
and explain how you feel about this neighbour
model: I’d like to talk about Mrs Hoa, who lives next door to my parents’ house in my hometown.
I’ve known her for more than twenty years, since I was a small child. She used to give me sweets when I came back from school, and she still calls me “little Nam”, even though I’m almost thirty now.

She’s a very warm and helpful person. She’s retired, so she spends most of her day in her small garden, and she always notices what is happening on the street. Some people might say she’s a bit nosy, but in fact she looks out for everyone. When my father was ill last year, she cooked soup for him every day.
I feel very grateful to her. I live in Hanoi now and I can’t visit my parents often, so it’s a big comfort to know that someone kind is next door. For me, she is almost part of the family.

write.prompt: In many cities, people do not know their neighbours. Why is this happening? What can be done to build stronger communities?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase the problem and preview two reasons and two solutions
Body 1: reasons — busy lifestyles, apartment living, technology
Body 2: solutions — local events, shared spaces, online groups
Conclusion: summarise and give a short opinion
model: In many modern cities, it is common for people to live next to someone for years without knowing their name. This essay will explain why this happens and suggest some ways to bring neighbours closer together.

There are two main reasons for this situation. Firstly, people in cities are very busy. They often work long hours and spend their free time with friends or online, so they have little time to talk to the people around them. Secondly, many people now live in large apartment blocks, where residents move in and out frequently. In this situation, it is difficult to build relationships, and many people prefer to keep to themselves.

However, there are several ways to build stronger communities. Local authorities and building managers can organise simple events, such as shared meals, sports days or clean-up days, which give neighbours a reason to meet. In addition, buildings can include shared spaces like gardens and playgrounds, where people naturally start conversations. Finally, online residents’ groups can help neighbours share information and support each other in emergencies.

In conclusion, busy lifestyles and modern housing make it harder for neighbours to know each other, but small events and shared spaces can make a real difference. I believe that a friendly community makes city life safer and less lonely for everyone.

lines.t: Do you like reading?
lines.vi: Bạn có thích đọc sách không?

lines.t: Yes, I do, but I don’t read as much as I used to. These days I mostly read on my phone during my commute.
lines.vi: Có, nhưng tôi không đọc nhiều như trước. Bây giờ tôi chủ yếu đọc trên điện thoại khi đi làm.

lines.t: What kind of books do you read?
lines.vi: Bạn đọc loại sách nào?

lines.t: Mainly fiction, especially detective novels. I like a good plot that keeps me guessing until the end.
lines.vi: Chủ yếu là truyện hư cấu, nhất là tiểu thuyết trinh thám. Tôi thích cốt truyện hay khiến tôi đoán đến tận cuối.

lines.t: Do you prefer paper books or e-books?
lines.vi: Bạn thích sách giấy hay sách điện tử?

lines.t: I prefer paper books because I can concentrate better, and I like the smell of new pages. But e-books are more convenient when I travel.
lines.vi: Tôi thích sách giấy vì tập trung tốt hơn, và tôi thích mùi trang giấy mới. Nhưng sách điện tử tiện hơn khi đi du lịch.

sents.t: Many people believe that young people no longer read books because of smartphones.
sents.vi: Nhiều người tin rằng người trẻ không còn đọc sách vì điện thoại thông minh.

sents.t: However, a recent study found that teenagers read a lot, but mostly on screens.
sents.vi: Tuy nhiên, một nghiên cứu gần đây cho thấy thanh thiếu niên đọc nhiều, nhưng chủ yếu trên màn hình.

sents.t: They read news, comics and online stories every day.

sents.t: Sales of audiobooks have also grown quickly in the last five years.

q.q: The study found that teenagers do not read at all.
Audiobook sales have increased in recent years.
Most teachers prefer e-books to paper books.

gram.title: Comparatives for preferences
gram.rule: I prefer A to B · A is more convenient than B · A isn’t as … as B
gram.note: In Part 1, you often compare two things. Use prefer A to B, or a comparative with than: E-books are lighter than paper books. Use not as … as for a softer comparison: Audiobooks aren’t as relaxing as real books for me.

ex.t: I prefer novels to short stories.
ex.vi: Tôi thích tiểu thuyết hơn truyện ngắn.

ex.t: E-books are cheaper than paperbacks.

ex.vi: Sách nói không thư giãn bằng sách giấy.

lines.t: Why is reading important for children?
lines.vi: Vì sao đọc sách quan trọng với trẻ em?

lines.t: It helps them develop their imagination and vocabulary. Also, children who read a lot usually do better at school, because they can understand texts more easily.
lines.vi: Nó giúp trẻ phát triển trí tưởng tượng và vốn từ. Hơn nữa, trẻ đọc nhiều thường học tốt hơn vì hiểu văn bản dễ hơn.

lines.t: Will paper books disappear in the future?
lines.vi: Sách giấy có biến mất trong tương lai không?

lines.t: I don’t think so. E-books are popular, but many people still enjoy holding a real book, and they are nice gifts. Maybe there will be fewer paper books, but they won’t disappear completely.
lines.vi: Tôi không nghĩ vậy. Sách điện tử phổ biến, nhưng nhiều người vẫn thích cầm sách thật, và sách là món quà đẹp. Có thể sách giấy sẽ ít đi nhưng không biến mất hoàn toàn.

lines.t: How can parents encourage children to read?
lines.vi: Cha mẹ có thể khuyến khích con đọc sách thế nào?

lines.t: The best way is to read with them, for example a bedtime story every night. Children copy their parents, so if parents read instead of looking at their phones, children will too.
lines.vi: Cách tốt nhất là đọc cùng con, ví dụ một câu chuyện trước giờ ngủ mỗi tối. Trẻ bắt chước cha mẹ, nên nếu cha mẹ đọc thay vì xem điện thoại thì con cũng vậy.

gram2.title: Giving examples: for example, such as, like
gram2.rule: for example + full sentence · such as / like + noun
gram2.note: Examples make your answers longer and clearer. Use for example or for instance before a clause: For example, I read on the bus. Use such as or like before nouns: books such as novels and biographies.

ex.t: I enjoy many types of books, such as novels and biographies.
ex.vi: Tôi thích nhiều loại sách như tiểu thuyết và tiểu sử.

ex.t: Reading has many benefits. For example, it improves your vocabulary.
ex.vi: Đọc sách có nhiều lợi ích. Ví dụ, nó cải thiện vốn từ.

ex.vi: Những ứng dụng như Kindle giúp đọc sách dễ dàng.

cue.card: Describe a book you enjoyed reading.
points: and explain why you enjoyed it
model: I’d like to talk about a novel called “The Little Prince”, which is a famous French book. I read the Vietnamese translation when I was about fifteen.
I came across it by chance in my school library. It looked like a children’s book because it was short and had simple drawings, so I thought it would be easy to read.

The story is about a pilot whose plane crashes in the desert, where he meets a little prince from another planet. The prince tells him about his travels and the strange adults he has met. On the surface it is a simple story, but it has many deep messages about friendship, love and what is really important in life.

I enjoyed it because it made me think. Every time I read it again, I understand something new. My favourite line says that the most important things are invisible to the eyes, and I still remember that today. I often recommend it to friends because it’s short but very meaningful.

write.prompt: Some people think that children should read paper books, while others believe that e-books and online reading are better for them. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
plan: Introduction: paraphrase both views and give your opinion (a mix, but paper first for young children)
Body 1: benefits of paper books — concentration, eyes, less distraction
Body 2: benefits of e-books — cheap, many choices, interactive
Conclusion: balanced opinion
model: Nowadays, children can read both traditional paper books and digital texts on tablets and phones. Some people believe paper books are better, while others prefer e-books and online reading. In my opinion, both have advantages, but young children should start with paper books.

On the one hand, paper books help children concentrate. When a child reads a printed book, there are no notifications, games or videos to distract them. In addition, reading on paper is easier on the eyes, which is important because many children already spend hours looking at screens. Paper books also give families a special time together, for example when parents read bedtime stories.

On the other hand, e-books and online reading have clear benefits. They are often cheaper, and children can access thousands of books instantly, even if there is no library nearby. Some digital books are interactive, with sounds and pictures that can help children who find reading difficult. Moreover, children need digital skills for their future studies and jobs.

In conclusion, although e-books are convenient and useful, I believe paper books should come first for young children because they build concentration and a love of reading. As children grow older, they can gradually add digital reading to their habits.

units.title: Clothes & fashion

lines.t: What kind of clothes do you like to wear?
lines.vi: Bạn thích mặc loại quần áo nào?

lines.t: Do you follow fashion trends?
lines.vi: Bạn có theo xu hướng thời trang không?

lines.t: Not really. Trends change too quickly, and I don’t want to buy new clothes every month. I just choose things that suit me.
lines.vi: Không hẳn. Xu hướng thay đổi quá nhanh, và tôi không muốn mua quần áo mới mỗi tháng. Tôi chỉ chọn đồ hợp với mình.

lines.t: Do you wear traditional clothes?
lines.vi: Bạn có mặc trang phục truyền thống không?

lines.t: Sometimes. My wife wears an ao dai at Tết and at weddings, and I have one too, but I only wear it on very special occasions.
lines.vi: Thỉnh thoảng. Vợ tôi mặc áo dài dịp Tết và đám cưới, tôi cũng có một chiếc nhưng chỉ mặc vào dịp rất đặc biệt.

read.title: The real cost of cheap clothes

sents.t: Clothes are much cheaper today than they were thirty years ago.
sents.vi: Quần áo ngày nay rẻ hơn nhiều so với ba mươi năm trước.

sents.t: This is partly because of fast fashion: shops produce new designs every few weeks.
sents.vi: Một phần là do thời trang nhanh: các cửa hàng ra mẫu mới vài tuần một lần.

sents.t: On average, people now buy far more clothes but wear each item fewer times.
sents.vi: Trung bình người ta giờ mua nhiều quần áo hơn nhưng mỗi món mặc ít lần hơn.

sents.t: Making clothes uses a lot of water and energy, and many old clothes end up in landfill.
sents.vi: Sản xuất quần áo tốn nhiều nước và năng lượng, và nhiều quần áo cũ bị chôn lấp.

q.q: People wear each item of clothing more times than in the past.
Producing clothes requires a lot of water.
Second-hand clothes are more popular than new ones.

gram.title: It depends on… for flexible answers

gram.note: When the answer is “sometimes yes, sometimes no”, start with It depends and explain the conditions. This makes your answer natural and longer: It depends on the weather. If it’s hot, I wear shorts; if it’s cold, I wear a jacket.

ex.t: It depends. If it’s a wedding, I dress up.

lines.t: Why do some people spend a lot of money on clothes?
lines.vi: Vì sao một số người chi nhiều tiền cho quần áo?

lines.t: I think clothes are part of their image. Some people want to look successful, so they buy famous brands. Others just enjoy fashion as a hobby.
lines.vi: Tôi nghĩ quần áo là một phần hình ảnh của họ. Có người muốn trông thành đạt nên mua đồ hiệu. Người khác chỉ đơn giản thích thời trang như một sở thích.

lines.t: Should students wear uniforms?

lines.t: Yes, I think so. Uniforms are cheaper for parents, and children don’t compete with each other about clothes. It also gives a sense of belonging to the school.
lines.vi: Có, tôi nghĩ vậy. Đồng phục rẻ hơn cho phụ huynh, và trẻ không đua nhau về quần áo. Nó cũng tạo cảm giác gắn bó với trường.

lines.t: Is fast fashion a problem?
lines.vi: Thời trang nhanh có phải là vấn đề không?

lines.t: Yes, because it creates a lot of waste. People buy cheap clothes, wear them a few times and throw them away. I think we should buy fewer clothes of better quality.
lines.vi: Có, vì nó tạo ra nhiều rác. Người ta mua đồ rẻ, mặc vài lần rồi vứt. Tôi nghĩ nên mua ít đồ hơn nhưng chất lượng tốt hơn.

gram2.title: Should / shouldn’t for opinions
gram2.rule: I think people should + verb · I don’t think … should + verb · We should + verb instead of + -ing
gram2.note: Should is the simplest way to give an opinion about what is right. Notice that we usually say I don’t think people should (not I think people shouldn’t). Use instead of + -ing to suggest an alternative.

ex.t: I think students should wear uniforms.
ex.vi: Tôi nghĩ học sinh nên mặc đồng phục.

ex.t: I don’t think people should buy so many clothes.
ex.vi: Tôi không nghĩ người ta nên mua quá nhiều quần áo.

ex.t: We should repair clothes instead of throwing them away.
ex.vi: Chúng ta nên sửa quần áo thay vì vứt đi.

ex.t: Shops should use recycled materials.
ex.vi: Các cửa hàng nên dùng vật liệu tái chế.

drill.vi: Trẻ em nên đi giày thoải mái.

drill.vi: Tôi nghĩ cửa hàng nên tái chế quần áo cũ.

cue.card: Describe a piece of clothing that is special to you.
points: and explain why it is special to you
model: I’d like to talk about a dark blue ao dai that my mother had made for me when I graduated from university.

She took me to an old tailor in Hue, the same tailor who made her wedding ao dai thirty years ago. The tailor measured me carefully, and two weeks later it was ready. It fitted me perfectly, which is not common with ready-made clothes.

I don’t wear it very often — maybe three or four times a year, for example on the first day of Tết, at family weddings and once for an important ceremony at work. I keep it in a special bag in my wardrobe so it stays in good condition.

It’s special to me for two reasons. Firstly, it reminds me of my graduation day, which was one of the proudest days for my parents. Secondly, it connects me with my mother and my hometown. Whenever I wear it, I feel elegant and confident, and I also feel that I’m carrying a little bit of my family history with me.

write.prompt: Fast fashion makes clothes cheap, but it is bad for the environment. Do the advantages of fast fashion outweigh the disadvantages?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase and give a clear position (disadvantages outweigh)
Body 1: advantages — cheap, choice, jobs
Body 2: disadvantages — waste, pollution, poor quality and working conditions
Conclusion: position + suggestion
model: In recent years, fast fashion has made it possible for almost everyone to buy fashionable clothes at very low prices. While this has some clear benefits, I believe that the disadvantages, especially for the environment, are greater.

There are several advantages of fast fashion. Firstly, it allows people with low incomes to buy new clothes and follow trends, which was impossible for many in the past. Secondly, shoppers have a huge choice of styles and sizes. In addition, the industry creates millions of jobs, particularly in developing countries such as Vietnam and Bangladesh.

However, these benefits come at a high cost. Producing clothes requires enormous amounts of water and energy, and the chemicals used in dyeing often pollute rivers. Because fast fashion items are cheap and low in quality, people wear them only a few times before throwing them away, so huge amounts of textiles end up in landfill. Furthermore, factory workers are sometimes paid very little and work in unsafe conditions.

In conclusion, although fast fashion makes clothes affordable and provides jobs, its damage to the environment and to workers outweighs these advantages. I believe consumers should buy fewer, better-quality clothes, and governments should encourage recycling and second-hand shopping.

lines.t: Do you have a pet?
lines.vi: Bạn có nuôi thú cưng không?

lines.t: Yes, I have a cat called Miu. I adopted her from a shelter two years ago. She’s very independent, so she doesn’t need much attention.
lines.vi: Có, tôi có một con mèo tên Miu. Tôi nhận nuôi nó từ trạm cứu hộ hai năm trước. Nó rất độc lập nên không cần nhiều sự chú ý.

lines.t: Did you have pets when you were a child?
lines.vi: Hồi nhỏ bạn có nuôi thú cưng không?

lines.t: Yes, we kept a dog in the countryside. He was very loyal and followed me everywhere, even to school.
lines.vi: Có, nhà tôi ở quê nuôi một con chó. Nó rất trung thành và theo tôi khắp nơi, cả đến trường.

lines.t: What is the most popular pet in your country?
lines.vi: Thú cưng phổ biến nhất ở nước bạn là gì?

lines.t: Probably dogs, especially in the countryside, where they also guard the house. But in cities, cats are becoming more popular because flats are small.
lines.vi: Có lẽ là chó, nhất là ở nông thôn, nơi chó còn trông nhà. Nhưng ở thành phố, mèo ngày càng được ưa chuộng vì căn hộ nhỏ.

sents.t: Studies show that owning a pet can be good for our health.
sents.vi: Các nghiên cứu cho thấy nuôi thú cưng có thể tốt cho sức khoẻ.

gram.title: have to / don’t have to / must for responsibilities
gram.rule: have to + verb (necessary) · don’t have to (not necessary) · mustn’t (not allowed)
gram.note: Use have to for things that are necessary: You have to feed a pet every day. Don’t have to means it is not necessary: Cats don’t have to go for walks. Mustn’t means it is not allowed or a very bad idea: You mustn’t leave a dog in a hot car.

ex.t: Dog owners have to walk their dogs every day.
ex.vi: Người nuôi chó phải dắt chó đi dạo hằng ngày.

ex.t: You don’t have to bathe a cat very often.
ex.vi: Bạn không cần tắm cho mèo thường xuyên.

ex.t: You mustn’t give chocolate to dogs.

lines.t: Why do people keep pets?
lines.vi: Vì sao người ta nuôi thú cưng?

lines.t: Mainly for company. Pets make people feel less lonely, and they can reduce stress. Some people, especially in the countryside, also keep dogs to guard the house.
lines.vi: Chủ yếu để có bạn. Thú cưng khiến người ta bớt cô đơn và giảm căng thẳng. Một số người, nhất là ở nông thôn, còn nuôi chó để trông nhà.

lines.t: Should children have pets?
lines.vi: Trẻ em có nên nuôi thú cưng không?

lines.t: Yes, if the parents help. Looking after a pet teaches children responsibility. But parents have to remember that the pet needs care for many years, not just for a few weeks.
lines.vi: Có, nếu bố mẹ giúp. Chăm thú cưng dạy trẻ tinh thần trách nhiệm. Nhưng bố mẹ phải nhớ thú cưng cần được chăm nhiều năm chứ không chỉ vài tuần.

lines.t: Are zoos a good idea?
lines.vi: Sở thú có phải là ý hay không?

lines.t: It depends. Good zoos protect endangered animals and teach children about nature. But in bad zoos the animals live in small cages, which is cruel.
lines.vi: Còn tuỳ. Sở thú tốt bảo vệ động vật có nguy cơ tuyệt chủng và dạy trẻ về thiên nhiên. Nhưng ở sở thú kém, động vật sống trong lồng nhỏ, điều đó thật tàn nhẫn.

gram2.title: Linking ideas: and, but, also, however
gram2.rule: and / also (adding) · but / however (contrast) · Also, … · However, …
gram2.note: Simple linking words make your speaking more organised. And and but join two clauses. Also adds another point and often comes before the main verb or at the start: Pets also reduce stress. However starts a new sentence and is followed by a comma.

ex.t: Dogs are loyal, and they protect the house.
ex.vi: Chó trung thành và chúng bảo vệ nhà.

ex.t: Cats are cute, but they can scratch furniture.
ex.vi: Mèo dễ thương nhưng có thể cào đồ đạc.

cue.card: Describe an animal you like.
points: and explain why you like it
model: I’d like to talk about elephants, which have been my favourite animal since I was a child.

In Vietnam, you can still see elephants in Dak Lak province, in the Central Highlands. I went there with my family a few years ago and visited a national park, where some elephants live in a protected area. Of course, you can also see them in zoos, but it’s much better to see them in a natural environment.

Elephants are huge, grey animals with long trunks and big ears. What surprised me most was how gently they moved, even though they are so heavy. They use their trunks like hands — to pick up food, to drink water and even to touch each other.

I like elephants because they are intelligent and very family-oriented. They live in groups, look after their babies together and seem to remember friends for many years. Sadly, they are an endangered species in Vietnam now, so I support organisations that protect them, and I hope my children will still be able to see them in the wild.

write.prompt: Some people think that keeping pets in cities is unfair to the animals. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase and give a clear partial-disagree position
Body 1: why it can be unfair — small spaces, noise, long hours alone
Body 2: why it can be fine — suitable pets, responsible owners, parks
Conclusion: depends on the owner and the type of pet
model: In many cities, more and more people are keeping dogs and cats in small flats. Some believe that this is unfair to the animals. I partly agree, but I think the problem depends more on the owner and the type of pet than on the city itself.

It is true that city life can be difficult for some animals. Large dogs, for example, need a lot of space and exercise, and a small apartment cannot give them the freedom they need. City streets are also noisy and crowded, which can make animals anxious. Moreover, many owners work long hours, so their pets spend most of the day alone, which can cause stress and bad behaviour.

However, pets can live happy lives in cities if their owners are responsible. Small dogs, cats and fish are well suited to flats, and many cities now have parks where dogs can run safely. An owner who walks their dog twice a day, plays with it and takes it to the vet regularly can give it a better life than an animal left alone in a big garden in the countryside. In addition, adopting animals from shelters gives stray animals a home they would not otherwise have.

In conclusion, keeping pets in cities is not unfair in itself. What matters is choosing a pet that suits city life and taking proper care of it. People who cannot give an animal enough time and attention should not keep one, wherever they live.

units.title: Childhood memories
units.goal: Describe childhood memories using the past simple, “used to” and “would” for repeated past actions.

lines.t: Where did you grow up?
lines.vi: Bạn lớn lên ở đâu?

lines.t: I grew up in a small village in Nam Dinh province. My family had a rice field and a few chickens, so my childhood was very simple but happy.
lines.vi: Tôi lớn lên ở một ngôi làng nhỏ ở Nam Định. Nhà tôi có ruộng lúa và vài con gà, nên tuổi thơ tôi rất giản dị nhưng hạnh phúc.

lines.t: What did you like doing as a child?
lines.vi: Hồi nhỏ bạn thích làm gì?

lines.t: I loved flying kites. In summer, my friends and I would make kites from paper and bamboo and fly them in the rice fields after school.

lines.t: Were you a naughty child?
lines.vi: Bạn có phải là đứa trẻ nghịch ngợm không?

lines.t: A little! I used to climb trees in my neighbour’s garden to pick fruit. My mother was quite strict, so I got into trouble a few times.
lines.vi: Một chút! Tôi hay trèo cây trong vườn nhà hàng xóm để hái quả. Mẹ tôi khá nghiêm nên tôi bị mắng vài lần.

sents.t: Thirty years ago, most children played outdoors with friends after school.
sents.vi: Ba mươi năm trước, hầu hết trẻ em chơi ngoài trời với bạn sau giờ học.

sents.t: Today, many children spend their free time indoors with tablets and phones.
sents.vi: Ngày nay nhiều trẻ dành thời gian rảnh trong nhà với máy tính bảng và điện thoại.

sents.t: Parents also worry more about traffic and safety, so they let children go out alone less often.
sents.vi: Cha mẹ cũng lo hơn về giao thông và an toàn nên ít cho con ra ngoài một mình.

sents.t: Some experts say that outdoor play helps children become more confident and creative.
sents.vi: Một số chuyên gia nói chơi ngoài trời giúp trẻ tự tin và sáng tạo hơn.

sents.t: Many schools now organise outdoor activities to encourage children to play in nature.
sents.vi: Nhiều trường giờ tổ chức hoạt động ngoài trời để khuyến khích trẻ chơi giữa thiên nhiên.

q.q: Children today play outdoors more than in the past.
Parents worry about traffic and safety.
All schools have a garden.

gram.title: used to and would for past habits
gram.rule: used to + verb (habits and states) · would + verb (repeated actions only)
gram.note: Use used to for past habits and states: I used to be shy. Would can describe repeated past actions, especially in stories, but not states: Every summer we would fly kites. You can’t say “I would be shy”.

ex.t: I used to live with my grandparents.
ex.vi: Tôi từng sống với ông bà.

ex.t: Every evening we would play hide-and-seek.

ex.t: I used to be scared of the dark.
ex.vi: Tôi từng sợ bóng tối.

ex.t: My grandfather would tell us stories.

drill.t: I ___ be very shy at school.

lines.t: Is childhood today better or worse than in the past?
lines.vi: Tuổi thơ ngày nay tốt hơn hay tệ hơn trước?

lines.t: In some ways it’s better — children have better food, healthcare and education. But in other ways it’s worse, because they spend too much time on screens and have more pressure from school.
lines.vi: Ở mặt nào đó thì tốt hơn — trẻ ăn uống, y tế và giáo dục tốt hơn. Nhưng mặt khác thì tệ hơn vì chúng dành quá nhiều thời gian cho màn hình và chịu áp lực học hành nhiều hơn.

lines.t: Why do adults often feel nostalgic about their childhood?
lines.vi: Vì sao người lớn hay hoài niệm tuổi thơ?

lines.t: Because childhood was a carefree time. Adults have to worry about work, money and family, so they remember a time when life was simpler.
lines.vi: Vì tuổi thơ là quãng thời gian vô tư. Người lớn phải lo công việc, tiền bạc và gia đình nên họ nhớ về thời cuộc sống đơn giản hơn.

lines.t: What can parents do to give children a happy childhood?
lines.vi: Cha mẹ có thể làm gì để con có tuổi thơ hạnh phúc?

lines.t: I think the most important thing is time. Parents should play with their children, take them outdoors and listen to them, instead of only buying expensive toys.

cue.card: Describe a happy memory from your childhood.
points: and explain why it is a happy memory
model: I’d like to talk about the first time my family went to the beach, when I was about eight years old.

At that time, we lived in a village in the north, and my parents worked very hard on the farm, so we almost never travelled. One summer, after a good harvest, my father announced that we were going to Sam Son beach for three days. I was so excited that I couldn’t sleep the night before.

I went with my parents, my younger sister and my grandmother. We took an old bus that was hot and crowded, but nobody complained. When we arrived, I ran straight into the sea with my clothes on, and my mother laughed so much. We spent the days swimming, building sandcastles and eating fresh seafood, which was a real luxury for us.

It’s a happy memory because it was the first time I saw my parents completely relaxed. They didn’t have to think about work, and we were all together. Whenever I smell the sea now, it reminds me of that trip, and I feel very nostalgic. I hope to give my own children memories like that.

write.prompt: Some people believe that children today have a better childhood than children in the past. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase and give a balanced but clear position (partly agree)
Body 1: better — health, education, opportunities
Body 2: worse — screens, pressure, less outdoor freedom
Conclusion: better in material terms, but parents must protect play and freedom
model: It is often said that children today enjoy a better childhood than previous generations. I partly agree with this view, because modern children have many advantages, but they also face new problems that children in the past did not.

On the one hand, children today are generally healthier and better educated. They have better food, vaccines and medical care, so fewer children suffer from serious illnesses. Most children can go to school for many years, and they have access to books, technology and information from all over the world. In addition, many families have more money, so children can enjoy holidays, hobbies and activities that were impossible for most children in the past.

On the other hand, modern childhood has some disadvantages. Many children spend hours every day looking at screens instead of playing outdoors with friends, which can affect their health and social skills. Furthermore, the pressure to do well at school has increased, and some children attend extra classes in the evenings and at weekends, leaving them little free time. Parents also worry more about safety, so children have less freedom to explore their neighbourhood.

In conclusion, although children today have better health and more opportunities, I do not think their childhood is better in every way. Parents and schools should make sure that children still have enough time to play, rest and enjoy being young.

lines.t: Do you like giving gifts?

lines.vi: Có. Tôi thích chọn món hợp với người nhận, và rất thích nhìn nét mặt họ khi mở quà.

lines.t: What gifts do people give in your country?

lines.t: It depends on the occasion. At Tết we give lucky money in red envelopes, and at weddings guests usually give cash too. For birthdays, people give clothes, flowers or cakes.
lines.vi: Còn tuỳ dịp. Tết chúng tôi lì xì trong phong bao đỏ, đám cưới khách cũng thường mừng tiền. Sinh nhật thì người ta tặng quần áo, hoa hay bánh.

sents.t: Experiences, such as a concert ticket or a meal together, are often remembered longer than objects.

lines.t: Is it better to give money or a gift?

cue.card: Describe a gift you gave to someone.
points: and explain how the person felt about it
model: I’d like to talk about a photo album I made for my grandparents’ fiftieth wedding anniversary last year.

My grandparents live in Hai Phong, and the whole family planned a big celebration for them. Everyone was thinking about what to buy, but my grandparents already have everything they need, and they hate it when we spend money on them.

So I decided to make something by hand. I spent about a month collecting old photos from my aunts and uncles — some were over fifty years old, from their wedding day. I scanned them, printed them and put them in a large album in order, from their wedding to the birth of their great-grandchildren. Under each photo, I wrote a short note about the memory.

When I gave it to them at the party, my grandmother started crying, and my grandfather, who is usually very quiet, spent the whole evening turning the pages and telling stories. They said it was the best gift they had ever received. It didn’t cost much money, but it had huge sentimental value, and it reminded me that it really is the thought that counts.

write.prompt: In many countries, people spend more and more money on gifts for festivals and celebrations. Why is this happening? Is it a positive or negative development?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase; reasons + mainly negative view
Body 1: reasons — higher incomes, advertising, social media comparison
Body 2: evaluation — supports economy but creates pressure, debt, waste
Conclusion: negative overall; value thoughtfulness over price
model: In recent years, the amount of money people spend on gifts for festivals such as Tết, Christmas and birthdays has increased significantly. This essay will discuss the reasons for this trend and explain why I believe it is mostly a negative development.

There are several reasons for this change. Firstly, incomes have risen in many countries, so people can afford more expensive presents. Secondly, advertising and online shopping promotions encourage people to buy more, especially before big festivals, by suggesting that a valuable gift shows more love or respect. Finally, social media plays a role, as people often share photos of the gifts they give and receive, which creates pressure to compete with others.

Although spending on gifts can benefit the economy and support small businesses, I believe the negative effects are greater. Many families feel pressure to spend money they do not have, and some even borrow money to buy gifts for festivals. In addition, expensive gifts can change the meaning of celebrations, making them about money rather than relationships. A lot of unwanted gifts are also thrown away or never used, which is wasteful and harmful to the environment.

In conclusion, people are spending more on gifts because of higher incomes, advertising and social pressure. In my view, this is generally a negative trend, and we should remember that the most meaningful gifts are often simple ones that show care and thought rather than a high price.
