lines.t: Should university education be free?
lines.vi: Giáo dục đại học có nên miễn phí không?

lines.t: I think it should be free, or at least much cheaper, for students from poor families. Otherwise talented young people drop out simply because they can’t afford tuition fees, and the whole country loses their skills.
lines.vi: Tôi nghĩ nên miễn phí, hoặc ít nhất rẻ hơn nhiều, cho sinh viên nhà nghèo. Nếu không, người trẻ có năng lực bỏ học chỉ vì không đủ tiền học phí, và cả đất nước mất đi kỹ năng của họ.

lines.t: Is rote learning still useful?
lines.vi: Học thuộc lòng có còn hữu ích không?

lines.t: To some extent. You need to memorise basic facts, like times tables or vocabulary. But if schools rely only on rote learning, students can repeat information without really understanding it.
lines.vi: Ở mức độ nào đó. Bạn cần nhớ những kiến thức cơ bản như bảng cửu chương hay từ vựng. Nhưng nếu trường chỉ dựa vào học thuộc, học sinh có thể nhắc lại thông tin mà không thật sự hiểu.

lines.t: How will education change in the future?
lines.vi: Giáo dục sẽ thay đổi thế nào trong tương lai?

lines.t: I expect more distance learning and personalised courses. Teachers will probably act more like coaches, guiding students rather than just giving lectures.
lines.vi: Tôi nghĩ sẽ có nhiều học từ xa và khoá học cá nhân hoá hơn. Giáo viên có lẽ sẽ giống huấn luyện viên hơn, định hướng học sinh thay vì chỉ giảng bài.

gram2.title: Discussing both sides
gram2.rule: On the one hand … On the other hand … · Some people argue that … whereas others believe … · While it is true that …, …
gram2.note: In a discussion essay, present each view fairly before giving your own. Use whereas or while to contrast two ideas in one sentence. Start your opinion clearly: In my view, … / I would argue that … Avoid writing only “some people think” without saying what you think.

ex.t: On the one hand, exams motivate students to study.
ex.vi: Một mặt, thi cử thúc đẩy học sinh học tập.

ex.t: Some argue that fees should be abolished, whereas others disagree.
ex.vi: Một số người cho rằng nên bỏ học phí, trong khi người khác không đồng ý.

ex.t: While it is true that online courses are flexible, they can feel lonely.
ex.vi: Dù đúng là khoá học trực tuyến linh hoạt, chúng có thể gây cảm giác cô đơn.

ex.t: In my view, both approaches have value.
ex.vi: Theo tôi, cả hai cách đều có giá trị.

drill.t: ___ the one hand, uniforms reduce bullying.
drill.vi: Một mặt, đồng phục giảm bắt nạt.

drill.t: Some prefer lectures, ___ others prefer projects.
drill.vi: Một số người thích nghe giảng, trong khi người khác thích làm dự án.

drill.t: ___ it is true that tests are stressful, they are necessary.
drill.vi: Dù đúng là bài kiểm tra căng thẳng, chúng vẫn cần thiết.

drill.t: ___ my view, practical skills matter most.
drill.vi: Theo tôi, kỹ năng thực hành quan trọng nhất.

cue.card: Describe a teacher who influenced you.
points: and explain how they influenced you
model: I’d like to talk about Mrs Lan, who taught me physics in my last two years of high school. She was in her fifties at the time and had been teaching for almost thirty years, but she still seemed genuinely excited about every lesson.

What made her different was that she hated rote learning. Instead of asking us to memorise formulas, she brought in simple objects — a bicycle wheel, a bottle of water — and made us work out the rules ourselves. She was quite strict about discipline, though. If you didn’t do your homework, she would quietly ask you to stay after class and explain why.

She influenced me in two ways. First, she’s the reason I chose engineering, because she showed me that physics explains things we see every day. Second, she taught me to ask “why” instead of just accepting an answer, and that habit of critical thinking has helped me far more than any single formula.

write.prompt: Some people believe that universities should focus on providing academic knowledge, while others think they should prepare students for employment. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
plan: Introduction: paraphrase both views + your position (both, but employment skills must be included)
Body 1: academic knowledge — deep understanding, research, adapting to future jobs
Body 2: employment — graduate unemployment, practical skills, internships
Conclusion: restate a balanced view in different words
model: There is an ongoing debate about the main role of universities. Some argue that they should concentrate on academic knowledge, whereas others believe their priority should be preparing graduates for work. In my view, a good university should do both, but employability can no longer be treated as an afterthought.

On the one hand, there are strong reasons to protect academic study. A degree in physics or history teaches students to analyse evidence, build arguments and understand complex ideas in depth. These abilities are not linked to one particular job, so they remain valuable even when the labour market changes. In addition, universities are where most research takes place, and research depends on students who have a solid theoretical foundation.

On the other hand, many graduates today struggle to find suitable work. Employers frequently complain that new graduates lack practical skills such as teamwork, communication and the use of industry software. When students pay high tuition fees, it is reasonable for them to expect a course that improves their career prospects. Universities that offer internships and hands-on projects therefore produce graduates who are ready to contribute from their first day.

In conclusion, while academic knowledge remains the core purpose of higher education, I believe universities must also equip students with the skills employers need. The best courses combine theory with real-world practice, so that graduates are both well-educated and employable.

units.title: Health & healthcare
units.goal: Talk about health services and lifestyles, and describe trends in a line graph.

words.ex: Everyone should have access to basic healthcare.
words.exVi: Ai cũng nên được tiếp cận chăm sóc y tế cơ bản.

words.ex: Life expectancy has risen to 75 years.
words.exVi: Tuổi thọ trung bình đã tăng lên 75 tuổi.

words.ex: Prevention is better than cure.
words.exVi: Phòng bệnh hơn chữa bệnh.

words.ex: The treatment lasted three months.
words.exVi: Việc điều trị kéo dài ba tháng.

words.ex: Diabetes is a chronic disease.
words.exVi: Tiểu đường là bệnh mãn tính.

words.ex: Infectious diseases spread quickly in crowded areas.
words.exVi: Bệnh truyền nhiễm lây nhanh ở nơi đông đúc.

words.ex: Most children are vaccinated against measles.
words.exVi: Hầu hết trẻ em được tiêm phòng sởi.

words.ex: The hospital treats 2,000 patients a day.
words.exVi: Bệnh viện điều trị 2.000 bệnh nhân mỗi ngày.

words.ex: Smoking is a serious public health problem.
words.exVi: Hút thuốc là vấn đề y tế cộng đồng nghiêm trọng.

words.ex: I have a medical check-up every year.
words.exVi: Tôi khám sức khoẻ định kỳ mỗi năm.

words.ex: Mental health is as important as physical health.
words.exVi: Sức khoẻ tinh thần quan trọng như sức khoẻ thể chất.

words.ex: An ageing population increases healthcare costs.
words.exVi: Dân số già hoá làm tăng chi phí y tế.

words.ex: Health insurance covers most of the cost.
words.exVi: Bảo hiểm y tế chi trả phần lớn chi phí.

words.ex: This medicine has few side effects.
words.exVi: Thuốc này ít tác dụng phụ.

words.ex: The country faced an epidemic of flu.
words.exVi: Đất nước đối mặt với dịch cúm.

words.ex: She recovered quickly after the operation.
words.exVi: Cô ấy hồi phục nhanh sau ca mổ.

words.ex: A high fever is a common symptom.
words.exVi: Sốt cao là triệu chứng thường gặp.

words.ex: Exercise improves overall well-being.
words.exVi: Tập thể dục cải thiện sức khoẻ tổng thể.

words.ex: The number of cases fluctuated during the year.
words.exVi: Số ca bệnh dao động trong năm.

words.ex: Hospital visits peaked in January.
words.exVi: Số lượt khám đạt đỉnh vào tháng Một.

lines.t: What do you do to stay healthy?
lines.vi: Bạn làm gì để giữ sức khoẻ?

lines.t: I try to walk at least eight thousand steps a day, and I avoid sugary drinks. I also go for a medical check-up once a year, just to be safe.
lines.vi: Tôi cố đi bộ ít nhất tám nghìn bước mỗi ngày và tránh đồ uống có đường. Tôi cũng khám sức khoẻ mỗi năm một lần cho chắc.

lines.t: Do you often go to the doctor?
lines.vi: Bạn có hay đi khám bác sĩ không?

lines.t: Not very often, only when I have symptoms that don’t go away, like a cough that lasts more than a week.
lines.vi: Không thường xuyên lắm, chỉ khi có triệu chứng kéo dài, như ho hơn một tuần.

lines.t: Is it easy to see a doctor where you live?
lines.vi: Ở nơi bạn sống, đi khám bác sĩ có dễ không?

lines.t: In the city, yes, but public hospitals are very crowded. Many people with health insurance still choose private clinics to avoid waiting for hours.
lines.vi: Ở thành phố thì dễ, nhưng bệnh viện công rất đông. Nhiều người có bảo hiểm y tế vẫn chọn phòng khám tư để khỏi chờ hàng giờ.

sents.t: Global life expectancy rose from about 52 years in 1960 to over 72 years in 2020.
sents.vi: Tuổi thọ trung bình toàn cầu tăng từ khoảng 52 tuổi năm 1960 lên hơn 72 tuổi năm 2020.

sents.t: The biggest single factor was the fall in deaths among young children.
sents.vi: Yếu tố lớn nhất là số trẻ nhỏ tử vong giảm.

sents.t: Clean water, vaccination programmes and better nutrition all played a major role.
sents.vi: Nước sạch, chương trình tiêm chủng và dinh dưỡng tốt hơn đều đóng vai trò lớn.

sents.t: Today, however, chronic diseases such as heart disease cause most deaths in richer countries.
sents.vi: Tuy nhiên ngày nay, bệnh mãn tính như bệnh tim gây ra phần lớn ca tử vong ở các nước giàu.

sents.t: For this reason, many governments now spend more on prevention than in the past.
sents.vi: Vì vậy nhiều chính phủ hiện chi cho phòng ngừa nhiều hơn trước.

q.q: Life expectancy has increased by around 20 years since 1960.
Adult deaths fell more than child deaths.
Heart disease is the main cause of death in poorer countries.

gram.title: Describing trends
gram.rule: rise / increase / grow · fall / decrease / decline · fluctuate · peak at · level off · + sharply / gradually / slightly / steadily
gram.note: Use a verb + adverb (rose sharply) or adjective + noun (a sharp rise). Use by for the size of a change (fell by 5%) and to / at for the final figure (rose to 70%, peaked at 90). Choose the past simple for past years and will / is expected to for forecasts.

ex.t: The number of patients rose sharply in 2019.
ex.vi: Số bệnh nhân tăng mạnh vào năm 2019.

ex.t: There was a gradual decline in smoking.
ex.vi: Có sự giảm dần về hút thuốc.

ex.t: Cases peaked at 5,000 in March.
ex.vi: Số ca đạt đỉnh 5.000 vào tháng Ba.

ex.t: Spending is expected to level off after 2030.
ex.vi: Chi tiêu dự kiến chững lại sau năm 2030.

drill.t: Prices rose ___ 10% last year.
drill.vi: Giá tăng 10% năm ngoái.

drill.t: Visits reached a ___ in winter.
drill.vi: Lượt khám đạt đỉnh vào mùa đông.

drill.t: There was a ___ fall in cases.
drill.vi: Số ca giảm nhẹ.

drill.t: The figure ___ between 20 and 30.
drill.vi: Con số dao động từ 20 đến 30.

lines.t: Who should pay for healthcare: individuals or the government?
lines.vi: Ai nên chi trả y tế: cá nhân hay chính phủ?

lines.t: I’d say it should be shared. The government should cover basic services and emergencies, because nobody should die simply because they are poor. But people can pay part of the cost through health insurance.
lines.vi: Tôi cho rằng nên chia sẻ. Chính phủ nên chi trả dịch vụ cơ bản và cấp cứu, vì không ai nên chết chỉ vì nghèo. Nhưng người dân có thể trả một phần qua bảo hiểm y tế.

lines.t: Why do some people ignore health advice?
lines.vi: Vì sao một số người phớt lờ lời khuyên về sức khoẻ?

lines.t: Partly because the benefits are long-term. If you eat fast food today, you don’t feel ill tomorrow, so it’s easy to believe the risk isn’t real. Stress and long working hours also make healthy habits harder.
lines.vi: Một phần vì lợi ích mang tính lâu dài. Ăn đồ ăn nhanh hôm nay thì mai chưa thấy ốm, nên dễ tin là rủi ro không có thật. Căng thẳng và làm việc nhiều giờ cũng khiến thói quen lành mạnh khó hơn.

lines.t: How might an ageing population affect healthcare?
lines.vi: Dân số già hoá có thể ảnh hưởng y tế ra sao?

lines.t: It will put a lot of pressure on hospitals, because older people tend to have chronic conditions. Countries will need more nurses and more care at home, not just bigger hospitals.
lines.vi: Nó sẽ gây áp lực lớn lên bệnh viện, vì người già thường mắc bệnh mãn tính. Các nước sẽ cần nhiều điều dưỡng và chăm sóc tại nhà hơn, chứ không chỉ bệnh viện lớn hơn.

gram2.title: Cause and effect language
gram2.rule: lead to / result in / cause + noun · be caused by / result from · As a result, … · Consequently, … · due to + noun
gram2.note: Leads to and results in go from cause to effect: Smoking leads to lung disease. Results from and is caused by go from effect back to cause: Lung disease often results from smoking. Due to and because of are followed by a noun, not a clause.

ex.t: Poor diet can lead to obesity.
ex.vi: Chế độ ăn kém có thể dẫn đến béo phì.

ex.t: Many deaths result from road accidents.
ex.vi: Nhiều ca tử vong do tai nạn giao thông.

ex.t: Hospitals are crowded due to a shortage of doctors.
ex.vi: Bệnh viện đông vì thiếu bác sĩ.

ex.t: As a result, waiting times have increased.
ex.vi: Kết quả là thời gian chờ đã tăng.

drill.t: Stress can ___ sleep problems.

drill.t: The illness ___ a virus.
drill.vi: Căn bệnh do virus gây ra.

drill.t: The clinic closed ___ a lack of funding.
drill.vi: Phòng khám đóng cửa vì thiếu kinh phí.

drill.t: Fewer people smoke. ___, lung cancer rates are falling.
drill.vi: Ít người hút thuốc hơn. Do đó tỉ lệ ung thư phổi giảm.

cue.card: Describe a time when you were ill or injured.
points: and explain how you felt about it
model: I’m going to describe the time I broke my wrist, about three years ago. It was a rainy evening and I was riding my motorbike home from work when the road suddenly became slippery and I fell off at quite low speed.

At first I thought it was just a bruise, but the pain got worse overnight, so the next morning I went to the hospital. An X-ray showed a small fracture, and the doctor put my arm in a cast for six weeks. After that I needed about a month of physiotherapy, because my wrist had become very stiff.

Honestly, I felt quite frustrated, because I couldn’t type properly and I had to ask colleagues for help. But looking back, it taught me two things: to slow down in bad weather, and to appreciate how much work nurses and physiotherapists do. Since then I’ve also become much more careful about road safety.

write.prompt: The graph below shows the average number of hospital visits per person per year in three age groups in one country between 2000 and 2020. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
plan: Introduction: paraphrase (average number of visits → how often people in each age group went to hospital)
Overview: over-65s visited most and rose strongly; children fell; working-age stayed stable
Body 1: the 65+ group with the start, middle and end figures
Body 2: children and working-age adults, including the point where they meet in 2020
model: The line graph illustrates how often people in three age groups went to hospital on average each year in a particular country from 2000 to 2020.

Overall, people aged 65 and over visited hospitals far more frequently than the other two groups, and their figure rose considerably. In contrast, visits by children declined, while the rate for working-age adults remained relatively stable.

In 2000, an older person went to hospital 5.5 times a year on average. This figure increased steadily throughout the period, climbing to 7.2 in 2010 before rising more sharply to reach a peak of 9.8 visits in 2020, almost double the original level.

Children aged 0 to 14 started at 3.2 visits per year, but this number fell gradually to 2.4 by 2020. The figure for people aged 15 to 64 fluctuated slightly between 2.0 and 2.3 before ending at 2.4, which meant that by the end of the period children and working-age adults visited hospitals equally often.

units.title: Crime & the law
units.goal: Discuss crime, punishment and safety, and write a problem–solution essay.

words.ex: Young offenders need education, not just prison.
words.exVi: Người phạm tội trẻ tuổi cần được giáo dục, không chỉ là tù.

words.ex: Most people who commit a crime are under 25.
words.exVi: Phần lớn người phạm tội dưới 25 tuổi.

words.ex: The punishment should fit the crime.
words.exVi: Hình phạt nên tương xứng với tội.

words.ex: He received a two-year prison sentence.
words.exVi: Anh ta nhận án tù hai năm.

words.ex: Rehabilitation helps prisoners return to society.
words.exVi: Cải tạo giúp phạm nhân tái hoà nhập xã hội.

words.ex: Heavy fines act as a deterrent.
words.exVi: Phạt nặng có tác dụng răn đe.

words.ex: Many prisoners reoffend within two years.
words.exVi: Nhiều phạm nhân tái phạm trong vòng hai năm.

words.ex: Juvenile crime has fallen in recent years.
words.exVi: Tội phạm vị thành niên đã giảm mấy năm gần đây.

words.ex: Pickpocketing is a common petty crime.
words.exVi: Móc túi là tội vặt phổ biến.

words.ex: Violent crime is rare in this area.
words.exVi: Tội phạm bạo lực hiếm gặp ở khu này.

words.ex: Law enforcement agencies share information.
words.exVi: Các cơ quan thực thi pháp luật chia sẻ thông tin.

words.ex: He was ordered to do community service.
words.exVi: Anh ta bị buộc làm lao động công ích.

words.ex: CCTV surveillance has reduced theft.
words.exVi: Giám sát bằng camera đã giảm trộm cắp.

words.ex: The victim reported the theft to the police.
words.exVi: Nạn nhân trình báo vụ trộm với cảnh sát.

words.ex: She was fined for speeding.
words.exVi: Cô ấy bị phạt vì chạy quá tốc độ.

words.ex: It is illegal to drive without a licence.
words.exVi: Lái xe không bằng là bất hợp pháp.

words.ex: Poverty is closely linked to crime.
words.exVi: Nghèo đói gắn chặt với tội phạm.

words.ex: The government must tackle youth unemployment.
words.exVi: Chính phủ phải giải quyết thất nghiệp ở người trẻ.

words.ex: Cybercrime costs businesses billions.

words.exVi: Chúng ta phải xử lý nguyên nhân gốc rễ của tội phạm.

lines.t: Do you feel safe in the area where you live?
lines.vi: Bạn có thấy an toàn ở khu mình sống không?

lines.t: Generally, yes. Violent crime is very rare, although petty crime like phone snatching does happen on busy streets, so I’m careful at night.
lines.vi: Nhìn chung là có. Tội phạm bạo lực rất hiếm, dù tội vặt như giật điện thoại vẫn xảy ra ở phố đông, nên buổi tối tôi khá cẩn thận.

lines.t: Have you ever lost something valuable?
lines.vi: Bạn đã bao giờ mất đồ quý chưa?

lines.t: Once. Someone took my wallet on a crowded bus. I reported it to the police, but I never got it back.
lines.vi: Một lần. Có người lấy ví tôi trên xe buýt đông. Tôi đã trình báo cảnh sát nhưng không bao giờ tìm lại được.

lines.t: Are there many security cameras in your city?
lines.vi: Thành phố bạn có nhiều camera an ninh không?

lines.t: More and more. Most shops and apartment buildings have CCTV now, and I think that surveillance makes people think twice before stealing.
lines.vi: Ngày càng nhiều. Giờ hầu hết cửa hàng và chung cư đều có camera, và tôi nghĩ việc giám sát khiến người ta phải nghĩ kỹ trước khi trộm cắp.

sents.t: In many countries, more than half of prisoners reoffend within five years of release.
sents.vi: Ở nhiều nước, hơn một nửa phạm nhân tái phạm trong năm năm sau khi ra tù.

sents.t: Norway has one of the lowest reoffending rates in the world, at around 20 per cent.
sents.vi: Na Uy có tỉ lệ tái phạm thuộc hàng thấp nhất thế giới, khoảng 20%.

sents.t: Its prisons focus on rehabilitation, offering education and job training to almost every inmate.
sents.vi: Nhà tù của họ tập trung vào cải tạo, cung cấp giáo dục và đào tạo nghề cho gần như mọi phạm nhân.

sents.t: Critics say this approach is too soft and does not satisfy victims.
sents.vi: Những người phản đối nói cách này quá nhẹ tay và không làm nạn nhân thoả đáng.

sents.t: Supporters reply that fewer repeat crimes means fewer victims in the future.
sents.vi: Những người ủng hộ đáp lại rằng ít tái phạm hơn nghĩa là ít nạn nhân hơn trong tương lai.

q.q: Norway’s reoffending rate is about one in five.
Norwegian prisons offer education to very few prisoners.
Norway spends more on prisons than any other country.

gram.title: Second and third conditionals for arguments
gram.rule: If + past simple, would + verb (unreal now) · If + past perfect, would have + past participle (unreal past)
gram.note: Use the second conditional to discuss imaginary policies: If prisons offered more training, fewer people would reoffend. Use the third conditional for past situations that did not happen: If he had received support, he would not have committed the crime. Never put would in the if-clause.

ex.t: If the police were more visible, people would feel safer.
ex.vi: Nếu cảnh sát xuất hiện nhiều hơn, người dân sẽ thấy an toàn hơn.

ex.t: If young people had jobs, they would be less likely to commit crimes.
ex.vi: Nếu người trẻ có việc làm, họ ít có khả năng phạm tội hơn.

ex.t: If she had locked the door, the burglar would not have got in.
ex.vi: Nếu cô ấy khoá cửa thì tên trộm đã không vào được.

ex.t: Crime would fall if poverty were reduced.
ex.vi: Tội phạm sẽ giảm nếu nghèo đói được giảm bớt.

drill.t: If fines ___ higher, fewer people would speed.
drill.vi: Nếu tiền phạt cao hơn, sẽ ít người chạy quá tốc độ.

lines.t: Why do young people commit crimes?

lines.t: There are several root causes. Some come from poor families and see crime as an easy way to get money. Others are influenced by friends, and a few simply want excitement because they have nothing else to do.
lines.vi: Có nhiều nguyên nhân gốc rễ. Một số đến từ gia đình nghèo và coi phạm tội là cách kiếm tiền dễ. Số khác bị bạn bè ảnh hưởng, và vài người chỉ muốn cảm giác mạnh vì không có gì khác để làm.

lines.t: Is prison the best punishment?

lines.t: How has crime changed with technology?

lines.t: Cybercrime has grown enormously. Criminals don’t need to break into your house anymore; they can steal your bank details with one fake message. Law enforcement has to learn new skills to keep up.
lines.vi: Tội phạm mạng tăng vọt. Kẻ gian không cần đột nhập nhà bạn nữa; chúng có thể lấy thông tin ngân hàng chỉ bằng một tin nhắn giả. Cơ quan thực thi pháp luật phải học kỹ năng mới để theo kịp.

gram2.title: Problem–solution language
gram2.rule: One major cause of … is … · This problem could be tackled by + -ing · An effective solution would be to … · If this were done, …
gram2.note: In a problem–solution essay, link each solution clearly to a cause. Use modal verbs to sound measured: could, would, should. A good pattern is: cause → solution → expected result: One cause is unemployment. This could be tackled by offering training, which would give young people a legal income.

ex.t: One major cause of crime is unemployment.
ex.vi: Một nguyên nhân chính của tội phạm là thất nghiệp.

ex.t: This problem could be tackled by investing in youth centres.
ex.vi: Vấn đề này có thể được giải quyết bằng cách đầu tư vào trung tâm thanh niên.

ex.t: An effective solution would be to improve street lighting.
ex.vi: Một giải pháp hiệu quả sẽ là cải thiện chiếu sáng đường phố.

ex.t: If this were done, people would feel safer at night.
ex.vi: Nếu làm được điều này, mọi người sẽ thấy an toàn hơn vào ban đêm.

cue.card: Describe a rule or law in your country that you think is important.
points: what the rule or law is
and explain why you think it is important
model: I’d like to talk about the law that makes it illegal to drive after drinking any alcohol at all. In Vietnam this zero-tolerance rule was introduced in 2020, and the fines are very heavy — a motorbike rider can lose their licence for almost two years.

At first a lot of people complained, because drinking with friends after work is a big part of our culture, and restaurant owners said they were losing customers. But the police enforced it strictly, with checkpoints in the evenings, so people quickly changed their habits. Now it’s normal for groups to take a taxi or use a ride-hailing app after a party.

I think it’s important because traffic accidents are one of the main causes of death for young people here. The law works as a real deterrent: a friend of mine who used to ride home after a few beers now never does. If this law hadn’t been introduced, I think thousands more families would have lost someone on the roads.

write.prompt: In many cities, crime rates among young people are increasing. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to solve it?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase the problem; say there are social and family causes and practical solutions
Body 1: causes — unemployment and boredom; peer pressure and weak family supervision
Body 2: solutions — training and youth centres; parenting support and community service for first offenders
Conclusion: summarise causes and solutions in new words
model: Crime committed by young people appears to be rising in many urban areas. This essay will argue that the main causes are a lack of opportunities and weak social support, and that these problems can be tackled through education, activities for teenagers and better guidance for families.

One major cause of youth crime is unemployment. When school leavers cannot find work, some turn to theft or selling stolen goods because it seems like the only way to earn money. Boredom is a related factor: in neighbourhoods with no sports facilities or clubs, teenagers spend their evenings on the street, where they are easily drawn into trouble. Peer pressure and a lack of supervision at home make this situation worse, particularly when both parents work long hours.

These problems could be tackled in several ways. Firstly, governments should fund vocational training and apprenticeships, which would give young people a legal income and a sense of purpose. Secondly, local authorities could open youth centres offering sport, music and homework help, so that teenagers have safe places to go after school. Finally, first-time offenders should be given community service rather than prison sentences, because prison often brings them into contact with more serious criminals and increases the chance that they will reoffend.

In conclusion, youth crime is largely driven by unemployment, boredom and insufficient support from families and communities. If young people were offered training, activities and a second chance instead of harsh punishment, I believe crime rates among this age group would fall significantly.

Visitor numbers increased after cars were removed.

gram.title: Passive forms for describing maps
gram.rule: was built / was demolished / was converted into / was replaced by / has been extended · There used to be …
gram.note: Map tasks compare two times, so use the past passive (was built) for changes between past dates and the present perfect passive (has been extended) when the second map is now. Use prepositions of place: to the north of, next to, opposite, in the centre. Avoid saying who made the change; it is not important.

lines.t: What are the biggest problems in large cities today?
lines.vi: Những vấn đề lớn nhất của thành phố lớn hiện nay là gì?

lines.t: I’d say housing and transport. Because of rapid urbanisation, there simply isn’t enough affordable housing, and traffic congestion wastes hours of people’s time every week.
lines.vi: Tôi cho là nhà ở và giao thông. Do đô thị hoá nhanh, đơn giản là không đủ nhà giá phải chăng, và tắc đường lãng phí hàng giờ của mọi người mỗi tuần.

gram2.title: Expressing the future with certainty and doubt

cue.card: Describe a place in a city that has changed a lot.
points: and explain how you feel about the change
model: I’m going to describe the riverside area in my hometown, which has been completely redeveloped over the last ten years.

When I was a child, it was quite an unattractive place. There were small warehouses, a fish market and a muddy road along the water, and people rarely went there unless they had to. In the evening it was dark and, honestly, a little unsafe.

Now it’s unrecognisable. The warehouses were demolished and replaced by a long pedestrianised promenade with trees, benches and a cycle lane. A couple of the old buildings were kept and converted into cafés, and there’s an open-air stage where concerts are held at weekends. I have mixed feelings about it. On the one hand, it’s one of the best green spaces in the city and families love it. On the other hand, the fish market moved to the outskirts, so the area has lost some of its character, and many of the new apartments nearby are far from affordable for local people.

write.prompt: The maps below show the centre of a small town called Riverton in 1990 and today. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
write.data:
1990: north — farmland; centre — small market square, two-lane main road through the middle; east — factory beside the river; south — houses and a primary school; west — forest.
Today: north — housing estate; centre — pedestrianised square with shops (main road moved to the west); east — factory converted into a museum, new footbridge over the river; south — houses and primary school (unchanged), new sports centre; west — forest reduced by half, new bypass road and car park.
plan: Introduction: paraphrase (show → illustrate; today → the present day)
Overview: the town became more residential and pedestrian-friendly; nature was reduced; the south stayed mostly the same
Body 1: north and centre — farmland → housing; square pedestrianised; road moved
Body 2: east, west and south — museum, footbridge, bypass, car park, sports centre
model: The maps illustrate the changes that have taken place in the centre of Riverton between 1990 and the present day.

Overall, the town has become considerably more residential and more pedestrian-friendly, with traffic moved away from the centre. These developments, however, have come at the expense of farmland and part of the forest, while the southern area has remained largely unchanged.

The most noticeable change is in the north, where the farmland has been replaced by a large housing estate. In the centre, the main road that used to run through the town has been relocated to the west, allowing the old market square to be pedestrianised and lined with shops.

To the east, the factory beside the river has been converted into a museum, and a new footbridge now crosses the river. In the west, around half of the forest has been cleared to make room for a bypass road and a car park. Finally, the houses and primary school in the south are still there, although a sports centre has been added next to them.

read.title: The rise of the gig economy

sents.t: Around one in six workers in some Asian cities now earn money through apps, for example by delivering food.
sents.vi: Khoảng một phần sáu lao động ở một số thành phố châu Á hiện kiếm tiền qua ứng dụng, chẳng hạn giao đồ ăn.

sents.t: Many choose this work because they can decide when and how much to work.

gram.title: Comparing figures precisely
gram.rule: twice as many as · three times higher than · slightly / considerably / significantly more · the same proportion as · in contrast, … · whereas
gram.note: In Task 1, avoid repeating “more than”. Use multiples (twice as many …as), adverbs that show size (considerably higher), and linking words that show contrast (whereas, in contrast). Use the number of for countable nouns and the amount of for uncountable ones; use the proportion / percentage of for parts of a whole.

ex.t: Twice as many men as women worked in manufacturing.
ex.vi: Số nam làm sản xuất gấp đôi nữ.

lines.t: Will automation cause mass unemployment?

lines.t: I don’t think so, at least not permanently. Automation will certainly replace some jobs, especially in manufacturing, but new jobs will appear too. The real challenge is helping older workers retrain.
lines.vi: Tôi không nghĩ vậy, ít nhất không phải mãi mãi. Tự động hoá chắc chắn sẽ thay thế một số công việc, nhất là trong sản xuất, nhưng việc làm mới cũng sẽ xuất hiện. Thách thức thật sự là giúp người lớn tuổi đào tạo lại.

lines.t: Why do young people change jobs so often?
lines.vi: Vì sao người trẻ hay đổi việc?

lines.t: Partly for higher salaries, because job-hopping is often the quickest way to get a pay rise. They also want work that matches their values, and they’re less willing than their parents to stay in a job they dislike.
lines.vi: Một phần vì lương cao hơn, vì nhảy việc thường là cách nhanh nhất để tăng lương. Họ cũng muốn công việc phù hợp giá trị của mình, và ít chấp nhận hơn bố mẹ việc ở lại một công việc mình không thích.

lines.t: Is job satisfaction more important than salary?
lines.vi: Sự hài lòng trong công việc có quan trọng hơn lương không?

lines.t: Once you earn enough to live comfortably, yes. Research suggests that above a certain income, a higher salary doesn’t make people much happier, but a good manager and meaningful tasks do.
lines.vi: Khi đã kiếm đủ để sống thoải mái thì có. Nghiên cứu cho thấy trên một mức thu nhập nhất định, lương cao hơn không làm người ta hạnh phúc hơn nhiều, nhưng một người quản lý tốt và công việc ý nghĩa thì có.

gram2.title: Hedging: sounding careful, not absolute
gram2.rule: tend to · it seems that · generally · in most cases · to some extent · may / might / could
gram2.note: Strong claims such as “Everyone hates their job” are easy to disagree with. Hedging makes your argument more accurate and sounds more academic: Young people tend to change jobs more often. Use it in both Speaking Part 3 and Task 2, but don’t hedge every sentence or you will sound unsure.

ex.t: In most cases, experience matters more than a degree.

ex.t: Automation could reduce some types of jobs.
ex.vi: Tự động hoá có thể làm giảm một số loại việc làm.

cue.card: Describe a job you would not like to do.
points: what people in this job do
why you would not like it
and explain whether you think it is an important job
model: A job I really wouldn’t like to do is working as a call-centre operator, particularly in customer complaints.

People in this job sit at a desk for eight or nine hours, answering one call after another. Most callers are already angry when they phone, because something has gone wrong with a product or a bill, and the operator has to calm them down and follow a strict script. Their performance is measured very closely — how long each call lasts, how many calls they take — so there’s a lot of pressure.

I wouldn’t enjoy it for two reasons. First, I find repetitive work quite draining, and I think I’d experience burnout fairly quickly. Second, I’d find it hard not to take people’s anger personally. That said, I think it’s an important job. When I had a problem with my internet connection last year, a patient operator solved it in ten minutes and completely changed my opinion of the company. So I really respect people who do it well.

write.prompt: The bar chart below shows the percentage of workers in four employment sectors in one country in 1990 and 2020. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
write.data:
Sector            1990    2020
Agriculture       48%     22%
Manufacturing     20%     27%
Services          28%     46%
Other              4%      5%
plan: Introduction: paraphrase (percentage of workers → proportion of the workforce employed in)
Overview: agriculture was the largest in 1990 but services was the largest in 2020; agriculture fell by more than half
Body 1: agriculture and services — the main swap
Body 2: manufacturing and other — smaller changes
model: The bar chart compares the proportion of the workforce employed in four different sectors in one country in 1990 and 2020.

Overall, there was a clear shift away from agriculture over the thirty-year period. While farming was the main source of employment in 1990, the service sector had become the largest employer by 2020.

In 1990, almost half of all workers (48%) were employed in agriculture, compared with only 28% in services. By 2020, however, the situation had reversed: the share of agricultural workers had fallen by more than half to 22%, whereas the percentage working in services had risen significantly to 46%, making it more than twice as large as the agricultural sector.

Manufacturing also grew, although more modestly, increasing from a fifth of the workforce to 27%. Meanwhile, the proportion of people working in other sectors remained very small and almost unchanged, rising only slightly from 4% to 5%.

units.goal: Discuss advertising and spending habits, and write an agree/disagree essay.

lines.t: Do you pay attention to advertisements?

lines.t: Not really. I usually skip adverts on videos as soon as I can. But I have to admit that some clever slogans stay in my head for days.
lines.vi: Không hẳn. Tôi thường bỏ qua quảng cáo trên video ngay khi có thể. Nhưng phải thừa nhận vài khẩu hiệu thông minh cứ ở trong đầu tôi mấy ngày.

lines.t: Have you ever bought something because of an advert?
lines.vi: Bạn đã bao giờ mua gì vì một quảng cáo chưa?

lines.t: Yes, a pair of running shoes. A famous athlete endorsed them, and the advert made them look perfect. They were fine, but nothing special.
lines.vi: Có, một đôi giày chạy bộ. Một vận động viên nổi tiếng quảng bá cho chúng và quảng cáo làm chúng trông hoàn hảo. Giày cũng được, nhưng không có gì đặc biệt.

lines.t: Where do you see the most adverts?

lines.t: Definitely on social media. It’s a bit worrying how accurate the targeted advertising is — I search for something once and then see it everywhere.

sents.t: Today, however, most advertising to children happens online, where it is much harder to regulate.

gram.title: Agreeing and disagreeing in essays
gram.rule: I completely agree / disagree that … · I partly agree … · There is some truth in the idea that … · I am not convinced that …
gram.note: For an agree/disagree question, state your position clearly in the introduction and keep it the same in the conclusion. If you partly agree, say exactly which part you accept and which part you reject. Avoid “I 100% agree” and other informal phrases.

ex.t: I completely agree that tobacco adverts should be banned.
ex.vi: Tôi hoàn toàn đồng ý rằng quảng cáo thuốc lá nên bị cấm.

ex.t: I partly agree with this statement.
ex.vi: Tôi đồng ý một phần với nhận định này.

ex.t: There is some truth in the idea that adverts are useful.
ex.vi: Có phần đúng trong ý kiến rằng quảng cáo hữu ích.

ex.t: I am not convinced that a total ban would work.
ex.vi: Tôi không tin rằng cấm hoàn toàn sẽ hiệu quả.

drill.t: I ___ agree that adverts can be useful.
drill.vi: Tôi đồng ý một phần rằng quảng cáo có thể hữu ích.

drill.t: There is some ___ in this argument.
drill.vi: Lập luận này có phần đúng.

drill.t: I am not ___ that this policy works.
drill.vi: Tôi không tin chính sách này hiệu quả.

drill.t: I ___ disagree with the idea.
drill.vi: Tôi phản đối mạnh mẽ ý kiến này.

lines.t: Do advertisements have a positive effect on society?
lines.vi: Quảng cáo có tác động tích cực đến xã hội không?

lines.t: They can. Adverts inform people about new products and services, and public campaigns, like ones about road safety, can actually save lives. The problem is when adverts are misleading.
lines.vi: Có thể. Quảng cáo cung cấp thông tin về sản phẩm, dịch vụ mới, và các chiến dịch cộng đồng như về an toàn giao thông thực sự có thể cứu người. Vấn đề là khi quảng cáo gây hiểu lầm.

lines.t: Why are young people so interested in brands?
lines.vi: Vì sao người trẻ quan tâm nhiều đến thương hiệu?

lines.t: Mostly because of peer pressure. A branded phone or trainers work as a status symbol at school, and teenagers want to fit in. Social media influencers make this even stronger.
lines.vi: Chủ yếu vì áp lực bạn bè. Điện thoại hay giày hàng hiệu là biểu tượng địa vị ở trường, và thiếu niên muốn hoà nhập. Người có ảnh hưởng trên mạng xã hội càng làm điều này mạnh hơn.

lines.t: Should the government control advertising?
lines.vi: Chính phủ có nên kiểm soát quảng cáo không?

lines.t: To some extent. I think adverts for unhealthy products like alcohol and junk food should be regulated, especially when they target children. But banning all advertising would hurt small businesses.
lines.vi: Ở mức độ nào đó. Tôi nghĩ quảng cáo sản phẩm không lành mạnh như rượu và đồ ăn vặt nên bị quản lý, nhất là khi nhắm vào trẻ em. Nhưng cấm mọi quảng cáo sẽ gây hại cho doanh nghiệp nhỏ.

gram2.title: Relative clauses for adding information
gram2.rule: who / which / that (defining) · , who / , which (non-defining, with commas) · , which refers to the whole sentence
gram2.note: Defining clauses tell us which one: Adverts that target children should be banned (no commas). Non-defining clauses add extra information with commas, and you cannot use that: Coca-Cola, which spends billions on marketing, … A clause with “, which” can also comment on a whole idea: Adverts are everywhere, which makes them hard to avoid.

ex.t: Adverts that target children should be controlled.
ex.vi: Quảng cáo nhắm vào trẻ em nên được kiểm soát.

ex.t: Influencers, who are often paid by brands, have huge audiences.
ex.vi: Người có ảnh hưởng, thường được thương hiệu trả tiền, có lượng người xem khổng lồ.

ex.t: Online adverts follow us everywhere, which can be annoying.

ex.vi: Người tiêu quá nhiều thường mắc nợ.

cue.card: Describe an advertisement that you remember well.
points: and explain why you remember it
model: The advert I remember best was for a mobile network, and I first saw it on TV around Lunar New Year a few years ago.

It told a very simple story. A young man is working in a big city and can’t afford to go home for Tet. His elderly mother doesn’t know how to use a smartphone, so his little niece secretly teaches her, and on New Year’s Eve the mother surprises him with a video call. The whole family appears on the screen, and the slogan at the end is something like “Distance is only a number”.

I remember it for two reasons. First, it was emotional without being misleading — it didn’t claim the network was the fastest or the cheapest, it just showed what the service makes possible. Second, it was very close to my own situation at the time, because I was also working far from home. Honestly, I’ve forgotten most adverts I’ve ever seen, but that one made me phone my parents that evening.

write.prompt: Advertising aimed at children should be banned. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase + clear position (agree for young children and unhealthy products; total ban too extreme)
Body 1: why children need protection — cannot judge adverts, junk food, pester power
Body 2: why a total ban is unrealistic — educational products, online enforcement, media literacy is better
Conclusion: restate the partial agreement
model: Many people believe that companies should not be allowed to advertise to children at all. While I agree that young children need strong protection, especially from adverts for unhealthy products, I believe a complete ban would be difficult to enforce and is not the most effective solution.

There are good reasons to restrict this kind of advertising. Young children cannot easily distinguish between entertainment and persuasion, so they tend to believe whatever an advert tells them. Much of the marketing aimed at them promotes sugary snacks and expensive toys, which can contribute to poor diets and make children more materialistic. In addition, advertisers deliberately encourage children to pressure their parents into buying products, which creates conflict in families with limited budgets.

However, banning all advertising to children would be unrealistic. Not every advert is harmful: some inform families about books, educational apps or sports clubs. Furthermore, most children now spend their time on international websites and games, where national laws are very hard to apply. In my view, it would be more effective to ban advertising of unhealthy food and to require clear labelling of sponsored content, while schools teach children how adverts try to persuade them.

In conclusion, I partly agree with the statement. Advertising aimed at children should be strictly regulated, and adverts for harmful products should be prohibited, but a total ban is neither practical nor necessary if children are taught to recognise persuasive techniques.

lines.t: Do you prefer travelling in your own country or abroad?

lines.t: At the moment, domestic travel, because it’s cheaper and Vietnam has so much variety, from mountains in the north to islands in the south.
lines.vi: Hiện tại là trong nước, vì rẻ hơn và Việt Nam rất đa dạng, từ núi ở phía bắc đến đảo ở phía nam.

lines.t: What kind of places do you like to visit?
lines.vi: Bạn thích đến những nơi như thế nào?

lines.t: Places off the beaten track. I find famous spots too commercialised, so I’d rather stay in a small village and eat whatever the locals eat.
lines.vi: Những nơi ít người biết. Tôi thấy các điểm nổi tiếng quá thương mại hoá, nên tôi thích ở một ngôi làng nhỏ và ăn những gì người dân ăn.

lines.t: Do you buy souvenirs?
lines.vi: Bạn có mua quà lưu niệm không?

lines.t: Only small, local things, like handmade tea or textiles. I avoid the mass-produced ones you find at every tourist trap.
lines.vi: Chỉ những thứ nhỏ, của địa phương như trà làm tay hay vải dệt. Tôi tránh đồ sản xuất hàng loạt bán ở mọi điểm chặt chém du khách.

sents.t: Venice has about 50,000 residents but receives more than 20 million visitors a year.
sents.vi: Venice có khoảng 50.000 cư dân nhưng đón hơn 20 triệu lượt khách mỗi năm.

sents.t: Rising rents caused by holiday apartments have forced many local families to leave.
sents.vi: Giá thuê tăng do căn hộ cho khách du lịch đã buộc nhiều gia đình địa phương rời đi.

sents.t: In 2024 the city began charging day visitors an entrance fee on busy days.
sents.vi: Năm 2024, thành phố bắt đầu thu phí vào cửa với khách trong ngày vào những ngày đông.

sents.t: Officials hope the fee will spread visitors more evenly across the year.
sents.vi: Chính quyền hy vọng mức phí sẽ phân bổ du khách đều hơn trong năm.

sents.t: Critics argue that the fee is too small to change tourists’ behaviour.
sents.vi: Những người phản đối cho rằng mức phí quá nhỏ để thay đổi hành vi du khách.

q.q: Venice receives far more visitors than it has residents.
The entrance fee applies to all visitors every day of the year.
The fee has already reduced visitor numbers by half.

gram.title: Describing proportions in pie charts
gram.rule: account for · make up · constitute · represent · a quarter / a third / the majority / a small minority · just under / just over
gram.note: Pie charts show parts of a whole, so focus on proportions rather than rises and falls (unless there are two years). Vary your verbs: accounted for, made up, represented. Turn percentages into fractions when they are close: 26% → just over a quarter; 48% → just under half; 70% → the vast majority.

lines.t: What are the benefits of international tourism?
lines.vi: Lợi ích của du lịch quốc tế là gì?

lines.t: Economically, it brings in a lot of revenue and creates jobs in hospitality. Culturally, it encourages exchange; when people meet each other face to face, stereotypes tend to break down.
lines.vi: Về kinh tế, nó mang lại nhiều doanh thu và tạo việc làm trong ngành dịch vụ lưu trú. Về văn hoá, nó thúc đẩy giao lưu; khi gặp nhau trực tiếp, định kiến thường mất dần.

lines.t: Can tourism damage local culture?
lines.vi: Du lịch có thể làm hỏng văn hoá địa phương không?

lines.t: Yes, if it isn’t managed. Traditions sometimes turn into performances just for visitors, and places become so commercialised that they lose their authentic character.
lines.vi: Có, nếu không được quản lý. Truyền thống đôi khi trở thành màn trình diễn chỉ cho du khách, và nơi đó thương mại hoá đến mức mất đi nét chân thực.

lines.t: How can tourism be made more sustainable?

lines.t: Governments could limit visitor numbers at heritage sites and support ecotourism, where the money stays in the local community. Tourists can also help by travelling outside peak season.
lines.vi: Chính phủ có thể giới hạn số khách ở các di sản và hỗ trợ du lịch sinh thái, nơi tiền ở lại với cộng đồng địa phương. Du khách cũng có thể góp phần bằng cách đi ngoài mùa cao điểm.

gram2.title: Talking about benefits and drawbacks
gram2.rule: One advantage / benefit of … is that … · The main drawback is … · On the positive side, … · A downside of … is …
gram2.note: Use noun phrases to organise ideas: The main benefit of tourism is that it creates jobs. After of, use a noun or -ing: the advantage of travelling. After is that, use a full clause. Balance positive and negative points in Part 3 to show a mature view.

cue.card: Describe a tourist attraction you visited that you would recommend.
points: what it is and where it is
and explain why you would recommend it
model: I’d recommend the Ban Gioc waterfall in Cao Bang province, right on the border between Vietnam and China. I went there with three friends two summers ago, during the rainy season, which is actually the best time because the water is at its strongest.

It’s a long trip — about seven hours by coach from Hanoi — but the journey itself is part of the experience, because the road winds through limestone mountains and rice terraces. When we arrived, we took a small bamboo raft right up to the bottom of the falls. The spray was so strong that we got completely soaked, but it was breathtaking. In the evening we stayed with a Tay family in a nearby village, who cooked us dinner and taught us a few words of their language.

I’d recommend it because it still feels authentic. Unlike some famous places, it hasn’t become a tourist trap yet: the entrance fee is reasonable and most of the money goes to local people. My only advice is to go soon, before mass tourism changes it.

write.prompt: The pie charts below show the purpose of visits to one country in 2005 and 2025. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
write.data:
Purpose of visit       2005    2025
Holiday / leisure      52%     38%
Business               26%     18%
Visiting friends       12%     14%
Study                   6%     20%
Other                   4%     10%
plan: Introduction: paraphrase (purpose of visits → reasons why people travelled to)
Overview: holidays were the main reason in both years but fell; study rose most dramatically
Body 1: holiday and business — the two that declined
Body 2: study, visiting friends and other — the ones that grew
model: The two pie charts compare the reasons why international visitors travelled to a particular country in 2005 and 2025.

Overall, holidays were the most common purpose of visits in both years, although their share declined. The most striking change was the rapid growth in visitors coming to study, while business travel became less significant.

In 2005, just over half of all visits (52%) were for holidays and leisure. Twenty years later, this proportion had fallen to 38%, but it still remained the largest category. Business trips followed a similar pattern, decreasing from just over a quarter of visits to 18%.

By contrast, the share of people visiting to study more than tripled, rising from only 6% to a fifth of all visits by 2025. Visits to friends and relatives increased slightly, from 12% to 14%, and the proportion of trips for other reasons also grew, from 4% to 10%.

lines.t: Did you like science subjects at school?

lines.t: Do you read about science now?

lines.t: Sometimes. I follow a few channels that explain new discoveries in simple language, especially anything about space or artificial intelligence.
lines.vi: Thỉnh thoảng. Tôi theo dõi vài kênh giải thích những khám phá mới bằng ngôn ngữ đơn giản, nhất là về vũ trụ hay trí tuệ nhân tạo.

lines.t: Should governments fund scientific research?

lines.t: Yes, because a lot of important research doesn’t make money quickly, so private companies won’t pay for it. Many breakthroughs, like the internet, started with government funding.

cue.card: Describe an invention that has changed people’s lives.
points: when it was invented or became popular
and explain how it has changed people’s lives
model: I’d like to talk about online maps, particularly navigation apps on smartphones. The technology existed earlier, but it only became really popular in my country around 2012, when cheap smartphones and mobile data spread.

People use them for far more than just finding directions. They check traffic before leaving home, look up opening hours, read reviews of restaurants and even share their live location with family members. Delivery riders and taxi drivers basically depend on them for their whole job.

They’ve changed our lives in several ways. Most obviously, getting lost has almost disappeared — my parents still talk about stopping to ask strangers for directions. They’ve also created thousands of jobs in delivery and ride-hailing. On the other hand, some research suggests that relying on navigation apps has weakened our natural sense of direction. I’ve definitely noticed that I can’t remember routes as well as I used to, so it’s a good example of an invention that has both benefits and drawbacks.

write.prompt: The diagram below shows how coffee beans are processed. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features.
write.data: Stages: 1 coffee cherries picked by hand → 2 cherries washed and pulp removed → 3 beans dried in the sun for 2–3 weeks → 4 outer skin removed (hulling) → 5 beans sorted by size and quality → 6 beans roasted at about 200°C → 7 beans cooled → 8a packed as whole beans  OR  8b ground and packed.
plan: Introduction: paraphrase (how coffee beans are processed → the stages in producing coffee)
Overview: eight main stages, from picking to packing; two possible final products
Body 1: stages 1–4 — picking, washing, drying, hulling
Body 2: stages 5–8 — sorting, roasting, cooling, packing whole or ground
model: The diagram illustrates the stages involved in producing coffee, from picking the fruit to packing the finished product.
Overall, there are eight main stages in the process. It begins with harvesting coffee cherries by hand and ends with the beans being packed, either whole or after they have been ground.

First, ripe coffee cherries are picked by hand. They are then washed, and the soft pulp is removed so that only the beans remain. After that, the beans are spread out and dried in the sun for two to three weeks. Once they are completely dry, their outer skin is removed in a process known as hulling.

Next, the beans are sorted according to their size and quality. They are subsequently roasted at a temperature of around 200°C and then left to cool. Finally, the beans are packed. At this point there are two options: they can either be sold as whole beans or be ground into powder before packaging.

words.ex: My grandmother passed on her recipes to me.

lines.t: Do you live with your family?
lines.vi: Bạn có sống cùng gia đình không?

lines.t: Yes, in a multigenerational home — my parents, my grandmother, my wife and I. It’s a bit crowded, but it means someone is always there to help.
lines.vi: Có, trong một nhà nhiều thế hệ — bố mẹ, bà, vợ tôi và tôi. Hơi chật nhưng lúc nào cũng có người giúp đỡ.

lines.t: How often do you see your grandparents?
lines.vi: Bạn gặp ông bà thường xuyên không?

lines.t: Every day, since my grandmother lives with us. She’s eighty-five and still tells the best stories in the family.
lines.vi: Hằng ngày, vì bà sống cùng chúng tôi. Bà tám mươi lăm tuổi và vẫn kể chuyện hay nhất nhà.

lines.t: Is family more important to you now than when you were a child?
lines.vi: Gia đình có quan trọng với bạn hơn so với hồi bé không?

lines.t: I think so. As a child I took it for granted, but now I realise how much my parents sacrificed, so I try to spend more time with them.
lines.vi: Tôi nghĩ vậy. Hồi bé tôi coi đó là điều hiển nhiên, nhưng giờ tôi nhận ra bố mẹ đã hy sinh bao nhiêu, nên tôi cố dành nhiều thời gian hơn cho họ.

sents.t: Almost 30 per cent of people in Japan are now over 65, the highest proportion in the world.
sents.vi: Gần 30% dân số Nhật hiện trên 65 tuổi, tỉ lệ cao nhất thế giới.

sents.t: With a low birth rate, the working-age population has been shrinking since the 1990s.
sents.vi: Với tỉ lệ sinh thấp, dân số trong độ tuổi lao động đã giảm từ thập niên 1990.

sents.t: The government has responded by encouraging older people to keep working.
sents.vi: Chính phủ đã ứng phó bằng cách khuyến khích người già tiếp tục làm việc.

sents.t: Robots are also being tested in care homes to help staff lift and move residents.
sents.vi: Robot cũng đang được thử nghiệm ở viện dưỡng lão để giúp nhân viên nâng, di chuyển người cao tuổi.

sents.t: Nevertheless, there is still a serious shortage of nurses and caregivers.
sents.vi: Tuy vậy, vẫn thiếu nghiêm trọng điều dưỡng và người chăm sóc.

q.q: Japan has the highest proportion of over-65s in the world.
Japan’s working-age population started to grow in the 1990s.
Most Japanese care homes now use robots.

gram.title: Advantages–disadvantages essay structure
gram.rule: The main advantage is that … · Another benefit is … · However, this also has drawbacks. · Overall, the advantages outweigh the disadvantages.
gram.note: If the question asks “Do the advantages outweigh the disadvantages?”, you must give a clear answer. Write one body paragraph for each side, then explain in the conclusion which side is stronger and why. Use outweigh as a verb: the benefits outweigh the costs.

ex.t: The main advantage is that children grow up with grandparents.
ex.vi: Lợi ích chính là trẻ lớn lên cùng ông bà.

ex.t: Another benefit is lower childcare costs.
ex.vi: Một lợi ích khác là chi phí trông trẻ thấp hơn.

ex.t: However, this arrangement also has drawbacks.
ex.vi: Tuy nhiên, cách sắp xếp này cũng có hạn chế.

ex.t: In my view, the advantages outweigh the disadvantages.
ex.vi: Theo tôi, lợi ích lớn hơn bất lợi.

drill.t: The benefits ___ the drawbacks.
drill.vi: Lợi ích lớn hơn bất lợi.

drill.t: The main advantage is ___ costs are shared.
drill.vi: Lợi ích chính là chi phí được chia sẻ.

drill.t: ___ benefit is emotional support.
drill.vi: Một lợi ích khác là sự hỗ trợ tinh thần.

drill.t: This also has some ___.
drill.vi: Điều này cũng có vài hạn chế.

lines.t: Who should look after elderly people: families or the state?
lines.vi: Ai nên chăm sóc người già: gia đình hay nhà nước?

lines.t: Ideally both. In my culture filial duty is very strong, so families do most of the caring. But when someone needs professional nursing, families can’t do it alone, and the state should help.
lines.vi: Lý tưởng là cả hai. Trong văn hoá của tôi đạo hiếu rất mạnh nên gia đình chăm sóc là chính. Nhưng khi ai đó cần điều dưỡng chuyên nghiệp, gia đình không tự làm được, và nhà nước nên hỗ trợ.

lines.t: What can young people learn from older people?
lines.vi: Người trẻ học được gì từ người già?

lines.t: Patience, mainly, and a sense of perspective. My grandmother lived through a war, so when I complain about small problems at work, she reminds me what real difficulty looks like.
lines.vi: Chủ yếu là sự kiên nhẫn và cách nhìn nhận. Bà tôi đã sống qua chiến tranh, nên khi tôi than vãn chuyện nhỏ ở chỗ làm, bà nhắc tôi khó khăn thật sự là thế nào.

lines.t: Why are people having fewer children?
lines.vi: Vì sao người ta sinh ít con hơn?

lines.t: Mainly cost. Housing, education and childcare are so expensive that many couples feel they can only afford one child. Women also have more career opportunities now, so they tend to have children later.
lines.vi: Chủ yếu là chi phí. Nhà ở, giáo dục và trông trẻ đắt đến mức nhiều cặp vợ chồng thấy chỉ nuôi nổi một con. Phụ nữ giờ cũng có nhiều cơ hội nghề nghiệp hơn nên thường sinh con muộn hơn.

gram2.title: Gerunds as subjects and after prepositions
gram2.rule: Living with grandparents is … · instead of / without / by / after + -ing · be used to + -ing
gram2.note: An -ing form can be the subject of a sentence: Caring for elderly parents is demanding. After every preposition, use -ing, not to + verb: instead of moving, by working, without asking. Be used to + -ing means “be familiar with”, which is different from used to + verb (past habit).

ex.t: Caring for an elderly parent can be exhausting.
ex.vi: Chăm sóc cha mẹ già có thể rất mệt mỏi.

ex.t: Many couples delay having children.
ex.vi: Nhiều cặp vợ chồng trì hoãn việc sinh con.

ex.t: Instead of retiring, she started a business.
ex.vi: Thay vì nghỉ hưu, bà ấy mở một công việc kinh doanh.

ex.t: I’m used to living with a big family.
ex.vi: Tôi đã quen sống trong gia đình đông người.

drill.vi: Anh ấy tiết kiệm tiền bằng cách sống với bố mẹ.

drill.t: She is used to ___ early.

cue.card: Describe an older person you enjoy spending time with.
points: and explain why you enjoy spending time with them
model: I’d like to talk about Mr Tuan, who lives in the flat next to mine. He’s a retired history teacher in his late seventies, and I got to know him about four years ago when I helped him carry some shopping upstairs.

Since then we’ve developed a kind of routine. Every Sunday morning I join him for tea on his balcony, and we play a game of Chinese chess, which he almost always wins. Sometimes I help him with his phone — he’s very keen to video-call his grandchildren in Germany — and in return he tells me about the history of our neighbourhood, like which buildings were here before the war.

I enjoy his company because he’s curious about everything and he never lectures me, even though he was a teacher for forty years. There’s obviously a generation gap — he thinks my generation spends too much time on screens — but we laugh about it. I also think it matters to him: his wife passed away a few years ago, and I know loneliness can be a real problem for older people living alone.

write.prompt: In many countries, more and more older people are living alone rather than with their families. Do the advantages of this trend outweigh the disadvantages?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase + answer (disadvantages outweigh, mainly because of loneliness and safety)
Body 1: advantages — independence, privacy, fewer family conflicts
Body 2: disadvantages — loneliness, health emergencies, cost of care
Conclusion: restate the answer and suggest a middle way (living nearby)
model: In many parts of the world, an increasing number of elderly people now live on their own instead of with their children. Although this arrangement offers some benefits, I believe its drawbacks, particularly loneliness and the risks to health, are more significant.

Living alone certainly has advantages. Many older people value their independence and prefer to organise their days in their own way, without having to adapt to the routines of a busy household. It also gives both generations more privacy, which can reduce the tension that sometimes arises when parents and adult children share a home. For those who are healthy and have an active social life, living independently can help them stay confident and mentally alert.

However, these benefits are outweighed by serious disadvantages. The most obvious is loneliness: older people who live alone may go for days without a proper conversation, and research has linked social isolation to depression and memory problems. Safety is another concern. If an elderly person falls or becomes ill at night, there may be nobody there to call for help. Finally, when they eventually need daily assistance, paying for professional care can be extremely expensive for families and governments.

In conclusion, while living alone allows older people to remain independent, the risks of isolation and unattended health emergencies are, in my view, greater. A sensible compromise may be for elderly parents to live close to their children, so that they can keep their independence while still receiving regular support.

units.title: Waste, energy & recycling
units.goal: Talk about environmental habits and policies, and compare two sets of data.

lines.t: Do you recycle at home?
lines.vi: Bạn có tái chế ở nhà không?

lines.t: We try to. We separate plastic bottles and paper, and my mother composts vegetable waste for her plants. But honestly, I’m not sure everything we separate actually gets recycled.
lines.vi: Chúng tôi cố gắng. Chúng tôi tách chai nhựa và giấy, mẹ tôi ủ rau thừa làm phân bón cây. Nhưng thật lòng, tôi không chắc mọi thứ đã tách có thật sự được tái chế.

lines.t: Do you try to save energy?
lines.vi: Bạn có cố tiết kiệm năng lượng không?

lines.t: Yes, mostly to save money. I switch off the air conditioner when I leave a room, and we’ve replaced all our bulbs with energy-efficient ones.
lines.vi: Có, chủ yếu để tiết kiệm tiền. Tôi tắt điều hoà khi ra khỏi phòng, và chúng tôi đã thay toàn bộ bóng đèn bằng loại tiết kiệm năng lượng.

lines.t: Do you use a lot of plastic?
lines.vi: Bạn có dùng nhiều đồ nhựa không?

lines.t: More than I’d like. I carry a reusable bottle, but takeaway food comes with so much single-use packaging that it’s hard to avoid.
lines.vi: Nhiều hơn tôi muốn. Tôi mang bình nước dùng lại, nhưng đồ ăn mang về đi kèm quá nhiều bao bì dùng một lần nên khó tránh.

sents.t: The price of solar panels fell by around 90 per cent between 2010 and 2020.
sents.vi: Giá pin mặt trời giảm khoảng 90% từ năm 2010 đến 2020.

sents.t: In many sunny countries, solar is now the cheapest way to generate new electricity.
sents.vi: Ở nhiều nước nhiều nắng, điện mặt trời hiện là cách rẻ nhất để sản xuất điện mới.

sents.t: Vietnam installed more than 16,000 megawatts of solar capacity in just three years.
sents.vi: Việt Nam đã lắp đặt hơn 16.000 MW công suất điện mặt trời chỉ trong ba năm.

sents.t: However, the power grid was not ready, so some of this electricity could not be used.
sents.vi: Tuy nhiên, lưới điện chưa sẵn sàng nên một phần điện này không được sử dụng.

sents.t: Experts say that storage and grid investment are now as important as building new panels.
sents.vi: Chuyên gia nói đầu tư lưu trữ và lưới điện giờ quan trọng ngang xây thêm pin.

q.q: Solar panels became much cheaper between 2010 and 2020.
All of the electricity from Vietnam’s new solar farms was used.
Vietnam now produces more solar power than wind power.

gram.title: Giving and comparing figures
gram.rule: respectively · compared with · while / whereas · followed by · the figure for X · approximately / roughly / nearly
gram.note: When two data sets appear together, compare them in the same sentence instead of listing them one by one. Respectively matches figures to items in order: Germany and Spain recycled 60% and 40% respectively. Use approximately or nearly for rounded numbers, and the figure for … to avoid repeating nouns.

ex.t: Germany and Italy recycled 67% and 50% respectively.
ex.vi: Đức và Ý tái chế lần lượt 67% và 50%.

ex.t: The figure for France was slightly lower.
ex.vi: Con số của Pháp thấp hơn một chút.

ex.t: Coal was the main source, followed by gas.
ex.vi: Than là nguồn chính, sau đó là khí đốt.

ex.t: Nearly a third of waste went to landfill.
ex.vi: Gần một phần ba rác được đưa đến bãi chôn lấp.

drill.t: The UK and Spain produced 30 and 20 tonnes ___.
drill.vi: Anh và Tây Ban Nha lần lượt sản xuất 30 và 20 tấn.

drill.t: ___ for nuclear power was 10%.

drill.t: Wind was the largest source, ___ by solar.
drill.vi: Gió là nguồn lớn nhất, tiếp theo là mặt trời.

drill.t: Recycling rose to ___ 45%.

lines.t: Who is more responsible for protecting the environment: individuals or governments?
lines.vi: Ai có trách nhiệm bảo vệ môi trường nhiều hơn: cá nhân hay chính phủ?

lines.t: Governments and large companies, in my opinion, because their decisions have a much bigger impact. One power station can produce more emissions than a whole city of people trying to save energy. But individual choices still send a message.
lines.vi: Theo tôi là chính phủ và các công ty lớn, vì quyết định của họ tác động lớn hơn nhiều. Một nhà máy điện có thể thải nhiều hơn cả một thành phố người dân cố tiết kiệm điện. Nhưng lựa chọn cá nhân vẫn tạo ra thông điệp.

lines.t: How can people be encouraged to recycle more?
lines.vi: Làm sao khuyến khích mọi người tái chế nhiều hơn?

lines.t: Make it easy and give incentives. In some countries you get money back when you return bottles, and recycling rates there are above ninety per cent. If people have to travel far to dispose of rubbish properly, they simply won’t.
lines.vi: Làm cho nó dễ dàng và có biện pháp khuyến khích. Ở một số nước, trả lại chai sẽ được hoàn tiền, và tỉ lệ tái chế ở đó trên chín mươi phần trăm. Nếu phải đi xa mới xử lý rác đúng cách, người ta sẽ không làm.

lines.t: Should fossil fuels be phased out completely?
lines.vi: Có nên loại bỏ hoàn toàn nhiên liệu hoá thạch không?

lines.t: Eventually, yes, but it has to be gradual. Developing countries still need cheap and reliable electricity, so rich countries should help them pay for renewable energy rather than just telling them to stop using coal.
lines.vi: Cuối cùng thì có, nhưng phải từ từ. Các nước đang phát triển vẫn cần điện rẻ và ổn định, nên nước giàu nên giúp họ chi trả cho năng lượng tái tạo thay vì chỉ bảo họ ngừng dùng than.

gram2.title: Making suggestions and recommendations
gram2.rule: should / ought to · It is essential that … · One way to … would be to … · suggest + -ing / suggest that + subject + verb
gram2.note: In Speaking and Writing, recommendations sound more natural when they are specific. After suggest, use -ing or a that-clause, never “suggest to do”: I suggest charging for plastic bags. It is essential / vital that + subject + base verb is formal and strong: It is essential that every city provide recycling bins.

ex.t: The government should invest in solar power.

ex.t: One way to reduce waste would be to charge for bags.
ex.vi: Một cách giảm rác là thu phí túi nilon.

ex.t: I suggest using public transport twice a week.
ex.vi: Tôi đề nghị đi phương tiện công cộng hai lần một tuần.

ex.t: It is essential that companies reduce packaging.
ex.vi: Điều thiết yếu là các công ty giảm bao bì.
