cue.card: Describe something you do to help protect the environment.
points: how difficult or easy it is
and explain why you do it
model: One thing I do is avoid single-use plastic as much as I can, especially bags and drinking straws. I started about three years ago, after watching a documentary that showed how much plastic washes up on beaches in central Vietnam.

In practice, it means carrying a small kit with me: a cloth bag, a metal straw and a reusable water bottle. When I order coffee, I ask them to pour it into my bottle, and at the market I put vegetables straight into my bag. I also buy shampoo and washing-up liquid from a refill shop near my office.

Some parts are easy now that it’s become a habit, but takeaway food is still difficult, because almost every restaurant packs meals in plastic boxes. I do it partly because I genuinely don’t want to add to the landfill problem, and partly because I think small actions spread. Two of my colleagues started bringing their own bottles after seeing mine, so even if one person’s impact is small, it isn’t zero.

write.prompt: The table below shows how household waste was dealt with in four countries in 2022. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
write.data:
Country     Recycled   Composted   Burned for energy   Landfill
Germany     48%        19%         32%                 1%
UK          28%        16%         45%                11%
Italy       33%        20%         21%                26%
Greece      15%         6%          2%                77%
plan: Introduction: paraphrase (dealt with → disposed of / methods of managing)
Overview: Germany relied least on landfill and recycled most; Greece sent most waste to landfill
Body 1: Germany and the UK — recycling vs burning for energy
Body 2: Italy and Greece — more landfill, much less burning
model: The table compares the methods that four European countries used to manage their household waste in 2022.

Overall, Germany had the most environmentally friendly system, recycling the highest share of its waste and sending almost none to landfill. Greece, by contrast, relied overwhelmingly on landfill and recycled the least.

Nearly half of Germany’s household waste (48%) was recycled and a further 19% was composted, while most of the remainder was burned to generate energy. Only 1% ended up in landfill. The UK also landfilled relatively little (11%), but it burned far more waste than any other country, at 45%, and recycled 28%.

Italy’s figures were more evenly distributed: it recycled a third of its waste and composted a fifth, but just over a quarter still went to landfill. Greece was very different from the other three countries. More than three quarters of its waste (77%) was buried in landfill, whereas recycling and composting accounted for only 15% and 6% respectively, and almost none was used for energy.

units.title: Friendship & social life
units.goal: Discuss friendship, making friends as an adult and online versus face-to-face relationships, using defining relative clauses.

words.ex: I have three close friends from university.
words.exVi: Tôi có ba người bạn thân từ đại học.

words.ex: He’s more of an acquaintance than a friend.
words.exVi: Anh ấy là người quen hơn là bạn.

words.ex: It’s harder to make friends as an adult.
words.exVi: Kết bạn khi trưởng thành khó hơn.

words.ex: We drifted apart after school.
words.exVi: Chúng tôi dần xa nhau sau khi ra trường.

words.ex: We keep in contact through messages.
words.exVi: Chúng tôi giữ liên lạc qua tin nhắn.

words.ex: He’s very sociable and makes friends easily.
words.exVi: Anh ấy rất hoà đồng và dễ kết bạn.

words.ex: She’s very outgoing and loves parties.
words.exVi: Cô ấy rất hướng ngoại và thích tiệc tùng.

words.ex: As an introvert, I prefer small groups.
words.exVi: Là người hướng nội, tôi thích nhóm nhỏ.

words.ex: I met like-minded people at a hiking club.
words.exVi: Tôi gặp những người cùng chí hướng ở câu lạc bộ leo núi.

words.ex: Friendships often start with a common interest.
words.exVi: Tình bạn thường bắt đầu từ sở thích chung.

words.ex: Face-to-face conversations feel more real.
words.exVi: Trò chuyện trực tiếp cảm thấy thật hơn.

words.ex: I’ve never met some of my online friends.
words.exVi: Tôi chưa từng gặp vài người bạn qua mạng.

words.ex: Social isolation is common among the elderly.
words.exVi: Sự cô lập xã hội phổ biến ở người già.

words.ex: I’m still close to two classmates from school.
words.exVi: Tôi vẫn thân với hai bạn cùng lớp thời đi học.

words.ex: I can always count on my best friend.
words.exVi: Tôi luôn có thể trông cậy vào bạn thân.

words.ex: Let’s meet for coffee and catch up.
words.exVi: Gặp nhau uống cà phê hàn huyên nhé.

words.ex: They have been lifelong friends.
words.exVi: Họ là bạn suốt đời.

words.ex: A genuine friend tells you the truth.
words.exVi: Một người bạn thật lòng sẽ nói thật với bạn.

words.ex: I fell out with my roommate over money.
words.exVi: Tôi giận bạn cùng phòng vì tiền.

words.ex: My social circle got smaller after I moved.
words.exVi: Vòng bạn bè của tôi thu hẹp sau khi chuyển đi.

lines.t: Do you have many friends?
lines.vi: Bạn có nhiều bạn không?

lines.t: Not many close friends, maybe four or five, but I have lots of acquaintances through work. I think a few genuine friends are more valuable than many casual ones.
lines.vi: Không nhiều bạn thân, khoảng bốn năm người, nhưng tôi có nhiều người quen qua công việc. Tôi nghĩ vài người bạn thật lòng giá trị hơn nhiều người quen sơ.

lines.t: How often do you meet your friends?
lines.vi: Bạn gặp bạn bè bao lâu một lần?

lines.t: Less often than I’d like. We’re all busy with work and family, so we usually catch up once a month over dinner, but we chat online almost every day.
lines.vi: Ít hơn tôi muốn. Ai cũng bận công việc và gia đình nên thường mỗi tháng gặp một lần ăn tối, nhưng ngày nào cũng nói chuyện online.

lines.t: Is it easy to make new friends where you live?
lines.vi: Ở nơi bạn sống có dễ kết bạn mới không?

lines.t: Not really. In a big city like Ho Chi Minh City, people are friendly but busy. I made most of my recent friends through a running club, where people share a common interest.
lines.vi: Không hẳn. Ở thành phố lớn như TP.HCM, người ta thân thiện nhưng bận. Phần lớn bạn mới gần đây tôi quen qua câu lạc bộ chạy bộ, nơi mọi người có chung sở thích.

sents.t: Surveys in several countries suggest that adults have fewer close friends than they did thirty years ago.
sents.vi: Khảo sát ở nhiều nước cho thấy người trưởng thành có ít bạn thân hơn ba mươi năm trước.

sents.t: One reason is that people move more often for work, which makes it harder to keep in contact.
sents.vi: Một lý do là người ta chuyển nơi ở thường xuyên hơn vì công việc, khiến khó giữ liên lạc.

sents.t: Long working hours also leave less time to socialise.
sents.vi: Giờ làm việc dài cũng khiến ít thời gian giao lưu hơn.

sents.t: Although social media helps people stay connected, researchers say it cannot fully replace face-to-face contact.
sents.vi: Dù mạng xã hội giúp mọi người kết nối, các nhà nghiên cứu nói nó không thể thay thế hoàn toàn gặp gỡ trực tiếp.

sents.t: Loneliness has been linked to poorer health, which is why some governments now treat it as a public health issue.
sents.vi: Cô đơn có liên quan đến sức khoẻ kém hơn, vì thế một số chính phủ giờ coi đó là vấn đề sức khoẻ cộng đồng.

q.q: Adults today have more close friends than thirty years ago.
Moving for work can make friendships harder to maintain.
Most governments have a minister for loneliness.

gram.title: Defining relative clauses
gram.rule: who / that (people) · which / that (things) · where (places) · whose (possession)
gram.note: Defining relative clauses identify which person or thing you mean, with no commas: A friend who listens is valuable. I joined a club where people share my interests. You can drop who/which/that when it is the object: The friend (that) I trust most lives abroad.

ex.t: A real friend is someone who tells you the truth.
ex.vi: Bạn thật là người nói thật với bạn.

ex.t: I joined a club where I met like-minded people.
ex.vi: Tôi tham gia một câu lạc bộ nơi gặp những người cùng chí hướng.

ex.t: The app that I use most is a messaging app.
ex.vi: Ứng dụng tôi dùng nhiều nhất là ứng dụng nhắn tin.

ex.t: She’s the friend whose advice I always follow.
ex.vi: Cô ấy là người bạn mà tôi luôn nghe theo lời khuyên.

drill.t: A friend ___ you can rely on is rare.
drill.vi: Một người bạn mà bạn có thể dựa vào thật hiếm.

drill.t: That’s the café ___ we first met.
drill.vi: Đó là quán cà phê nơi chúng tôi gặp lần đầu.

drill.t: He’s the man ___ son is my classmate.
drill.vi: Ông ấy là người có con trai học cùng lớp tôi.

drill.t: The book ___ she recommended was great.
drill.vi: Cuốn sách cô ấy giới thiệu rất hay.

lines.t: Can online friends be as close as real-life friends?
lines.vi: Bạn qua mạng có thể thân như bạn ngoài đời không?

lines.t: In some cases, yes. People who share a passion can support each other online for years. But I think there are limits — an online friend can’t visit you in hospital or help you move house, so most deep friendships still need some face-to-face contact.
lines.vi: Trong vài trường hợp thì có. Những người chung đam mê có thể ủng hộ nhau online nhiều năm. Nhưng tôi nghĩ có giới hạn — bạn online không thể vào viện thăm bạn hay giúp bạn chuyển nhà, nên phần lớn tình bạn sâu sắc vẫn cần gặp trực tiếp.

lines.t: Why do friends sometimes drift apart?
lines.vi: Vì sao bạn bè đôi khi dần xa nhau?

lines.t: Usually it’s not because of an argument but because their lives change. One person gets married, another moves abroad, and gradually they have less in common.
lines.vi: Thường không phải do cãi nhau mà do cuộc sống thay đổi. Một người lập gia đình, người kia ra nước ngoài, và dần dần họ ít điểm chung hơn.

lines.t: Who has more influence on teenagers: parents or friends?
lines.vi: Ai ảnh hưởng đến thanh thiếu niên nhiều hơn: bố mẹ hay bạn bè?

lines.t: I’d say peers, at least in everyday matters like fashion, music and how they spend their free time. Parents still influence their values, but teenagers care a lot about being accepted by their friends.
lines.vi: Tôi cho là bạn bè đồng trang lứa, ít nhất trong chuyện hằng ngày như thời trang, âm nhạc và cách dùng thời gian rảnh. Bố mẹ vẫn ảnh hưởng đến giá trị sống, nhưng thanh thiếu niên rất quan tâm được bạn bè chấp nhận.

gram2.title: Hedging opinions: I’d say… / In some cases… / To some extent…
gram2.rule: I’d say … · In some cases … · To some extent … · It’s not always the case that …
gram2.note: Band 6+ answers avoid sounding too absolute. Use hedging phrases to show nuance: I’d say peers have more influence. To some extent, social media helps. It’s not always the case that online friends are less important.

ex.t: I’d say most people have fewer close friends now.
ex.vi: Tôi cho rằng giờ phần lớn người ta có ít bạn thân hơn.

ex.t: To some extent, technology brings people together.
ex.vi: Ở một mức độ nào đó, công nghệ kết nối mọi người.

ex.t: In some cases, online friends are very supportive.
ex.vi: Trong vài trường hợp, bạn online rất hỗ trợ.

ex.t: It’s not always the case that introverts are lonely.
ex.vi: Không phải lúc nào người hướng nội cũng cô đơn.

drill.t: To some ___, social media helps us stay in touch.
drill.vi: Ở một mức độ nào đó, mạng xã hội giúp ta giữ liên lạc.

drill.t: I’d ___ that friends matter more than money.
drill.vi: Tôi cho rằng bạn bè quan trọng hơn tiền.

drill.t: In some ___, people prefer online friends.
drill.vi: Trong vài trường hợp, người ta thích bạn online hơn.

drill.t: It’s not always the ___ that outgoing people have more friends.
drill.vi: Không phải lúc nào người hướng ngoại cũng nhiều bạn hơn.

cue.card: Describe a friend you have known for a long time.
points: and explain why your friendship has lasted
model: I’d like to talk about Linh, who has been my closest friend for almost twenty years.

We met on the first day of secondary school, when the teacher put us at the same desk. I was very shy at the time, and she was the opposite — outgoing and talkative — so at first I found her a bit overwhelming. But she kept sharing her snacks with me and helping me with maths, and by the end of the first term we were inseparable.

These days we live in different cities, so we don’t see each other as often as we’d like. When we do meet, usually at Tết or during summer holidays, we tend to do simple things: we go for long walks around the lake in our hometown, eat street food and talk for hours. In between, we send each other voice messages almost every day.

I think our friendship has lasted because it’s genuine and low-pressure. We’ve both changed a lot, but we’ve never stopped being honest with each other, even when it was uncomfortable. When my father was ill, she drove four hours just to sit with me in the hospital. Friends like that are rare, and I think we both realise how lucky we are.

write.prompt: Some people think that social media has made people more connected, while others believe it has made people more isolated. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
plan: Introduction: paraphrase both views; opinion — connected in breadth, but risk of isolation in depth
Body 1: more connected — distance, communities, support
Body 2: more isolated — replacing face-to-face, comparison, shallow contact
Conclusion: depends on how it is used; complement not substitute
model: Social media has transformed the way people communicate. While some argue that it has brought people closer together, others claim that it has actually left many people more isolated. In my view, social media increases the number of connections people have, but it can weaken the quality of relationships if it replaces real-life contact.

Those who believe social media connects people have strong arguments. It allows families separated by distance to share daily life through photos and video calls, which was impossible a generation ago. It also helps people with unusual interests or difficulties, such as a rare illness, to find communities of like-minded people who can offer support. For shy people, starting a conversation online can be easier than doing so face-to-face.

On the other hand, there is evidence that heavy social media use can increase feelings of loneliness. When people spend hours scrolling instead of meeting friends, their relationships may become shallow, consisting mainly of likes and brief comments. In addition, constantly seeing the edited highlights of other people’s lives can make users feel that everyone else is happier and more successful, which may lead them to withdraw further.

In conclusion, social media is neither purely good nor purely bad for human connection. I believe it is beneficial when it is used to support and arrange real-life relationships, but harmful when it becomes a substitute for them. The challenge for individuals is to use it as a bridge rather than a wall.

units.title: Online shopping & delivery
units.goal: Talk about online shopping habits, delivery and consumer problems, using the passive voice and contrast linkers.

words.ex: E-commerce has grown rapidly in Vietnam.
words.exVi: Thương mại điện tử tăng trưởng nhanh ở Việt Nam.

words.ex: I sold my old bike on an online marketplace.
words.exVi: Tôi bán chiếc xe đạp cũ trên sàn online.

words.ex: I bought a fan in a flash sale.
words.exVi: Tôi mua chiếc quạt trong đợt flash sale.

words.ex: Free shipping encourages people to buy more.
words.exVi: Miễn phí vận chuyển khuyến khích người ta mua nhiều hơn.

words.ex: I always read customer reviews first.
words.exVi: Tôi luôn đọc đánh giá của khách trước.

words.ex: The shoes turned out to be counterfeit.
words.exVi: Đôi giày hoá ra là hàng giả.

words.ex: You can return it within seven days.
words.exVi: Bạn có thể trả hàng trong bảy ngày.

words.ex: You can track your parcel in the app.
words.exVi: Bạn có thể theo dõi bưu kiện trong ứng dụng.

words.ex: The courier left the parcel with the guard.
words.exVi: Người giao hàng để bưu kiện ở chỗ bảo vệ.

words.ex: There is too much plastic packaging.
words.exVi: Có quá nhiều bao bì nhựa.

words.ex: My sister is a real bargain hunter.
words.exVi: Chị tôi đúng là người săn hàng giảm giá.

words.ex: People love the convenience of online shopping.
words.exVi: Người ta thích sự tiện lợi của mua sắm online.

words.ex: In-store prices are sometimes higher.
words.exVi: Giá tại cửa hàng đôi khi cao hơn.

words.ex: Live-stream selling is very popular now.
words.exVi: Bán hàng qua livestream giờ rất phổ biến.

words.ex: The online seller replied within minutes.
words.exVi: Người bán online trả lời trong vài phút.

words.ex: The product photo looked much better than the real thing.
words.exVi: Ảnh sản phẩm trông đẹp hơn nhiều so với hàng thật.

words.ex: The delivery fee was more than the item.
words.exVi: Phí giao hàng còn đắt hơn món hàng.

words.ex: Online shopping hurts local shops.

words.ex: Apps make it easy to compare prices.
words.exVi: Ứng dụng giúp dễ so sánh giá.

words.ex: Be careful of scams on social media.
words.exVi: Cẩn thận lừa đảo trên mạng xã hội.

lines.t: Do you often shop online?
lines.vi: Bạn có hay mua sắm online không?

lines.t: Yes, probably two or three times a week. Mostly small things like household products, books and phone accessories, because it saves me a lot of time.
lines.vi: Có, khoảng hai ba lần một tuần. Chủ yếu là đồ nhỏ như đồ gia dụng, sách và phụ kiện điện thoại, vì nó tiết kiệm cho tôi nhiều thời gian.

lines.t: What do you prefer to buy in shops?
lines.vi: Bạn thích mua gì ở cửa hàng hơn?

lines.t: Clothes and shoes, definitely. I need to try them on, and the photos online are often misleading — the colour or the size is different when it arrives.
lines.vi: Chắc chắn là quần áo và giày. Tôi cần thử, và ảnh online thường gây hiểu lầm — màu hay cỡ khác khi hàng tới.

lines.t: Have you ever had a problem with an online order?
lines.vi: Bạn đã bao giờ gặp vấn đề với đơn hàng online chưa?

lines.t: Yes, once I ordered a pair of branded trainers and they turned out to be counterfeit. Luckily, the platform gave me a full refund after I sent photos.
lines.vi: Có, có lần tôi đặt một đôi giày thể thao hàng hiệu và hoá ra là hàng giả. May là nền tảng hoàn tiền đầy đủ sau khi tôi gửi ảnh.

sents.t: Online shopping in Southeast Asia has grown faster than almost anywhere else in the world.
sents.vi: Mua sắm online ở Đông Nam Á tăng trưởng nhanh hơn hầu hết mọi nơi trên thế giới.

sents.t: Huge discount days are now promoted by every major platform.
sents.vi: Những ngày giảm giá lớn giờ được mọi nền tảng lớn quảng bá.

sents.t: However, the rise in deliveries has led to more traffic and much more plastic packaging.
sents.vi: Tuy nhiên, sự gia tăng giao hàng dẫn đến nhiều phương tiện hơn và nhiều bao bì nhựa hơn.

sents.t: Many small local shops say they have lost customers to e-commerce.
sents.vi: Nhiều cửa hàng nhỏ địa phương nói họ mất khách vào thương mại điện tử.

sents.t: Some platforms have started offering paper packaging and rewards for customers who choose slower, combined deliveries.
sents.vi: Một số nền tảng bắt đầu dùng bao bì giấy và thưởng cho khách chọn giao gộp, chậm hơn.

q.q: Online shopping in Southeast Asia has grown quickly.
Deliveries have reduced traffic in cities.
All platforms now use only paper packaging.

gram.title: The passive voice (present and past)
gram.rule: is / are + past participle · was / were + past participle · by + agent
gram.note: Use the passive when the action is more important than who does it, which is common in Part 3 and Writing: Millions of parcels are delivered every day. The shoes were made in a factory. Add by + agent only when it is useful.

ex.t: Most orders are delivered within two days.
ex.vi: Hầu hết đơn hàng được giao trong hai ngày.

ex.t: The parcel was left with the security guard.
ex.vi: Bưu kiện được để ở chỗ bảo vệ.

ex.t: A lot of packaging is thrown away.
ex.vi: Rất nhiều bao bì bị vứt đi.

ex.t: Fake products are sometimes sold online.
ex.vi: Hàng giả đôi khi được bán trên mạng.

drill.t: Millions of parcels ___ every day.
drill.vi: Hàng triệu bưu kiện được giao mỗi ngày.

drill.t: My order ___ yesterday.
drill.vi: Đơn hàng của tôi bị huỷ hôm qua.

drill.t: These phones ___ in Vietnam.
drill.vi: Những chiếc điện thoại này được sản xuất ở Việt Nam.

drill.t: The refund ___ to my account last week.
drill.vi: Tiền hoàn được gửi vào tài khoản tôi tuần trước.

lines.t: Will online shopping replace traditional shops?
lines.vi: Mua sắm online có thay thế cửa hàng truyền thống không?

lines.t: I don’t think it will replace them completely. Shops will probably become more like places for experiences — trying products, getting advice, meeting people. But many small shops that only sell basic goods will struggle.
lines.vi: Tôi không nghĩ sẽ thay thế hoàn toàn. Cửa hàng có lẽ sẽ trở thành nơi trải nghiệm — thử sản phẩm, được tư vấn, gặp gỡ. Nhưng nhiều cửa hàng nhỏ chỉ bán hàng cơ bản sẽ gặp khó.

lines.t: Why do people buy things they don’t need online?
lines.vi: Vì sao người ta mua những thứ không cần trên mạng?

lines.t: Platforms are designed to encourage impulse buys. Countdown timers, flash sales and “only two left” messages create pressure, and paying with one click doesn’t feel like spending real money.
lines.vi: Các nền tảng được thiết kế để khuyến khích mua bốc đồng. Đồng hồ đếm ngược, flash sale và thông báo “chỉ còn hai sản phẩm” tạo áp lực, và thanh toán một chạm không có cảm giác như tiêu tiền thật.

lines.t: How can consumers protect themselves?
lines.vi: Người tiêu dùng có thể tự bảo vệ thế nào?

lines.t: By reading reviews carefully, buying from official stores and comparing prices. Also, if a deal looks too good to be true, it probably is a scam.
lines.vi: Bằng cách đọc kỹ đánh giá, mua từ cửa hàng chính hãng và so sánh giá. Ngoài ra, nếu ưu đãi trông quá tốt để là thật thì có lẽ là lừa đảo.

gram2.title: Contrast linkers: although, while, whereas, however
gram2.rule: although / while + clause, … · A, whereas B · … . However, …
gram2.note: Use although or while at the start of a clause to show contrast: Although online shopping is convenient, it creates waste. Whereas compares two different facts: Online prices are lower, whereas shops offer advice. However starts a new sentence.

ex.t: Although it’s convenient, online shopping creates waste.
ex.vi: Dù tiện lợi, mua sắm online tạo ra rác.

ex.t: Online stores are open 24/7, whereas local shops close at night.
ex.vi: Cửa hàng online mở 24/7, trong khi cửa hàng địa phương đóng cửa ban đêm.

ex.t: While I buy books online, I prefer to buy clothes in shops.
ex.vi: Trong khi tôi mua sách online, tôi thích mua quần áo ở cửa hàng hơn.

ex.t: Prices are lower online. However, delivery can be slow.
ex.vi: Giá online thấp hơn. Tuy nhiên, giao hàng có thể chậm.

drill.vi: Dù giá rẻ nhưng chất lượng kém.

drill.t: I shop online, ___ my parents prefer markets.
drill.vi: Tôi mua sắm online, trong khi bố mẹ tôi thích đi chợ.

drill.t: It’s cheap. ___, it took two weeks to arrive.

cue.card: Describe something you bought online that you were happy with.
points: and explain why you were happy with it
model: I’d like to talk about a second-hand standing desk that I bought online about a year ago.
I found it on a local marketplace group on Facebook. A woman who was moving abroad was selling most of her furniture, and the desk was listed at less than half the price of a new one.

I bought it online mainly because of the price, but also because standing desks are hard to find in ordinary furniture shops in my city. Before paying, I asked the seller for a short video showing the motor working, and I checked her profile and the comments from other buyers, because I wanted to avoid scams.

I was really happy with it for a few reasons. It arrived the next day, in perfect condition, and the seller even included the original manual. More importantly, it has changed my working habits. I work from home three days a week, and alternating between sitting and standing has reduced my back pain significantly. It also felt good to give a piece of furniture a second life instead of buying something new.

write.prompt: Online shopping is replacing shopping in stores. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase; position — advantages for consumers, but disadvantages for communities and environment are significant; overall slightly positive with regulation
Body 1: advantages — convenience, price, choice, rural access
Body 2: disadvantages — local shops, packaging and traffic, fraud
Conclusion: benefits outweigh if managed
model: In many countries, online shopping is steadily replacing traditional shopping in stores. Although this trend causes some serious problems, I believe that its advantages outweigh the disadvantages, provided that governments and companies address its negative effects.

The main advantages are convenience, price and choice. Consumers can buy almost anything at any time without travelling, which saves time and is particularly helpful for busy workers, elderly people and those with disabilities. Online competition also tends to reduce prices, and comparison tools allow shoppers to find the best deal in seconds. Furthermore, people in rural areas now have access to the same products as city residents, which was impossible when shopping depended on physical stores.

However, this development also has clear drawbacks. Small local shops are losing customers, which can damage the character of neighbourhoods and reduce local employment. The huge increase in deliveries creates traffic and enormous amounts of packaging waste. In addition, online markets are vulnerable to counterfeit goods and scams, and many consumers make impulse purchases because platforms are designed to encourage them.

In conclusion, while online shopping harms some local businesses and the environment, its benefits for consumers are substantial. I believe these advantages outweigh the disadvantages, as long as regulations reduce packaging, protect consumers from fraud and support local shops in moving online themselves.

cue.card: Describe a time when you were very busy.
points: and explain how you felt about it
model: I’d like to talk about a period last December, which was probably the busiest month of my working life so far.

I work for a small design company, and at the end of the year three of our biggest clients all wanted their projects finished before Tết. On top of that, one of my colleagues was on maternity leave, so my workload almost doubled. For about four weeks, I was working twelve-hour days and replying to messages late at night.

At first I tried to do everything myself, which was a mistake — I started making careless errors and sleeping badly. So I sat down with my manager and we prioritised: we postponed one smaller project and hired a freelancer to help with the drawings. I also forced myself to take one full day off each week and to go running every morning, even for just twenty minutes, which really helped me stay calm.

Looking back, I feel proud that we delivered everything on time, but I also learned an important lesson. Being busy isn’t the same as being productive, and if I hadn’t set some boundaries, I would probably have burned out. Now I try to raise problems earlier instead of quietly working longer hours.

write.prompt: In many countries, people are working longer hours. What are the causes of this, and what effects does it have on individuals and society?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase; preview causes and effects
Body 1: causes — competition and job insecurity, technology, cost of living
Body 2: effects — health, family, productivity; society: lower birth rates, healthcare costs
Conclusion: summarise; brief recommendation
model: In many parts of the world, employees are spending more and more time at work. This essay will examine the main reasons for this trend and discuss its effects on both individuals and society as a whole.

There are several causes of longer working hours. Firstly, competition in the job market has increased, and many workers fear that leaving on time will make them look less committed than their colleagues, especially when jobs are insecure. Secondly, technology has blurred the boundary between work and home; with smartphones and messaging apps, employees are expected to be available in the evenings and at weekends. Finally, the rising cost of living, particularly housing, forces many people to work overtime or take side jobs simply to make ends meet.

These long hours have serious effects on individuals. Overwork is linked to stress, poor sleep and health problems such as heart disease, and it leaves little quality time for family and friends. Ironically, it can also reduce productivity, as tired employees make more mistakes. For society, the consequences are also significant. When parents have little time and energy, family life suffers, and in some countries long working hours are considered one reason for falling birth rates. In addition, the burden on healthcare systems grows as more people suffer from stress-related illnesses.

In conclusion, longer working hours are driven by competition, technology and economic pressure, and they harm both individual well-being and society. Governments and employers should consider measures such as limits on overtime and a legal right to disconnect, so that work supports people’s lives rather than taking them over.

lines.t: Are parents today more protective than in the past?

lines.t: Generally, yes. Families are smaller, so parents focus all their attention on one or two children, and cities feel less safe because of traffic. As a result, children have less freedom than their parents did.
lines.vi: Nhìn chung là có. Gia đình nhỏ hơn nên cha mẹ dồn hết sự chú ý vào một hai đứa con, và thành phố cảm giác kém an toàn vì giao thông. Kết quả là trẻ có ít tự do hơn thế hệ cha mẹ.

cue.card: Describe a rule your parents had when you were a child.
points: why your parents had this rule
and explain whether you think it was a good rule
model: I’d like to talk about a rule my parents had that we all had to eat dinner together at seven o’clock, with no phones or TV.

My parents both worked long hours — my father was a bus driver and my mother ran a small shop — so dinner was the only time of day the whole family was in the same place. They wanted to make sure that, however busy we were, we talked to each other at least once a day.

As a teenager, I found it annoying. My friends were chatting online in the evenings, and I felt I was missing out. Sometimes I invented excuses, like extra homework, to escape early, but my mother always saw through them.

Looking back, I think it was an excellent rule. Those dinners were where I learned about my parents’ lives, where we argued about the news and where my sister and I could raise problems before they became serious. I’m not a parent yet, but when I am, I’ll definitely keep the same rule — perhaps with a little more flexibility for teenagers.

write.prompt: Some people think that parents should give children a lot of freedom, while others believe children should follow strict rules. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
plan: Introduction: paraphrase; opinion — freedom within clear limits, increasing with age
Body 1: case for freedom — confidence, problem-solving, creativity
Body 2: case for strict rules — safety, discipline, habits
Conclusion: balance; age-appropriate
model: How much freedom children should have is a question that divides parents. Some argue that children develop best when they are free to make their own choices, while others believe that strict rules are essential. In my opinion, children need clear boundaries, but the freedom they are given should increase gradually as they grow older.

Those who support giving children freedom argue that it builds confidence and independence. When children are allowed to choose their hobbies, manage small amounts of money or travel short distances alone, they learn to solve problems and take responsibility for their decisions. Mistakes made in a safe environment are valuable lessons. In addition, too many rules may limit creativity and make children anxious or rebellious.

On the other hand, strict rules have important benefits. Young children cannot always judge risks, so rules about traffic, the internet and strangers protect them from real dangers. Consistent rules about homework, sleep and screen time also help children develop good habits and self-discipline, which are essential for success at school and later in life. Without such structure, some children may struggle to concentrate or to respect others.

In conclusion, both freedom and rules play a role in raising children. I believe the best approach is to set firm rules for young children, especially regarding safety, while explaining the reasons behind them, and then to give teenagers more freedom step by step. In this way, children can become responsible adults who are both disciplined and independent.

cue.card: Describe something you do to relax.
points: when and where you do it
how you learned to do it
and explain why it helps you relax
model: I’d like to talk about something quite simple: walking around West Lake in Hanoi in the early evening, without my phone.

I do it three or four times a week, usually around six o’clock, after work. The lake is about fifteen minutes from my flat, and the full loop takes me roughly an hour and a half. I leave my phone at home on purpose, which felt strange at first.

I started a couple of years ago, during a period when my job was very stressful and I was having restless nights. A friend who had been through burnout suggested walking without any screens, and I decided to try it for a month. It worked so well that it became a habit.

It helps me relax for several reasons. Physically, the exercise tires me out in a healthy way, so I sleep much better. Mentally, it gives my mind space: without notifications, I notice things — the sunset over the water, people fishing, the smell of street food — and my worries from the day slowly fade. It’s also free, which means there’s no pressure to “perform” as there is with a gym class. For me, it’s the easiest way to recharge.

write.prompt: Stress is now a major problem in many countries. What are the causes of stress, and what can be done to reduce it?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase; preview causes and solutions
Body 1: causes — work pressure, technology and constant connection, financial insecurity
Body 2: solutions — individual habits, employer policies, government and stigma
Conclusion: shared responsibility
model: Stress has become one of the most common health problems in modern society, affecting people of all ages. This essay will discuss the main causes of stress and suggest some measures that individuals, employers and governments can take to reduce it.

There are several reasons why stress levels have risen. Firstly, many people face intense pressure at work, including long hours, tight deadlines and job insecurity. Secondly, technology has made it difficult to switch off; smartphones mean that work emails and news follow people home, and social media encourages constant comparison with others. Finally, financial worries, particularly the rising cost of housing and education, place a heavy burden on many families.

Although stress cannot be eliminated entirely, there are effective ways to reduce it. Individuals can adopt healthier habits, such as regular exercise, sufficient sleep and limits on screen time, all of which are proven to improve mental well-being. Employers also have an important role: by setting realistic workloads, respecting employees’ time off and offering counselling services, they can create a healthier working environment. At a national level, governments can invest in mental health services and run campaigns to reduce the stigma that prevents many people from seeking help.

In conclusion, stress is caused by work pressure, technology and financial insecurity, and it requires action at several levels. If individuals, companies and governments all take responsibility, it is possible to create a society in which people are both productive and healthy.

lines.t: Are eating habits changing in your country?

lines.t: Definitely. Young people eat more fast food and sweet drinks than their parents did, and many families no longer eat dinner together because of work. On the positive side, people are more interested in healthy and organic food than before.
lines.vi: Chắc chắn. Người trẻ ăn đồ ăn nhanh và đồ ngọt nhiều hơn bố mẹ, và nhiều gia đình không còn ăn tối cùng nhau vì công việc. Mặt tích cực là người ta quan tâm đến đồ ăn lành mạnh và hữu cơ hơn trước.

lines.vi: Vì sao đồ ăn đường phố quan trọng với văn hoá một đất nước?

lines.t: Because it shows how ordinary people really live and eat. In Vietnam, street food is part of daily social life — people meet friends on tiny plastic stools, and recipes are passed down through families.
lines.vi: Vì nó cho thấy người bình thường thật sự sống và ăn thế nào. Ở Việt Nam, đồ ăn đường phố là một phần đời sống xã hội — người ta gặp bạn bè trên ghế nhựa nhỏ, và công thức được truyền qua các thế hệ.

gram2.title: Describing food precisely: adverb + adjective
gram2.rule: incredibly / slightly / a bit / rather + adjective · compound adjectives: mouth-watering, home-made
gram2.note: Avoid repeating “delicious”. Combine an adverb with a precise adjective: slightly sweet, incredibly fragrant, rather oily. Compound adjectives add colour: mouth-watering, home-made, freshly baked.

ex.vi: Bà ấy bán nem tự làm.

cue.card: Describe a restaurant or food stall you like.
points: what kind of food it serves
and explain why you like it
model: I’d like to describe a tiny bun cha stall in an alley near Hoan Kiem Lake, which I’ve been going to for about ten years.

It’s run by an elderly couple and their daughter, and it only opens at lunchtime. There’s no menu, because they serve just one thing: bun cha — grilled pork with rice noodles, fresh herbs and a slightly sweet, slightly sour dipping sauce. The pork is grilled over charcoal right on the pavement, so the smell is absolutely mouth-watering.
I go there at least once a week, usually with colleagues, and whenever friends visit Hanoi from abroad I take them there, because I think it’s more authentic than any restaurant in a guidebook.

I like it for several reasons. The food is consistently excellent and reasonably priced — less than two dollars a bowl. But I also love the atmosphere: you sit on low plastic stools, strangers share tables and the owners remember your order. It reminds me of what I love about Vietnamese food culture — it isn’t just about eating, it’s about community. I really hope the daughter keeps it going when her parents retire.

write.prompt: Nowadays, many people eat fast food or order meals online instead of cooking at home. Why is this happening? Is this a positive or negative development?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase; causes + mainly negative evaluation
Body 1: causes — long working hours, convenience apps, smaller households, price
Body 2: evaluation — health, family, skills, waste vs jobs and variety
Conclusion: negative overall; balance and education
model: In many countries, it has become increasingly common for people to rely on fast food and meal delivery rather than preparing food at home. This essay will discuss the reasons for this trend and explain why I believe it is, on balance, a negative development.

Several factors explain this change. The most important is lack of time: long working hours and long commutes leave many people with little energy to shop and cook in the evening. At the same time, delivery apps have made ordering food extremely convenient, offering thousands of dishes at the touch of a button. Smaller households also play a role, since cooking for one person can seem less worthwhile. Finally, in many cities, takeaway meals are relatively cheap, so cooking does not always save money.

Although this trend creates jobs for drivers and helps small restaurants reach more customers, I believe its disadvantages are greater. Takeaway and fast food tend to contain more salt, sugar and fat than home-cooked meals, contributing to rising rates of obesity and related diseases. Moreover, when families stop cooking and eating together, they lose an important opportunity to talk and connect, and children may never learn basic cooking skills. The huge amount of plastic packaging used for deliveries is also harmful to the environment.

In conclusion, people are cooking less because of busy lifestyles and the convenience of technology. While ordering food occasionally is not a problem, I believe the overall trend is negative for health, family life and the environment, and schools and employers should encourage simple cooking skills and reasonable working hours.

levels.name: Band 6→7
levels.title: Competent: abstract and global issues
levels.desc: Globalisation, public spending, art, artificial intelligence, language, housing, the media, wildlife, childhood and space — topics where you must explain ideas, not just describe them.
goals: Use less common vocabulary and collocations accurately (e.g. “widen the gap”, “a pressing concern”)
Write complex sentences with nominalisation, participle clauses and concession
Develop every body paragraph with a clear point, explanation and specific example
Speak at length in Part 3 with speculation, evaluation and comparison
Handle mixed Task 1 charts and select the key features instead of listing every number
extra: Cambridge IELTS 16–18: one full Reading test a week in 60 minutes, then analyse every wrong answer
Listen to a 10-minute podcast daily (BBC 6 Minute English → BBC Radio 4 “More or Less”) and shadow 2 minutes
Keep a collocation notebook: 10 new pairs a week, used in your own sentences
Have one Writing task a fortnight marked by a teacher against the four criteria

units.title: Globalisation
units.goal: Discuss the effects of globalisation on economies and cultures, using nominalisation and concession.

lines.t: Do you often buy products made in other countries?
lines.vi: Bạn có hay mua sản phẩm sản xuất ở nước khác không?

lines.t: All the time, often without realising it. My phone was designed in one country, assembled in another and probably contains parts from a dozen more.
lines.vi: Lúc nào cũng vậy, thường là không nhận ra. Điện thoại của tôi được thiết kế ở một nước, lắp ráp ở nước khác và có lẽ chứa linh kiện từ cả chục nước nữa.

lines.t: Do you prefer local or international food?
lines.vi: Bạn thích đồ ăn địa phương hay quốc tế?

lines.t: Local food on a daily basis, without a doubt. International chains are convenient, but they taste the same everywhere, which I find a bit dull.
lines.vi: Hằng ngày thì chắc chắn là đồ địa phương. Chuỗi quốc tế tiện, nhưng ở đâu vị cũng như nhau, tôi thấy hơi nhàm.

lines.t: Would you like to work for an international company?

lines.t: I already do, in a sense — our main client is Japanese. I enjoy it because you pick up different ways of working, although time differences can be exhausting.
lines.vi: Theo một nghĩa nào đó thì tôi đang làm — khách hàng chính của chúng tôi là người Nhật. Tôi thích vì học được nhiều cách làm việc khác nhau, dù chênh lệch múi giờ có thể rất mệt.

read.title: Winners and losers of global trade

sents.t: Between 1990 and 2019, the share of the world’s population living in extreme poverty fell from 36 per cent to under 10 per cent.
sents.vi: Từ 1990 đến 2019, tỉ lệ dân số thế giới sống trong nghèo cùng cực giảm từ 36% xuống dưới 10%.

sents.t: Much of this improvement took place in East Asia, where export-led growth created millions of factory jobs.
sents.vi: Phần lớn sự cải thiện này diễn ra ở Đông Á, nơi tăng trưởng dựa vào xuất khẩu tạo ra hàng triệu việc làm nhà máy.

sents.t: At the same time, some manufacturing towns in wealthier countries lost their main employers.
sents.vi: Cùng lúc đó, một số thị trấn sản xuất ở các nước giàu hơn mất đi những nhà tuyển dụng chính.

sents.t: Economists generally agree that trade increases total wealth, but they disagree about how the gains should be shared.
sents.vi: Các nhà kinh tế nhìn chung đồng ý rằng thương mại làm tăng tổng của cải, nhưng bất đồng về việc nên chia lợi ích thế nào.

sents.t: Retraining programmes for displaced workers have produced mixed results.
sents.vi: Các chương trình đào tạo lại cho lao động mất việc cho kết quả không đồng đều.

q.q: Extreme poverty fell to less than a tenth of the world’s population by 2019.
Economists disagree about whether trade increases total wealth.
Retraining programmes have been most successful in Europe.

gram.title: Nominalisation: turning verbs into nouns
gram.rule: globalise → globalisation · grow → growth · decide → decision · The rapid growth of trade has led to …
gram.note: Academic writing often packs an idea into a noun phrase instead of a whole clause. Compare “Because trade has grown rapidly, …” with “The rapid growth of trade has …”. This sounds more formal and lets you put the main idea at the start of the sentence. Don’t overdo it — two or three nominalised phrases per paragraph is enough.

ex.t: The expansion of free trade has created jobs.
ex.vi: Sự mở rộng thương mại tự do đã tạo việc làm.

ex.t: The disappearance of local shops worries residents.
ex.vi: Sự biến mất của cửa hàng địa phương khiến cư dân lo lắng.

ex.t: The introduction of tariffs led to higher prices.
ex.vi: Việc áp thuế quan dẫn đến giá cao hơn.

ex.t: There has been a significant reduction in poverty.
ex.vi: Đã có sự giảm nghèo đáng kể.

drill.t: The ___ of foreign companies created jobs.
drill.vi: Sự xuất hiện của công ty nước ngoài tạo việc làm.

drill.t: There was a sharp ___ in exports.
drill.vi: Xuất khẩu tăng mạnh.

drill.t: The ___ to close the factory shocked workers.
drill.vi: Quyết định đóng cửa nhà máy làm công nhân sốc.

drill.t: The ___ of traditions is a concern.
drill.vi: Việc mất đi truyền thống là một mối lo.

lines.t: Is globalisation making cultures more similar?
lines.vi: Toàn cầu hoá có làm các nền văn hoá giống nhau hơn không?

lines.t: On the surface, yes — people in Hanoi and Madrid wear the same brands and watch the same series. But I’d argue that deeper things, like family values or how people celebrate festivals, change much more slowly. If anything, global exposure sometimes makes people more protective of their own traditions.
lines.vi: Bề ngoài thì có — người ở Hà Nội và Madrid mặc cùng thương hiệu, xem cùng loạt phim. Nhưng tôi cho rằng những thứ sâu xa hơn, như giá trị gia đình hay cách đón lễ hội, thay đổi chậm hơn nhiều. Thậm chí, tiếp xúc toàn cầu đôi khi khiến người ta trân trọng truyền thống của mình hơn.

lines.t: Who benefits most from globalisation?
lines.vi: Ai hưởng lợi nhiều nhất từ toàn cầu hoá?

lines.t: Consumers and highly skilled workers, generally. Products are cheaper and skilled people can work anywhere. The ones who lose out tend to be low-skilled workers in industries that move abroad, and unless governments support them, resentment builds up.
lines.vi: Nhìn chung là người tiêu dùng và lao động tay nghề cao. Hàng rẻ hơn và người giỏi có thể làm việc ở bất cứ đâu. Người chịu thiệt thường là lao động tay nghề thấp trong các ngành chuyển ra nước ngoài, và nếu chính phủ không hỗ trợ, sự bất mãn sẽ tích tụ.

lines.t: Do you think globalisation will continue?
lines.vi: Bạn nghĩ toàn cầu hoá có tiếp tục không?

lines.t: In a different form. After the pandemic, many companies realised their supply chains were too fragile, so we’re seeing production move closer to home. But digital globalisation — services, ideas, online work — seems likely to keep accelerating.
lines.vi: Theo hình thức khác. Sau đại dịch, nhiều công ty nhận ra chuỗi cung ứng quá mong manh, nên ta thấy sản xuất dời về gần hơn. Nhưng toàn cầu hoá số — dịch vụ, ý tưởng, làm việc trực tuyến — có vẻ sẽ tiếp tục tăng tốc.

gram2.title: Concession: despite, although, even though, while
gram2.rule: Despite / In spite of + noun / -ing · Although / Even though + clause · While it is true that …, … · Admittedly, …
gram2.note: Concession shows that you have considered the other side, which is essential for band 7 in Task Response. Despite is followed by a noun or -ing, never a full clause: Despite earning more, … or Despite the fact that they earn more, … Even though is stronger than although. Admittedly introduces a point you accept before you challenge it.

ex.t: Despite creating jobs, foreign factories can pollute rivers.
ex.vi: Dù tạo việc làm, nhà máy nước ngoài có thể làm ô nhiễm sông.

ex.t: Although trade has grown, inequality remains.
ex.vi: Dù thương mại tăng, bất bình đẳng vẫn còn.

ex.t: Even though prices are lower, quality has fallen.
ex.vi: Dù giá thấp hơn, chất lượng đã giảm.

ex.t: Admittedly, some traditions have been lost.
ex.vi: Phải thừa nhận rằng một số truyền thống đã mất.

drill.t: ___ the benefits, many people oppose free trade.
drill.vi: Bất chấp lợi ích, nhiều người phản đối thương mại tự do.

drill.t: ___ wages rose, workers felt insecure.
drill.vi: Dù lương tăng, người lao động vẫn thấy bất an.

drill.t: In spite ___ the risks, they invested abroad.
drill.vi: Bất chấp rủi ro, họ đầu tư ra nước ngoài.

drill.t: Despite ___ cheap, the product sold badly.
drill.vi: Dù rẻ, sản phẩm bán kém.

cue.card: Describe a foreign product that is popular in your country.
points: and explain why you think it is so popular
model: I’m going to talk about Korean skincare products, which have become incredibly popular in Vietnam over the past decade.

They originally come from South Korea, of course, but they’re now sold everywhere here — in shopping malls, on social media and even in small neighbourhood shops. The main customers are young women, but I’ve noticed that more and more men, including some of my colleagues, have started using them too, mostly sunscreen and simple moisturisers.

I think there are three reasons for their popularity. The first is the influence of Korean dramas and music, which have made Korean beauty standards very fashionable. The second is that the products are marketed cleverly: the packaging is cute, the prices are affordable, and influencers post detailed reviews, so buyers feel well informed. And the third reason is practical — they’re designed for a climate and skin types fairly similar to ours. Admittedly, the trend has its downsides: some people now spend a lot of money on ten-step routines they don’t really need. But overall it’s a good example of how globalisation spreads culture through everyday consumer goods.

write.prompt: Some people think that globalisation has more negative effects than positive effects on developing countries. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase + position (disagree overall: benefits greater, but costs real and need managing)
Body 1: concede the negatives — exploitation, environmental damage, cultural erosion, with a specific example
Body 2: main argument — poverty reduction, technology transfer, jobs for women; East Asia example
Conclusion: restate the position and the condition (strong regulation)
model: It is often claimed that developing nations lose more than they gain from globalisation. Although its costs are real and sometimes severe, I largely disagree with this view, since the integration of these countries into the world economy has been the main driver of the dramatic reduction in poverty over the past three decades.

Admittedly, globalisation has brought significant problems. In the rush to attract foreign investment, some governments have tolerated poor working conditions and weak environmental standards, and the collapse of a garment factory in Bangladesh in 2013, which killed more than a thousand workers, showed the human cost of this approach. There is also a risk that the spread of global brands and media erodes local languages and traditions, particularly among young people in cities.

Nevertheless, the benefits have been considerably greater. The expansion of export industries in countries such as Vietnam and China has lifted hundreds of millions of people out of extreme poverty, giving families a stable income for the first time. Foreign companies have also brought technology and management skills that local firms have since adopted, while factory work has given many women financial independence. Moreover, cheaper imported goods, from medicines to mobile phones, have raised the standard of living for ordinary households.

In conclusion, while globalisation undoubtedly carries risks for developing countries, I believe its positive effects, above all the large-scale reduction in poverty, outweigh the negative ones. The key challenge for governments is not to resist globalisation but to regulate it so that growth does not come at the expense of workers’ safety or the environment.

lines.t: What public facilities do you use most?
lines.vi: Bạn dùng tiện ích công cộng nào nhiều nhất?

lines.t: Probably the parks and the public library near my office. The library was renovated last year and it’s now one of the few quiet places in the city centre where you can work for free.
lines.vi: Có lẽ là công viên và thư viện công cộng gần cơ quan. Thư viện được cải tạo năm ngoái và giờ là một trong số ít nơi yên tĩnh ở trung tâm mà bạn làm việc miễn phí được.

lines.t: Are there enough public facilities where you live?
lines.vi: Nơi bạn sống có đủ tiện ích công cộng không?

lines.t: Not really. What we lack most is green space. New apartment blocks keep going up, but parks and playgrounds haven’t kept pace with the population.
lines.vi: Không hẳn. Thứ chúng tôi thiếu nhất là không gian xanh. Chung cư mới cứ mọc lên, nhưng công viên và sân chơi không theo kịp dân số.

lines.t: Would you pay more tax for better services?
lines.vi: Bạn có sẵn sàng đóng thuế cao hơn để có dịch vụ tốt hơn không?

lines.t: I would, as long as I could see where the money goes. People don’t mind paying tax nearly as much as they mind feeling it’s being wasted.
lines.vi: Có, miễn là tôi thấy được tiền đi đâu. Người ta không ngại đóng thuế bằng việc cảm thấy tiền bị lãng phí.

sents.t: A study of public health programmes in high-income countries estimated that every dollar spent on prevention saved an average of fourteen dollars.
sents.vi: Một nghiên cứu về chương trình y tế công ở các nước thu nhập cao ước tính mỗi đô la chi cho phòng ngừa tiết kiệm trung bình mười bốn đô la.

sents.t: Programmes such as tobacco taxes and childhood vaccination gave the highest returns.
sents.vi: Các chương trình như thuế thuốc lá và tiêm chủng cho trẻ em mang lại lợi ích cao nhất.

sents.t: Despite this, prevention typically receives less than five per cent of health budgets.
sents.vi: Dù vậy, phòng ngừa thường chỉ nhận chưa đến 5% ngân sách y tế.

sents.t: One explanation is political: the benefits appear years later, long after the next election.
sents.vi: Một cách giải thích mang tính chính trị: lợi ích xuất hiện nhiều năm sau, lâu sau kỳ bầu cử tới.

sents.t: Hospitals, by contrast, produce visible results that voters can see immediately.
sents.vi: Ngược lại, bệnh viện tạo ra kết quả hữu hình mà cử tri thấy ngay.

q.q: Prevention programmes saved more money than they cost.
Prevention usually receives about a quarter of health budgets.
Vaccination programmes were more cost-effective than tobacco taxes.

gram.title: Cleft sentences for emphasis
gram.rule: What + clause + is/was … (What we need is …) · It is/was … that/who … (It is the government that …) · The reason why … is that …
gram.note: Cleft sentences split one idea into two parts to highlight the key information. They are very natural in Speaking Part 3 and useful in essays for emphasis: What concerns me most is … / It is not the cost but the lack of planning that … Use them occasionally; one or two per answer is enough.

ex.t: What the city needs is more affordable housing.
ex.vi: Điều thành phố cần là thêm nhà ở giá phải chăng.

ex.t: It is the poorest families who suffer most.
ex.vi: Chính các gia đình nghèo nhất chịu thiệt nhiều nhất.

ex.t: The reason why prevention is ignored is that results take years.
ex.vi: Lý do phòng ngừa bị bỏ qua là kết quả cần nhiều năm.

ex.t: What surprised me was how little was spent on parks.
ex.vi: Điều làm tôi ngạc nhiên là chi cho công viên ít đến thế.

drill.t: ___ we lack is good public transport.
drill.vi: Thứ chúng ta thiếu là giao thông công cộng tốt.

drill.t: It is teachers ___ make schools work.
drill.vi: Chính giáo viên làm nên trường học.

drill.t: The reason ___ taxes rose is the war.
drill.vi: Lý do thuế tăng là chiến tranh.

drill.t: It was in 2010 ___ the bridge opened.
drill.vi: Chính năm 2010 cây cầu thông xe.

lines.t: Should governments spend money on the arts when there are poor people?
lines.vi: Chính phủ có nên chi tiền cho nghệ thuật khi vẫn còn người nghèo?

lines.t: I think it’s a false choice. Arts funding is usually a tiny fraction of the budget, and cutting it wouldn’t solve poverty. What’s more, museums and festivals bring in tourism and jobs. That said, basic needs like healthcare must clearly take precedence when resources are scarce.
lines.vi: Tôi nghĩ đó là lựa chọn giả. Kinh phí nghệ thuật thường chỉ là phần nhỏ ngân sách, cắt đi cũng không giải quyết được nghèo đói. Hơn nữa, bảo tàng và lễ hội mang lại du lịch và việc làm. Dù vậy, nhu cầu cơ bản như y tế rõ ràng phải được ưu tiên khi nguồn lực khan hiếm.

lines.t: Is it better for services to be run by the state or by private companies?
lines.vi: Dịch vụ nên do nhà nước hay công ty tư nhân điều hành?

lines.t: It depends on the service. Where there’s real competition, like telecoms, private firms tend to be more efficient. But for natural monopolies such as water or railways, privatisation has often meant higher prices without better quality, so I’d keep those public.
lines.vi: Còn tuỳ dịch vụ. Nơi có cạnh tranh thực sự như viễn thông, công ty tư nhân thường hiệu quả hơn. Nhưng với độc quyền tự nhiên như nước hay đường sắt, tư nhân hoá thường đồng nghĩa giá cao hơn mà chất lượng không tốt hơn, nên tôi sẽ giữ chúng công lập.

lines.t: Why do governments often focus on short-term projects?
lines.vi: Vì sao chính phủ hay tập trung vào dự án ngắn hạn?

lines.t: Mainly because of elections. A new bridge can be opened before the next vote, whereas the benefits of better teacher training appear ten years later. It’s short-sighted, but it’s politically rational.
lines.vi: Chủ yếu vì bầu cử. Một cây cầu mới có thể khánh thành trước kỳ bỏ phiếu, còn lợi ích của việc đào tạo giáo viên tốt hơn mười năm sau mới thấy. Điều đó thiển cận nhưng hợp lý về mặt chính trị.

gram2.title: The language of priorities
gram2.rule: should take priority / precedence over · rather than · at the expense of · come first · be more pressing than
gram2.note: Many Task 2 questions ask what governments should prioritise. Show your ranking clearly and explain why. Take priority over and at the expense of are followed by a noun or -ing. Rather than can join two verbs in the same form: invest in schools rather than build stadiums.

ex.t: Healthcare should take priority over defence.
ex.vi: Y tế nên được ưu tiên hơn quốc phòng.

ex.t: The city invested in roads rather than public transport.
ex.vi: Thành phố đầu tư đường sá thay vì giao thông công cộng.

ex.t: Growth came at the expense of the environment.
ex.vi: Tăng trưởng đến với cái giá là môi trường.

ex.t: Housing is a more pressing problem than tourism.
ex.vi: Nhà ở là vấn đề cấp bách hơn du lịch.

drill.t: Safety should take priority ___ speed.
drill.vi: An toàn nên được ưu tiên hơn tốc độ.

drill.t: They built a stadium at the expense ___ schools.
drill.vi: Họ xây sân vận động với cái giá là trường học.

drill.t: Fund teachers rather than ___ new buildings.
drill.vi: Hãy đầu tư cho giáo viên thay vì xây toà nhà mới.

drill.t: Clean water must come ___.
drill.vi: Nước sạch phải được đặt lên hàng đầu.

cue.card: Describe a public service or facility that you think needs improving.
points: and explain how it could be improved
model: I’d like to talk about the public bus network in my city, which I use three or four times a week, mainly to get to work when it’s raining too hard to ride my motorbike.

In fairness, it’s improved in some ways — the buses are newer and most of them have air conditioning now. But it still has three big problems. The first is reliability: there’s no way of knowing when a bus will actually arrive, so you can wait five minutes or forty. The second is that buses get stuck in exactly the same traffic as everyone else, so they’re rarely faster than a car. And the third is the stops themselves, many of which have no shelter and are blocked by parked motorbikes.

What would make the biggest difference, I think, is dedicated bus lanes on the main roads, because if buses were genuinely faster, people would switch voluntarily. Real-time arrival information on an app would also be cheap and very effective. It’s frustrating, because a better bus system would cost far less than new flyovers, but flyovers are more visible, so they tend to get the money.

write.prompt: Some people believe that governments should spend money on improving public services such as healthcare and education rather than on arts and culture. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
plan: Introduction: paraphrase both views + position (essential services first, but a modest arts budget is justified)
Body 1: the case for prioritising services — scarce resources, life and death, equality
Body 2: the case for arts funding — identity, tourism revenue, market failure; small cost
Conclusion: balance, with the condition that core services are adequately funded first
model: There is considerable debate about whether public money should go exclusively to essential services, such as hospitals and schools, or whether part of it should also support the arts. In my opinion, healthcare and education must come first, but a modest investment in culture is still justified because of the wider benefits it brings.

Those who argue that services should take priority have a strong case. Public funds are limited, and every dollar spent on a theatre is a dollar not spent on medicines or teachers. In many countries hospitals remain overcrowded and rural schools lack basic equipment, so it can seem irresponsible to fund an orchestra while these needs are unmet. Furthermore, essential services benefit the whole population, whereas audiences for opera or galleries tend to be wealthier and better educated.

On the other hand, there are convincing reasons for supporting culture. The arts help to preserve a nation’s identity and pass on its history to younger generations, something the market alone will not do, since traditional crafts and performances are rarely profitable. Cultural institutions can also generate significant revenue: museums and festivals attract tourists, who spend money in hotels and restaurants and create jobs. Crucially, arts budgets are usually tiny compared with health or education spending, so eliminating them would make almost no difference to the quality of those services.

In conclusion, while I agree that governments should prioritise the services that people depend on, I do not believe this requires abandoning the arts altogether. Provided that healthcare and education are adequately funded, spending a small proportion of the budget on culture is a reasonable investment in a society’s identity and economy.

units.title: Art & creativity
units.goal: Talk about art, creativity and its value, using participle clauses and dependent prepositions.

words.ex: Schools should encourage creativity.
words.exVi: Trường học nên khuyến khích sáng tạo.

words.ex: The painting is considered a masterpiece.
words.exVi: Bức tranh được coi là kiệt tác.

words.ex: The exhibition attracted 50,000 visitors.
words.exVi: Triển lãm thu hút 50.000 khách.

words.ex: I prefer contemporary art to classical art.
words.exVi: Tôi thích nghệ thuật đương đại hơn cổ điển.

words.ex: Abstract paintings can be hard to interpret.
words.exVi: Tranh trừu tượng có thể khó hiểu.

words.ex: Everyone interprets a poem differently.
words.exVi: Mỗi người diễn giải bài thơ khác nhau.

words.ex: The building has great aesthetic value.
words.exVi: Toà nhà có giá trị thẩm mỹ cao.

words.ex: Art is a form of self-expression.
words.exVi: Nghệ thuật là một hình thức thể hiện bản thân.

words.ex: Children have vivid imaginations.
words.exVi: Trẻ em có trí tưởng tượng phong phú.

words.ex: The vase shows fine craftsmanship.
words.exVi: Chiếc bình thể hiện tay nghề tinh xảo.

words.ex: Dance and theatre are performing arts.
words.exVi: Múa và kịch là nghệ thuật biểu diễn.

words.ex: Painting and photography are visual arts.
words.exVi: Hội hoạ và nhiếp ảnh là nghệ thuật thị giác.

words.ex: Street art has made the area famous.
words.exVi: Nghệ thuật đường phố đã làm khu vực nổi tiếng.

words.ex: The city commissioned a statue.
words.exVi: Thành phố đặt làm một bức tượng.

words.ex: The sea inspired many of her paintings.
words.exVi: Biển đã truyền cảm hứng cho nhiều bức tranh của cô.

words.ex: His ideas are highly original.
words.exVi: Ý tưởng của anh ấy rất độc đáo.

words.ex: The sculpture was controversial.
words.exVi: Bức điêu khắc gây tranh cãi.

words.ex: You don’t need training to appreciate music.
words.exVi: Bạn không cần được đào tạo để thưởng thức âm nhạc.

words.ex: The film conveys a sense of loss.
words.exVi: Bộ phim truyền tải cảm giác mất mát.

words.ex: The exhibition was deliberately provocative.
words.exVi: Triển lãm cố tình gây suy nghĩ, tranh luận.

lines.t: Do you like art?
lines.vi: Bạn có thích nghệ thuật không?

lines.t: I do, though I’m more into photography and street art than traditional painting. There’s something about art you can see for free, on a wall in your own neighbourhood, that appeals to me.
lines.vi: Có, dù tôi thích nhiếp ảnh và nghệ thuật đường phố hơn hội hoạ truyền thống. Nghệ thuật bạn xem miễn phí trên bức tường ngay khu mình ở có điều gì đó cuốn hút tôi.

lines.t: Did you learn art at school?
lines.vi: Bạn có học mỹ thuật ở trường không?

lines.t: Only until about twelve. After that it was dropped to make room for exam subjects, which I think was a pity, because it was the only lesson where there was no single right answer.
lines.vi: Chỉ đến khoảng mười hai tuổi. Sau đó môn này bị bỏ để nhường chỗ cho các môn thi, điều tôi thấy tiếc, vì đó là tiết duy nhất không có một đáp án đúng duy nhất.

lines.t: Have you been to an art gallery recently?
lines.vi: Gần đây bạn có đi phòng tranh không?

lines.t: Yes, a photography exhibition about the old quarter. Seeing photos of my own city from the 1930s was surprisingly moving.
lines.vi: Có, một triển lãm ảnh về phố cổ. Xem ảnh thành phố của chính mình từ thập niên 1930 cảm động một cách bất ngờ.

sents.t: In 2022, an image created with an AI program won first prize in a digital art competition in the United States.
sents.vi: Năm 2022, một bức ảnh tạo bằng chương trình AI giành giải nhất một cuộc thi nghệ thuật số ở Mỹ.

sents.t: The decision provoked angry reactions from artists, who argued that the winner had not really made anything.
sents.vi: Quyết định này gây phản ứng gay gắt từ các nghệ sĩ, những người cho rằng người thắng thực ra không làm ra gì cả.

sents.t: The winner replied that he had spent more than eighty hours refining his instructions to the program.
sents.vi: Người thắng đáp lại rằng anh đã mất hơn tám mươi giờ để tinh chỉnh lời nhắc cho chương trình.

sents.t: Some philosophers suggest that creativity requires intention and experience, which machines lack.
sents.vi: Một số triết gia cho rằng sáng tạo đòi hỏi ý định và trải nghiệm, thứ máy móc không có.

sents.t: Others point out that photography was also dismissed as mechanical when it was first invented.
sents.vi: Số khác chỉ ra rằng nhiếp ảnh cũng từng bị coi là máy móc khi mới ra đời.

q.q: The AI-generated image won a prize in a competition.
Artists welcomed the competition’s decision.
The competition later changed its rules about AI.

gram.title: Participle clauses
gram.rule: -ing clause (active): Walking through the gallery, I … · -ed clause (passive): Painted in 1889, the picture … · Having + past participle (earlier action)
gram.note: Participle clauses make writing more concise and varied. The subject of the participle must be the same as the subject of the main clause: Painted in 1889, the picture is … (the picture was painted). A wrong subject gives a “dangling participle”: ✗ Walking into the room, the painting caught my eye. Having + past participle shows the first action finished before the second.

ex.t: Built in the 11th century, the temple is the oldest in the city.
ex.vi: Được xây từ thế kỷ 11, ngôi đền lâu đời nhất thành phố.

ex.t: Using only recycled materials, the artist created a huge sculpture.
ex.vi: Chỉ dùng vật liệu tái chế, nghệ sĩ tạo ra một tác phẩm điêu khắc khổng lồ.

ex.t: Having studied in Paris, she returned to open a gallery.
ex.vi: Sau khi học ở Paris, cô ấy trở về mở phòng tranh.

ex.t: Paintings created by children are often very original.
ex.vi: Tranh do trẻ em vẽ thường rất độc đáo.

drill.t: ___ in 1920, the theatre needs repairs.
drill.vi: Được xây năm 1920, nhà hát cần sửa chữa.

drill.t: ___ the exhibition, I bought a catalogue.
drill.vi: Sau khi xem triển lãm, tôi mua một cuốn catalogue.

drill.t: Artists ___ in the city struggle to pay rent.
drill.vi: Nghệ sĩ sống ở thành phố khó trả tiền thuê nhà.

drill.t: ___ by the sea, she painted waves.
drill.vi: Được biển truyền cảm hứng, cô ấy vẽ sóng.

lines.t: Why do people value art?
lines.vi: Vì sao con người coi trọng nghệ thuật?

lines.t: I think it does something that information can’t. A news report can tell you a war happened, but a novel or a painting can make you feel what it was like. It also connects us across time — we can look at a two-thousand-year-old pot and recognise someone who cared about beauty, just like us.
lines.vi: Tôi nghĩ nó làm được điều mà thông tin không làm được. Bản tin cho bạn biết chiến tranh đã xảy ra, nhưng tiểu thuyết hay bức tranh khiến bạn cảm nhận được nó ra sao. Nó còn kết nối ta qua thời gian — nhìn chiếc bình hai nghìn năm tuổi, ta nhận ra một người cũng quan tâm đến cái đẹp như mình.

lines.t: Should art be a compulsory subject at school?
lines.vi: Mỹ thuật có nên là môn bắt buộc không?

lines.t: At least until the mid-teens, yes. It’s not about producing artists; it’s about developing creativity and the confidence to try things without a fixed answer, which employers increasingly say they want.
lines.vi: Ít nhất đến giữa tuổi thiếu niên thì có. Không phải để tạo ra nghệ sĩ, mà để phát triển sự sáng tạo và tự tin thử nghiệm khi không có đáp án cố định, điều mà nhà tuyển dụng ngày càng nói họ cần.

lines.t: Will AI replace human artists?
lines.vi: AI có thay thế nghệ sĩ không?

lines.t: It will probably replace some commercial work, like simple illustrations for adverts. But people care about the story behind a work — who made it and why — so I suspect human-made art will become more valued, not less, in the same way handmade furniture is worth more than factory-made.
lines.vi: Có lẽ nó sẽ thay thế một phần công việc thương mại, như minh hoạ đơn giản cho quảng cáo. Nhưng người ta quan tâm câu chuyện đằng sau tác phẩm — ai làm và vì sao — nên tôi đoán nghệ thuật do người làm sẽ được coi trọng hơn, giống như đồ gỗ thủ công đắt hơn đồ nhà máy.

gram2.title: Dependent prepositions
gram2.rule: interested in · capable of · responsible for · aware of · influenced by · contribute to · benefit from · focus on
gram2.note: Many adjectives, verbs and nouns are followed by a fixed preposition, and errors with them are very common at band 6. Learn them as chunks. After a preposition, use a noun or -ing: capable of producing, contribute to improving (here to is a preposition).

ex.t: Children are capable of producing remarkable work.
ex.vi: Trẻ em có khả năng tạo ra tác phẩm đáng chú ý.

ex.t: Art contributes to a sense of community.
ex.vi: Nghệ thuật góp phần tạo cảm giác cộng đồng.

ex.t: Many artists are influenced by nature.
ex.vi: Nhiều nghệ sĩ chịu ảnh hưởng của thiên nhiên.

ex.t: The whole city benefits from the festival.
ex.vi: Cả thành phố được hưởng lợi từ lễ hội.

drill.t: She is very interested ___ pottery.
drill.vi: Cô ấy rất quan tâm đến gốm.

drill.t: Museums contribute ___ tourism.
drill.vi: Bảo tàng đóng góp cho du lịch.

drill.t: Who is responsible ___ the design?
drill.vi: Ai chịu trách nhiệm thiết kế?

drill.t: Most people are not aware ___ the artist’s name.
drill.vi: Phần lớn người ta không biết tên nghệ sĩ.

cue.card: Describe a piece of art you have seen that you liked.
points: and explain why you liked it
model: The piece I’d like to describe is a large lacquer painting I saw at the Fine Arts Museum in Hanoi. It was painted in the 1930s by Nguyen Gia Tri, one of the artists who turned lacquer — which had been used mainly for decorating furniture — into a serious art form.

It shows a group of young women in a garden, but it’s not realistic at all. The figures are almost floating against a deep black background, and the colours are gold, red and a kind of eggshell white that seems to glow when you walk past, because the light catches the different layers. Made using dozens of layers of resin, each one polished by hand, it apparently took years to finish.

I liked it for two reasons. First, I was impressed by the sheer craftsmanship — you can’t really appreciate it from a photo, because the surface changes depending on where you stand. And second, I liked the idea behind it: taking a traditional Vietnamese craft and using it to create something completely modern. Having seen it, I started paying much more attention to lacquerware in ordinary shops, so it genuinely changed how I look at everyday objects.

write.prompt: The charts below show the number of visitors to three types of cultural venue in a city and the main reasons visitors gave for attending in 2023. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
write.data:
Annual visitors (thousands)   2013   2023
Art museums                   420    610
Theatres                      380    290
Music festivals               150    540

Main reason for attending (2023, % of visitors)
Socialising with friends   41%
Interest in the art form   33%
Tourism / sightseeing      18%
Education / school trip     8%
plan: Introduction: paraphrase both charts in one sentence
Overview: festivals and museums grew while theatres declined; socialising was the top reason
Body 1: visitor numbers — festivals more than tripled, museums up by nearly half, theatres down
Body 2: reasons — socialising vs interest, tourism and education; link to festival growth
model: The bar chart compares the number of people who visited three kinds of cultural venue in a city in 2013 and 2023, while the pie chart shows the main reasons that visitors gave for attending in 2023.

Overall, attendance at music festivals and art museums rose over the decade, whereas theatres became less popular. In 2023, the most common motivation for attending cultural events was social rather than artistic.

Music festivals experienced the most dramatic growth, with visitor numbers more than tripling from 150,000 to 540,000. Art museums remained the most visited venue, attracting 610,000 people in 2023, an increase of almost half compared with 2013. Theatres, by contrast, were the only venue to lose visitors, with numbers falling from 380,000 to 290,000, which meant they had changed from the second most popular venue to the least popular.

As for motivation, 41% of visitors said they attended mainly to spend time with friends, compared with a third who were primarily interested in the art form itself. Tourism accounted for just under a fifth of visits, and only 8% of visitors were attending for educational reasons, such as school trips. The prominence of socialising may partly explain the rapid rise in festival attendance.

units.title: Artificial intelligence
units.goal: Discuss the opportunities and risks of AI, using future forms and advanced hedging.

words.ex: The algorithm recommends videos you might like.
words.exVi: Thuật toán gợi ý video bạn có thể thích.

words.ex: Machine learning finds patterns in huge datasets.
words.exVi: Học máy tìm ra quy luật trong tập dữ liệu khổng lồ.

words.ex: The model was trained on a large dataset.
words.exVi: Mô hình được huấn luyện trên một tập dữ liệu lớn.

words.ex: Biased data produces biased decisions.
words.exVi: Dữ liệu thiên lệch tạo ra quyết định thiên lệch.

words.ex: Users want more transparency about how AI decides.
words.exVi: Người dùng muốn minh bạch hơn về cách AI ra quyết định.
