words.ex: Airlines let passengers offset their emissions.
words.exVi: Hãng bay cho hành khách bù trừ phát thải.

words.vi: tài sản mắc kẹt (mất giá do chuyển đổi)
words.ex: New coal plants may become stranded assets.
words.exVi: Nhà máy than mới có thể trở thành tài sản mắc kẹt.

words.vi: đã đến lúc (lẽ ra phải làm từ lâu)
words.ex: It’s high time governments acted.
words.exVi: Đã đến lúc chính phủ phải hành động.

words.ex: Climate justice means protecting those who polluted least.
words.exVi: Công bằng khí hậu nghĩa là bảo vệ những người gây ô nhiễm ít nhất.

words.ex: Climate change requires collective action.
words.exVi: Biến đổi khí hậu đòi hỏi hành động tập thể.

lines.t: Has the weather where you live changed over the years?
lines.vi: Thời tiết nơi bạn sống có thay đổi qua các năm không?

lines.t: Noticeably. Summers in Hanoi feel longer and hotter than when I was a child, and flooding in the city after heavy rain has become much more common. My grandmother says the seasons used to be far more predictable.
lines.vi: Rõ rệt. Mùa hè ở Hà Nội có vẻ dài và nóng hơn so với hồi tôi còn nhỏ, và ngập lụt sau mưa lớn đã trở nên phổ biến hơn nhiều. Bà tôi nói các mùa trước đây dễ đoán hơn nhiều.

lines.t: Do you worry about climate change?
lines.vi: Bạn có lo về biến đổi khí hậu không?

lines.t: I do, though I try to focus on what I can actually influence. What worries me most is the Mekong Delta — if sea levels keep rising, millions of farmers could lose their land.
lines.vi: Có, dù tôi cố tập trung vào những gì mình thực sự tác động được. Điều tôi lo nhất là đồng bằng sông Cửu Long — nếu nước biển cứ dâng, hàng triệu nông dân có thể mất đất.

lines.t: Have you changed any habits because of the environment?
lines.vi: Bạn có thay đổi thói quen nào vì môi trường không?

lines.t: A few. I fly less, I’ve switched to an electric scooter, and I eat less beef. I’m realistic about the impact, but I’d rather my choices matched what I believe.
lines.vi: Một vài. Tôi bay ít hơn, đã chuyển sang xe máy điện, và ăn ít thịt bò hơn. Tôi thực tế về mức tác động, nhưng tôi muốn lựa chọn của mình khớp với điều mình tin hơn.

sents.t: Developed countries are responsible for roughly half of all carbon dioxide emitted since 1850, despite having a small fraction of the world’s population.
sents.vi: Các nước phát triển chịu trách nhiệm cho khoảng một nửa lượng CO2 phát thải từ năm 1850, dù chỉ chiếm phần nhỏ dân số thế giới.

sents.t: Meanwhile, many of the countries most vulnerable to rising seas and extreme heat have contributed very little to the problem.
sents.vi: Trong khi đó, nhiều nước dễ tổn thương nhất trước nước biển dâng và nắng nóng cực đoan lại đóng góp rất ít vào vấn đề.

sents.t: In 2009, wealthy nations promised to provide 100 billion dollars a year in climate finance by 2020.
sents.vi: Năm 2009, các nước giàu cam kết cung cấp 100 tỉ đô la tài chính khí hậu mỗi năm trước năm 2020.

sents.t: That target was missed, and much of the money that was provided came as loans rather than grants.
sents.vi: Mục tiêu đó đã không đạt được, và phần lớn số tiền được cung cấp là khoản vay chứ không phải viện trợ.

sents.t: Developing countries argue that loans add to debts that are already limiting their ability to adapt.
sents.vi: Các nước đang phát triển cho rằng khoản vay làm tăng nợ vốn đã hạn chế khả năng thích ứng của họ.

q.q: Developed countries have produced about half of historical CO₂ emissions.
The 100-billion-dollar target was reached on time.
Most climate finance has been spent on renewable energy.

gram.title: Unreal past: it’s time, would rather, wish, if only
gram.rule: It’s (high) time + subject + past simple · would rather + subject + past simple · wish / if only + past simple (present) or past perfect (past)
gram.note: These structures use a past form to talk about the present or future, expressing that something should happen or is unreal. It’s high time we acted (= we should have acted already). I’d rather governments spent money on adaptation (preference about others’ actions). I wish we had started earlier (regret about the past). They are natural in Speaking Part 3.

ex.t: It’s high time rich countries kept their promises.
ex.vi: Đã đến lúc các nước giàu phải giữ lời hứa.

ex.t: I’d rather the government invested in public transport.
ex.vi: Tôi muốn chính phủ đầu tư vào giao thông công cộng hơn.

ex.t: I wish we had taken climate warnings seriously in the 1990s.
ex.vi: Ước gì chúng ta đã coi trọng cảnh báo khí hậu từ thập niên 1990.

ex.t: If only electric cars were cheaper.
ex.vi: Giá như xe điện rẻ hơn.

drill.t: It’s high time we ___ coal.
drill.vi: Đã đến lúc ta ngừng dùng than.

drill.t: I’d rather you ___ the bus today.
drill.vi: Tôi muốn bạn đi xe buýt hôm nay hơn.

drill.t: I wish they ___ the forest last year.
drill.vi: Ước gì năm ngoái họ đã bảo vệ khu rừng.

drill.t: If only people ___ less meat.
drill.vi: Giá như mọi người ăn ít thịt hơn.

lines.t: Should developed countries do more than developing countries to fight climate change?
lines.vi: Các nước phát triển có nên làm nhiều hơn các nước đang phát triển trong chống biến đổi khí hậu?

lines.t: I believe so, for reasons of both fairness and capacity. They produced most historical emissions and they have the money and technology to decarbonise faster. That said, it’s not realistic for developing countries to wait — China and India are now huge emitters, so everyone has to act, just at different speeds.
lines.vi: Tôi tin là có, vì lý do công bằng lẫn năng lực. Họ tạo ra phần lớn lượng phát thải lịch sử và có tiền, công nghệ để khử carbon nhanh hơn. Dù vậy, các nước đang phát triển không thể chờ — Trung Quốc và Ấn Độ giờ là nguồn phát thải khổng lồ, nên ai cũng phải hành động, chỉ với tốc độ khác nhau.

lines.t: Can individuals make a real difference?
lines.vi: Cá nhân có thể tạo ra khác biệt thực sự không?

lines.t: Individually the impact is small, but collectively it shapes markets and politics. When enough consumers demand electric vehicles or vote for climate policies, companies and governments respond. The danger is when companies use individual responsibility to distract from their own emissions — a form of greenwashing.
lines.vi: Riêng lẻ thì tác động nhỏ, nhưng tập thể thì định hình thị trường và chính trị. Khi đủ người tiêu dùng đòi xe điện hay bầu cho chính sách khí hậu, doanh nghiệp và chính phủ sẽ phản ứng. Nguy hiểm là khi doanh nghiệp dùng trách nhiệm cá nhân để đánh lạc hướng khỏi khí thải của chính họ — một dạng tẩy xanh.

lines.t: Is adaptation more important than prevention?
lines.vi: Thích ứng có quan trọng hơn phòng ngừa không?

lines.t: We need both now, sadly. Some warming is already locked in, so places like the Mekong Delta have to adapt — salt-resistant crops, better flood defences. But adaptation has limits; if we cross major tipping points, no sea wall will be high enough.
lines.vi: Đáng buồn là giờ ta cần cả hai. Một mức nóng lên đã không thể tránh, nên những nơi như đồng bằng sông Cửu Long phải thích ứng — cây chịu mặn, đê chống lũ tốt hơn. Nhưng thích ứng có giới hạn; nếu vượt các điểm tới hạn lớn, không con đê nào đủ cao.

gram2.title: Collocations of responsibility and action
gram2.rule: bear / take / accept / shoulder responsibility · bear the brunt · take the lead · take action / measures / steps · meet / miss a target · honour / break a commitment
gram2.note: Abstract nouns like responsibility, action and target combine with specific verbs. Native-like combinations improve Lexical Resource: governments take steps (not “do steps”), countries meet or miss targets (not “reach a promise”), and nations honour or break commitments.

ex.t: Rich countries should take the lead in cutting emissions.
ex.vi: Các nước giàu nên đi đầu trong cắt giảm khí thải.

ex.t: Coastal communities bear the brunt of rising seas.
ex.vi: Cộng đồng ven biển gánh chịu nặng nề nhất nước biển dâng.

ex.t: Governments must take urgent measures.
ex.vi: Chính phủ phải có biện pháp khẩn cấp.

ex.t: Several countries failed to honour their commitments.
ex.vi: Nhiều nước không thực hiện cam kết của mình.

drill.t: The country missed its emissions ___.
drill.vi: Quốc gia không đạt mục tiêu phát thải.

drill.t: Who will ___ responsibility for the damage?
drill.vi: Ai sẽ chịu trách nhiệm cho thiệt hại?

drill.t: We must ___ steps to reduce waste.
drill.vi: Ta phải có các bước giảm rác thải.

drill.t: The government ___ its commitment.
drill.vi: Chính phủ đã thất hứa.

cue.card: Describe an environmental problem in your area.
points: and explain what you think should be done about it
model: The problem I’d like to describe is urban flooding in Hanoi, which has become noticeably worse during my lifetime.

After a heavy storm, which now seems to happen several times every rainy season, streets in some districts can be under half a metre of water within an hour. There are a few overlapping causes. Climate change is bringing more intense rainfall, but the bigger factor locally is probably development: many of the lakes and ponds that used to absorb water have been filled in to build housing, and the drainage system simply wasn’t designed for a city of eight million people.

It affects people in very practical ways. Motorbikes break down in the water, people miss work, small shops on the ground floor lose stock, and there are real health risks from contaminated water. Unsurprisingly, it’s poorer neighbourhoods in low-lying areas that bear the brunt. In terms of solutions, I wish the city had protected its lakes twenty years ago, but it’s high time we did what we can now: upgrading drains, creating parks that can temporarily store water, and stopping further construction on natural floodplains. Some cities, like Copenhagen, have built “sponge” neighbourhoods that absorb rain, and I’d rather we copied that than kept building higher walls.

write.prompt: Some people believe that individuals can do little to improve the environment and that only governments and large companies can make a difference. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase + position (disagree partly: governments/companies have the largest direct impact, but individuals matter collectively and politically)
Body 1: agree — scale of corporate/state emissions, policy changes, infrastructure examples
Body 2: disagree — individual demand shapes markets, social norms spread, political pressure; examples
Conclusion: the two are interdependent; avoid shifting blame either way
model: It is often argued that environmental problems are so vast that ordinary citizens are powerless, and that meaningful change can only come from governments and major corporations. While I accept that these institutions have by far the greatest direct influence, I disagree that individuals can do little, since their collective choices and political pressure are often what drive institutional action in the first place.

There is considerable truth in the view that institutions matter most. A single coal-fired power station can emit more carbon dioxide in a year than hundreds of thousands of households, and decisions about energy systems, public transport and building regulations are taken by governments, not individuals. Similarly, a handful of large companies are responsible for a substantial share of industrial emissions and plastic production. If these actors fail to act, recycling a few bottles or switching off lights at home will make little difference to global outcomes.

However, it would be a mistake to conclude that individual behaviour is irrelevant. Markets respond to consumer demand: the rapid growth of electric scooters in Vietnam and plant-based products in Europe has been driven largely by buyers, prompting manufacturers to invest further. Individual actions also spread socially; research suggests that people are more likely to install solar panels when their neighbours have done so. Most importantly, citizens shape policy through their votes, campaigns and public pressure. Many of the strongest environmental laws, from bans on single-use plastics to air-quality regulations, were introduced only after sustained public demand.

In conclusion, while governments and large corporations possess the greatest capacity to reduce environmental damage, they rarely act without pressure from the public. Individuals and institutions should therefore be seen as interdependent rather than as alternatives, and neither should use the other as an excuse for inaction.

units.title: Cultural heritage
units.goal: Discuss preserving history and tradition, using prepositional relative clauses and substitution.

words.ex: Temples and old houses are tangible heritage.
words.exVi: Đền chùa và nhà cổ là di sản vật thể.

words.ex: Ca trù singing is part of Vietnam’s intangible heritage.
words.exVi: Ca trù là một phần di sản phi vật thể của Việt Nam.

words.ex: The pagoda was restored using traditional methods.
words.exVi: Ngôi chùa được trùng tu bằng phương pháp truyền thống.

words.ex: The museum displays artefacts from the Bronze Age.
words.exVi: Bảo tàng trưng bày hiện vật từ thời kỳ đồ đồng.

words.ex: Some museums are repatriating stolen artefacts.
words.exVi: Một số bảo tàng đang trả lại hiện vật bị lấy cắp.

words.ex: Over-restoration can destroy authenticity.
words.exVi: Trùng tu quá mức có thể phá huỷ tính chân thực.

words.ex: These manuscripts are irreplaceable.
words.exVi: Những bản thảo này không thể thay thế.

words.ex: Many legends survive only in oral tradition.
words.exVi: Nhiều truyền thuyết chỉ còn qua truyền khẩu.

words.ex: Few young people want to become craftsmen.
words.exVi: Ít người trẻ muốn trở thành nghệ nhân.

words.ex: Folk music is enjoying a revival.
words.exVi: Âm nhạc dân gian đang được hồi sinh.

words.ex: Rapid modernisation has changed the old quarter.
words.exVi: Hiện đại hoá nhanh đã thay đổi phố cổ.

words.ex: Monuments shape a nation’s collective memory.
words.exVi: Đài tưởng niệm định hình ký ức tập thể của quốc gia.

words.ex: The library has digitised its ancient texts.
words.exVi: Thư viện đã số hoá các văn bản cổ.

words.ex: Festivals risk being commodified for tourists.
words.exVi: Lễ hội có nguy cơ bị hàng hoá hoá vì du khách.

words.ex: We visit our ancestral village every Tet.
words.exVi: Chúng tôi về quê tổ tiên mỗi dịp Tết.

words.vi: nghề thủ công có nguy cơ mai một
words.ex: Lacquer painting is an endangered craft in some villages.
words.exVi: Sơn mài là nghề có nguy cơ mai một ở một số làng.

words.ex: It is unclear the extent to which tourism helps.
words.exVi: Chưa rõ du lịch giúp ích đến mức nào.

words.ex: Local communities are the custodians of tradition.
words.exVi: Cộng đồng địa phương là người gìn giữ truyền thống.

words.ex: The poem has enduring popularity.
words.exVi: Bài thơ được yêu thích bền lâu.

words.ex: Many want to preserve the house, but few can afford to do so.
words.exVi: Nhiều người muốn giữ ngôi nhà nhưng ít ai đủ tiền làm như vậy.

lines.t: What traditional festivals do you celebrate?
lines.vi: Bạn đón những lễ hội truyền thống nào?

lines.t: Tet is the big one, of course. We still follow most of the customs — cleaning the house, visiting the graves of our ancestors, and giving lucky money — though the celebrations are shorter than in my grandparents’ day.
lines.vi: Tết là lớn nhất, đương nhiên. Chúng tôi vẫn giữ phần lớn phong tục — dọn nhà, viếng mộ tổ tiên, mừng tuổi — dù lễ ngắn hơn thời ông bà tôi.

lines.t: Do young people in your country value traditions?
lines.vi: Người trẻ ở nước bạn có coi trọng truyền thống không?

lines.t: More than people assume, actually. There’s been a real revival of interest in things like áo dài and traditional music, partly thanks to social media, although it’s sometimes more about style than meaning.
lines.vi: Thực ra nhiều hơn người ta nghĩ. Có sự hồi sinh thật sự trong quan tâm đến áo dài và âm nhạc truyền thống, một phần nhờ mạng xã hội, dù đôi khi thiên về phong cách hơn là ý nghĩa.

lines.t: Have you ever visited a historical site?
lines.vi: Bạn đã bao giờ thăm di tích lịch sử chưa?

lines.t: Many times. My favourite is the Temple of Literature in Hanoi, where students still go to pray before exams, which I find quite touching.
lines.vi: Nhiều lần. Tôi thích nhất Văn Miếu ở Hà Nội, nơi học sinh vẫn đến cầu may trước kỳ thi, điều tôi thấy khá cảm động.

sents.t: Many major European museums hold objects that were taken from other countries during the colonial period.
sents.vi: Nhiều bảo tàng lớn ở châu Âu đang giữ hiện vật được lấy từ các nước khác trong thời kỳ thuộc địa.

sents.t: In recent years, several governments have formally requested that these artefacts be returned.
sents.vi: Những năm gần đây, nhiều chính phủ đã chính thức yêu cầu trả lại các hiện vật này.

sents.t: In 2022, Germany began transferring ownership of more than 1,000 bronze sculptures to Nigeria.
sents.vi: Năm 2022, Đức bắt đầu chuyển quyền sở hữu hơn 1.000 tác phẩm điêu khắc bằng đồng cho Nigeria.

sents.t: Some museum directors have argued that objects are better protected and more widely seen in large international collections.
sents.vi: Một số giám đốc bảo tàng cho rằng hiện vật được bảo vệ tốt hơn và được nhiều người xem hơn ở các bộ sưu tập quốc tế lớn.

sents.t: Critics reply that this argument ignores the circumstances in which the objects were acquired.
sents.vi: Những người phản đối đáp rằng lập luận này phớt lờ hoàn cảnh hiện vật đã bị thu giữ.

q.q: Germany began returning bronze sculptures to Nigeria in 2022.
All museum directors support returning colonial artefacts.
The returned sculptures are now displayed in a new museum in Lagos.

gram.title: Relative clauses with prepositions
gram.rule: the village in which … · the people to whom … · the extent to which … · the period during which … · some / many / all of which / whom
gram.note: In formal English, the preposition moves to the front of the relative clause: the village where I grew up → the village in which I grew up. After a preposition, use which for things and whom for people — never that. Quantifier + of which / whom adds information about a group: The museum has 5,000 objects, many of which were donated.

ex.t: This is the house in which my grandfather was born.
ex.vi: Đây là ngôi nhà nơi ông tôi được sinh ra.

ex.t: It is unclear the extent to which tourism protects heritage.
ex.vi: Chưa rõ du lịch bảo vệ di sản đến mức nào.

ex.t: The artisans, most of whom are over sixty, need apprentices.
ex.vi: Các nghệ nhân, phần lớn đã ngoài sáu mươi, cần người học nghề.

ex.t: The period during which the temple was built remains uncertain.
ex.vi: Thời kỳ ngôi đền được xây vẫn chưa chắc chắn.

drill.t: The village ___ which the pottery is made is small.
drill.vi: Ngôi làng nơi làm gốm khá nhỏ.

drill.t: The man to ___ I spoke was a craftsman.
drill.vi: Người đàn ông tôi nói chuyện cùng là một nghệ nhân.

drill.t: It has 200 artefacts, most of ___ are bronze.
drill.vi: Có 200 hiện vật, phần lớn bằng đồng.

drill.t: Consider the extent to ___ it has changed.
drill.vi: Hãy xem nó đã thay đổi đến mức nào.

lines.t: Is it important to preserve old buildings in cities?
lines.vi: Bảo tồn công trình cổ trong thành phố có quan trọng không?

lines.t: Generally, yes, because they’re irreplaceable — once a building is demolished, the craftsmanship and the history it represents are gone for good. But preservation shouldn’t mean freezing a city. The most successful examples I’ve seen give old buildings new uses, so they’re lived in rather than just looked at.
lines.vi: Nhìn chung là có, vì chúng không thể thay thế — một khi bị phá, tay nghề và lịch sử nó đại diện sẽ mất vĩnh viễn. Nhưng bảo tồn không nên là đóng băng thành phố. Những ví dụ thành công nhất tôi từng thấy cho công trình cũ công năng mới, để chúng được sống trong đó chứ không chỉ để ngắm.

lines.t: Does tourism help or harm traditional culture?
lines.vi: Du lịch giúp hay hại văn hoá truyền thống?

lines.t: Both. It gives communities a financial reason to keep crafts and festivals alive, which matters when young people would otherwise leave. The risk is commodification — rituals being shortened or changed to suit tourists’ schedules, until they lose the meaning they had for the community itself.
lines.vi: Cả hai. Nó cho cộng đồng lý do tài chính để duy trì nghề thủ công và lễ hội, điều quan trọng khi người trẻ có thể bỏ đi. Rủi ro là hàng hoá hoá — nghi lễ bị rút ngắn hay thay đổi cho hợp lịch trình du khách, đến khi mất đi ý nghĩa với chính cộng đồng.

lines.t: Can technology help preserve heritage?
lines.vi: Công nghệ có giúp bảo tồn di sản không?

lines.t: Enormously. Digitising manuscripts and 3D-scanning monuments means that even if the original is damaged, detailed records survive. But a recording of a song isn’t the same as people still singing it, so technology complements living traditions rather than replacing them.
lines.vi: Rất nhiều. Số hoá bản thảo và quét 3D di tích nghĩa là kể cả khi bản gốc hư hại, hồ sơ chi tiết vẫn còn. Nhưng bản ghi một bài hát không giống việc người ta vẫn hát nó, nên công nghệ bổ trợ chứ không thay thế truyền thống sống.

gram2.title: Substitution and ellipsis
gram2.rule: do so / doing so · one / ones · so / not after think, hope, expect · the former / the latter · that of / those of
gram2.note: Repeating the same words makes writing heavy. Use do so to replace a verb phrase: Many want to visit the site, but few are permitted to do so. Use one(s) for countable nouns, and that of / those of to avoid repeating a noun in comparisons: The population of Hanoi is larger than that of Hue. In speech, I think so / I hope not are natural short answers.

ex.t: Some villages have kept their crafts alive; others have failed to do so.

cue.card: Describe a traditional skill or craft from your country.
points: what the skill or craft is
and explain why you think it should be preserved
model: I’d like to talk about Dong Ho woodblock printing, a folk art from a village of the same name in Bac Ninh province, about forty kilometres from Hanoi.

The prints are traditionally made for Tet and show simple, cheerful scenes — pigs with piglets, children with toads, a mouse wedding — each of which carries a wish for prosperity or happiness. What makes them special is the process. The paper, called “điệp”, is made from the bark of a local tree and coated with powdered seashells, which gives it a slightly sparkling surface. The colours all come from natural sources: black from burnt bamboo leaves, red from a type of gravel, yellow from flowers. Each colour is printed with a separate carved wooden block, one after another, so a single picture might require four or five blocks.

Unfortunately, it’s an endangered craft. Decades ago, almost every family in the village produced prints; now only a couple of families, most of whose members are elderly, still do so. I think it deserves to be preserved for two reasons. It’s a record of how ordinary people lived and what they hoped for, which official history rarely captures. And it’s a genuinely sustainable art form, made entirely from local, natural materials — something that seems more relevant now than ever.

write.prompt: The table shows the number of visitors (in thousands) to four heritage sites in a country, and the percentage who were international tourists, in 2010 and 2024. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
write.data:
Site              Visitors 2010   Visitors 2024   International 2010   International 2024
Ancient citadel   850             1,900           62%                  41%
Royal tombs       400             520             70%                  68%
Hill temple       120             760             15%                  12%
Old trading port  1,100           1,350           55%                  72%
plan: Introduction: paraphrase both measures
Overview: all sites grew; hill temple fastest proportionally, citadel largest absolute; international share fell at three sites but rose at the port
Body 1: visitor numbers — compare growth rates and rankings
Body 2: international share — domestic tourism boom at citadel vs port becoming more international
model: The table compares visitor numbers at four heritage sites in a particular country in 2010 and 2024, together with the proportion of those visitors who came from abroad.

Overall, every site attracted more visitors in 2024 than in 2010, with the ancient citadel and the hill temple growing most rapidly. Meanwhile, the share of international tourists fell at three of the four sites, suggesting that much of the growth came from domestic tourism, the only exception being the old trading port.

The ancient citadel saw the largest increase in absolute terms, with visitor numbers more than doubling from 850,000 to 1.9 million, which made it the most visited site by 2024, overtaking the old trading port. The most dramatic growth in relative terms, however, was at the hill temple, where attendance rose more than sixfold, from 120,000 to 760,000. By contrast, the royal tombs and the trading port recorded more modest increases of around 30% and 23% respectively.

As for the origin of visitors, the citadel underwent the most marked shift: international tourists accounted for 62% of its visitors in 2010 but only 41% in 2024. The proportions at the royal tombs and the hill temple declined only marginally and remained very different from each other, at roughly two-thirds and one-eighth respectively. The old trading port moved in the opposite direction, with the international share rising from 55% to almost three-quarters.

gram.note: Band 7+ writing avoids repeating “cause” and “lead to”. Notice the direction: stem from, arise from and be attributable to go from effect back to cause (The pollution stems from dyeing). Give rise to, trigger, fuel and exacerbate go from cause to effect (Low prices fuel overconsumption). Exacerbate means “make a bad situation worse”.

lines.t: Mainly because clothes have become so cheap relative to income, and because fashion cycles have sped up dramatically — some brands release new designs every week. Social media also plays a role; people feel they can’t be photographed in the same outfit twice.
lines.vi: Chủ yếu vì quần áo trở nên quá rẻ so với thu nhập, và vì chu kỳ thời trang tăng tốc chóng mặt — một số thương hiệu ra mẫu mới mỗi tuần. Mạng xã hội cũng góp phần; người ta cảm thấy không thể bị chụp ảnh hai lần với cùng một bộ đồ.

lines.t: Primarily companies, I’d argue, because they decide what materials to use and how much to produce. Consumers have limited information — it’s almost impossible to know how a T-shirt was made. Laws requiring supply chain transparency and making producers responsible for recycling would change behaviour far faster than appeals to shoppers.
lines.vi: Tôi cho rằng chủ yếu là doanh nghiệp, vì họ quyết định dùng vật liệu gì và sản xuất bao nhiêu. Người tiêu dùng có ít thông tin — gần như không thể biết một chiếc áo phông được làm thế nào. Luật yêu cầu minh bạch chuỗi cung ứng và buộc nhà sản xuất chịu trách nhiệm tái chế sẽ thay đổi hành vi nhanh hơn nhiều so với kêu gọi người mua.

cue.card: Describe an item of clothing that you have kept for a long time.
points: and explain why you have kept it for so long
model: I’d like to talk about a dark green wool jacket that used to belong to my father. I’ve had it for about eight years, but it’s actually much older — he bought it in the early nineties when he worked in Russia for a couple of years.

He gave it to me when I moved to Hanoi for university, mainly because he said I’d need something warm for the northern winter and he no longer wore it. At first I thought it was rather old-fashioned, so it stayed in the wardrobe. Then a few years ago that style came back into fashion, and suddenly friends were asking where I’d bought it.

These days I wear it most weeks between December and February. I’ve kept it for several reasons. Practically, it’s far better made than anything I could buy at a similar price now — the stitching is still perfect after thirty years, which is quite a contrast to some fast-fashion shirts I’ve owned that lost their shape after a few washes. But the main reason is sentimental. It reminds me of my father’s stories about that period of his life, and in a sense it connects his youth with mine. It’s also made me think about how much of our clothing is designed to be disposable, as opposed to something you might pass on.

write.prompt: The fashion industry has become one of the world’s major polluters. What are the causes of this, and what measures could be taken to reduce the environmental impact of clothing?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase + outline causes (fast production model, synthetic materials, low recycling) and solutions (regulation, producer responsibility, consumer shift)
Body 1: causes — overproduction and short cycles; synthetic fibres and dyes; disposal problem; specific data
Body 2: solutions — extended producer responsibility; standards and transparency laws; durable design and repair; secondhand
Conclusion: systemic causes need systemic solutions
model: Clothing production has expanded dramatically in recent decades, and the industry is now responsible for a significant share of global pollution. This problem stems mainly from a business model based on rapid, high-volume production of cheap garments, combined with materials that are difficult to recycle. Addressing it will require regulation of producers as well as changes in consumer behaviour.

The principal cause is the rise of fast fashion. Many brands now release new collections every few weeks, which has given rise to a culture in which clothes are bought cheaply, worn a handful of times and discarded. Global production roughly doubled in the first fifteen years of this century, while the average number of times each garment was worn fell sharply. The materials themselves exacerbate the problem: polyester and other synthetic fibres are derived from oil and release microplastics when washed, while dyeing processes in some producing countries discharge toxic chemicals into rivers. Finally, less than one per cent of clothing material is recycled into new garments, so most ends up in landfill or is incinerated.

Several measures could reduce this impact. Firstly, governments could introduce extended producer responsibility schemes, whereby brands pay for the collection and recycling of the clothes they sell. This would give companies a financial incentive to design durable, recyclable products. Secondly, laws requiring supply chain transparency and enforcing environmental standards in factories would make it harder for firms to outsource pollution to countries with weak regulation. Consumers also have a role, for instance by buying fewer but better-quality items, repairing clothes and using secondhand or rental services, but such changes are more likely to spread if they are supported by pricing and policy rather than left to individual conscience.

In conclusion, the environmental damage caused by fashion is largely attributable to a system that rewards overproduction and disposability. Since the causes are structural, the most effective solutions are likely to be regulatory, making producers responsible for the full life cycle of their products, while encouraging consumers to value durability over novelty.

lines.vi: Với tôi là người dễ gần, đưa ra mục tiêu rõ ràng rồi tin tưởng bạn đạt được. Những người quản lý tệ nhất tôi từng gặp là những người can thiệp vào mọi thứ.

sents.t: A large study by a technology company examined more than 180 of its internal teams to find out why some performed better than others.
sents.vi: Một nghiên cứu lớn của một công ty công nghệ khảo sát hơn 180 nhóm nội bộ để tìm hiểu vì sao một số nhóm làm việc tốt hơn.

sents.t: Researchers expected that the best teams would contain the most talented or experienced individuals.
sents.vi: Các nhà nghiên cứu từng nghĩ các nhóm tốt nhất sẽ gồm những cá nhân tài năng hoặc giàu kinh nghiệm nhất.

sents.t: Instead, the most important factor was psychological safety: whether members felt able to take risks and admit mistakes without being embarrassed.
sents.vi: Thay vào đó, yếu tố quan trọng nhất là an toàn tâm lý: các thành viên có cảm thấy dám chấp nhận rủi ro và thừa nhận lỗi mà không bị xấu hổ hay không.

sents.t: Teams in which everyone spoke roughly equally also tended to perform better.
sents.vi: Các nhóm mà mọi người phát biểu tương đối ngang nhau cũng có xu hướng làm việc tốt hơn.

sents.t: The findings suggest that a leader’s main role may be to create the right conditions rather than to have all the answers.
sents.vi: Kết quả cho thấy vai trò chính của người lãnh đạo có thể là tạo điều kiện phù hợp hơn là có mọi câu trả lời.

q.q: The researchers’ original expectation was confirmed by the study.
Psychological safety was the most important factor in team performance.
The best teams had the smallest number of members.

gram.title: Verbs whose meaning changes with -ing or to
gram.rule: stop / remember / forget / try / regret / go on / mean + -ing vs + to
gram.note: With these verbs, the choice between -ing and to-infinitive changes the meaning. Remember doing = remember a past action; remember to do = not forget a duty. Stop doing = quit; stop to do = pause in order to do. Try doing = experiment; try to do = make an effort. Regret to inform is formal bad news. Go on to do = do something next.

ex.t: I remember meeting the CEO for the first time.
ex.vi: Tôi nhớ lần đầu gặp giám đốc điều hành.

ex.t: Remember to send the report before Friday.
ex.vi: Nhớ gửi báo cáo trước thứ Sáu.

ex.t: She stopped working late after her health suffered.
ex.vi: Cô ấy thôi làm muộn sau khi sức khoẻ bị ảnh hưởng.

ex.t: He started as an intern and went on to become director.
ex.vi: Anh ấy bắt đầu là thực tập sinh và sau đó trở thành giám đốc.

drill.t: I regret ___ him — he was a great boss.
drill.vi: Tôi tiếc vì đã không nghe anh ấy — anh ấy là sếp tuyệt vời.

drill.t: We stopped ___ a coffee on the way.
drill.vi: Chúng tôi dừng lại để uống cà phê trên đường.

drill.t: Try ___ the meeting shorter — it might help.
drill.vi: Thử làm cuộc họp ngắn hơn xem — có thể có ích.

drill.t: Don’t forget ___ the client tomorrow.
drill.vi: Đừng quên gọi khách hàng ngày mai.

lines.t: Are leaders born or made?
lines.vi: Lãnh đạo là bẩm sinh hay được đào tạo?

lines.t: Mostly made, I think. Some traits help — confidence, perhaps charisma — but the skills that matter most, like listening, giving constructive feedback and making decisions with incomplete information, can be learned. Some of the most effective leaders I’ve seen were quite introverted.
lines.vi: Chủ yếu là được rèn luyện, tôi nghĩ vậy. Một số tố chất có ích — sự tự tin, có lẽ cả sức hút — nhưng những kỹ năng quan trọng nhất như lắng nghe, góp ý xây dựng và ra quyết định khi thông tin chưa đầy đủ đều học được. Một số nhà lãnh đạo hiệu quả nhất tôi từng thấy khá hướng nội.

lines.t: Is a strict hierarchy good for a company?
lines.vi: Cấp bậc nghiêm ngặt có tốt cho công ty không?

lines.t: In some situations — the military, or an emergency in a hospital — clear lines of authority save lives. But in creative or technical work, a rigid hierarchy tends to discourage junior staff from speaking up, and the people closest to a problem often have the best ideas.
lines.vi: Trong một số tình huống — quân đội, hay cấp cứu ở bệnh viện — tuyến quyền hạn rõ ràng cứu người. Nhưng trong công việc sáng tạo hay kỹ thuật, cấp bậc cứng nhắc thường khiến nhân viên cấp dưới ngại lên tiếng, trong khi người gần vấn đề nhất thường có ý tưởng tốt nhất.

lines.t: Should political leaders have a background in business?
lines.vi: Lãnh đạo chính trị có nên có nền tảng kinh doanh?

lines.t: It can help with managing budgets, but governing isn’t the same as running a company. A business can choose its customers; a government has to serve everyone, including people who will never be profitable. So I’d value integrity and the ability to build consensus more than business experience.
lines.vi: Nó có thể giúp quản lý ngân sách, nhưng điều hành đất nước không giống điều hành công ty. Doanh nghiệp có thể chọn khách hàng; chính phủ phải phục vụ tất cả, kể cả những người không bao giờ sinh lời. Nên tôi coi trọng sự chính trực và khả năng xây dựng đồng thuận hơn kinh nghiệm kinh doanh.

gram2.title: Describing character precisely
gram2.rule: compound adjectives: level-headed, strong-willed, open-minded, self-assured · adverb + adjective: deeply committed, genuinely interested, remarkably patient
gram2.note: Part 2 often asks you to describe a person. Instead of “nice” or “kind”, use precise compound adjectives and adverb–adjective collocations. Support each quality with a brief example: She is remarkably patient — she once explained the same process to me five times without any sign of irritation.

ex.t: My first manager was remarkably level-headed in a crisis.
ex.vi: Người quản lý đầu tiên của tôi điềm tĩnh lạ thường trong khủng hoảng.

ex.t: She is strong-willed but genuinely open-minded.
ex.vi: Cô ấy có ý chí mạnh mẽ nhưng thực sự cởi mở.

ex.t: He is deeply committed to his team’s development.
ex.vi: Anh ấy hết lòng với sự phát triển của đội.

ex.t: Our director is approachable and self-assured.
ex.vi: Giám đốc của chúng tôi dễ gần và tự tin.

drill.t: He never panics; he is very ___.
drill.vi: Anh ấy không bao giờ hoảng; anh ấy rất điềm tĩnh.

drill.t: She listens to all opinions; she is ___.
drill.vi: Cô ấy lắng nghe mọi ý kiến; cô ấy cởi mở.

drill.t: He is ___ committed to the project.
drill.vi: Anh ấy hết lòng với dự án.

drill.t: She won’t give up easily; she is ___.
drill.vi: Cô ấy không dễ bỏ cuộc; cô ấy có ý chí mạnh mẽ.

cue.card: Describe a person you have worked or studied with who was a good leader.
points: what they did as a leader
and explain why you think they were a good leader
model: I’d like to talk about Ms Thu, who was the project director on the first major building I worked on after graduating — a fifteen-storey office block in Da Nang.

About halfway through the project, we discovered that some of the foundation tests had been done incorrectly by a subcontractor, which meant a three-week delay and a serious risk of going over budget. I remember thinking the whole team would be blamed, and morale dropped sharply.

What she did impressed me enormously. First, she stayed remarkably level-headed — she called a meeting the same afternoon and simply laid out the facts without blaming anyone. Then she asked each of us, including the most junior engineers like me, for ideas on how to recover time, and two of the solutions we eventually used came from people who would never normally have spoken in that kind of meeting. Finally, she went to the client herself and took full accountability, rather than sending someone else. I think she was a good leader because she created what researchers call psychological safety: people weren’t afraid to admit mistakes or suggest ideas. I remember being surprised that a senior person would ask my opinion, and I’ve tried to lead my own small team the same way since then.

write.prompt: The pie charts show the results of a survey of employees in one company about their satisfaction with management in 2015 and 2025. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
write.data:
Rating               2015    2025
Very satisfied        12%     31%
Satisfied             28%     39%
Neutral               25%     15%
Dissatisfied          23%     10%
Very dissatisfied     12%      5%
plan: Introduction: paraphrase (survey of employees, satisfaction with management)
Overview: marked improvement; satisfied groups rose from 40% to 70%; dissatisfied halved+
Body 1: positive ratings — very satisfied nearly tripled; satisfied rose
Body 2: neutral and negative — all declined; combine to show the reversal
model: The two pie charts compare how satisfied employees in a particular company were with its management in 2015 and 2025.

Overall, attitudes towards management improved considerably over the decade. While only two-fifths of staff expressed satisfaction in 2015, this proportion had risen to seven in ten by 2025, and the share of dissatisfied employees fell sharply.

The most striking change was in the “very satisfied” category, which accounted for just 12% of responses in 2015 but almost tripled to 31% ten years later. The proportion who were satisfied also grew, from 28% to 39%, so that together these two groups rose from 40% to 70% of the workforce.

Meanwhile, every other category declined. The share of neutral responses dropped from a quarter to 15%. Dissatisfaction decreased even more markedly: the percentage of employees who were dissatisfied more than halved, from 23% to 10%, and the proportion who were very dissatisfied fell from 12% to only 5%. As a result, negative ratings, which had made up over a third of responses in 2015, accounted for just 15% in 2025.

units.title: Volunteering & civic life
units.goal: Discuss community involvement and civic duty, using advanced passives and synthesising language.

words.ex: She volunteers at an animal shelter.
words.exVi: Cô ấy làm tình nguyện ở trại cứu hộ động vật.

words.ex: Voting is a civic duty.
words.exVi: Bỏ phiếu là nghĩa vụ công dân.

words.vi: từ cơ sở, từ người dân
words.ex: A grassroots campaign cleaned up the river.
words.exVi: Một chiến dịch từ người dân đã làm sạch dòng sông.

words.ex: She works for a non-profit organisation.
words.exVi: Cô ấy làm cho một tổ chức phi lợi nhuận.

words.ex: Volunteering strengthens social cohesion.
words.exVi: Tình nguyện củng cố sự gắn kết xã hội.

words.ex: He wanted to give back to his community.
words.exVi: Anh ấy muốn đóng góp lại cho cộng đồng.

words.ex: Not all volunteering is pure altruism.
words.exVi: Không phải mọi hoạt động tình nguyện đều hoàn toàn vị tha.

words.vi: phục vụ cộng đồng bắt buộc
words.ex: Some schools require compulsory community service.
words.exVi: Một số trường yêu cầu phục vụ cộng đồng bắt buộc.

words.ex: Civil society groups monitor public spending.
words.exVi: Các nhóm xã hội dân sự giám sát chi tiêu công.

words.vi: hoạt động từ thiện (quy mô lớn)
words.ex: Philanthropy funded the new hospital wing.
words.exVi: Hoạt động từ thiện đã tài trợ khu mới của bệnh viện.

words.ex: Volunteers joined the disaster relief effort.
words.exVi: Tình nguyện viên tham gia nỗ lực cứu trợ thảm hoạ.

words.ex: Volunteering gives a sense of belonging.
words.exVi: Tình nguyện mang lại cảm giác thuộc về.

words.vi: tỉ lệ tham gia (bầu cử, sự kiện)
words.ex: Voter turnout was low among young people.
words.exVi: Tỉ lệ đi bầu thấp ở người trẻ.

words.ex: Political apathy is common among the young.
words.exVi: Sự thờ ơ chính trị phổ biến ở người trẻ.

words.ex: Residents signed a petition against the plan.
words.exVi: Cư dân ký kiến nghị phản đối kế hoạch.

words.ex: Social media mobilised thousands of volunteers.
words.exVi: Mạng xã hội huy động hàng nghìn tình nguyện viên.

words.ex: Some corporate volunteering is tokenistic.
words.exVi: Một số hoạt động tình nguyện của doanh nghiệp chỉ mang tính hình thức.

words.ex: All things considered, the scheme was a success.
words.exVi: Xét mọi mặt, chương trình đã thành công.

words.vi: nhìn chung, cân nhắc tổng thể
words.ex: On balance, I support the proposal.
words.exVi: Nhìn chung, tôi ủng hộ đề xuất.

words.ex: More needs to be done to support carers.
words.exVi: Cần làm nhiều hơn để hỗ trợ người chăm sóc.

lines.t: Have you ever done any volunteer work?
lines.vi: Bạn đã bao giờ làm tình nguyện chưa?

lines.t: Yes, during university I spent two summers teaching English to children in a mountainous district of Lao Cai. It was exhausting but probably the most meaningful thing I did as a student.
lines.vi: Có, thời đại học tôi dành hai mùa hè dạy tiếng Anh cho trẻ em ở một huyện miền núi Lào Cai. Rất mệt nhưng có lẽ là điều ý nghĩa nhất tôi làm khi còn là sinh viên.

lines.t: Do people in your country often help their neighbours?
lines.vi: Người dân nước bạn có hay giúp hàng xóm không?

lines.t: In villages, definitely — there’s a strong sense of community. In city apartment buildings it’s less common, though during the floods a few years ago, our building organised itself remarkably quickly.
lines.vi: Ở làng quê thì chắc chắn — có ý thức cộng đồng mạnh. Ở chung cư thành phố thì ít hơn, dù trong đợt lũ vài năm trước, toà nhà chúng tôi tự tổ chức nhanh đáng kinh ngạc.

lines.t: Would you like to volunteer in the future?
lines.vi: Bạn có muốn làm tình nguyện trong tương lai không?

lines.t: I would. I’d like to use my engineering skills, perhaps helping to design safer schools in flood-prone areas, rather than just doing general tasks.
lines.vi: Có. Tôi muốn dùng kỹ năng kỹ thuật, có lẽ giúp thiết kế trường học an toàn hơn ở vùng hay lũ, thay vì chỉ làm việc chung chung.

sents.t: A long-term study of older adults found that those who volunteered regularly reported higher life satisfaction and lower rates of depression.
sents.vi: Một nghiên cứu dài hạn về người cao tuổi cho thấy những người tình nguyện thường xuyên báo cáo mức hài lòng cuộc sống cao hơn và tỉ lệ trầm cảm thấp hơn.

sents.t: They also appeared to live slightly longer, even after differences in income and health were taken into account.
sents.vi: Họ cũng có vẻ sống lâu hơn một chút, ngay cả sau khi đã tính đến khác biệt về thu nhập và sức khoẻ.

sents.t: However, the benefits were only found among people whose main motivation was helping others.
sents.vi: Tuy nhiên, lợi ích chỉ thấy ở những người có động lực chính là giúp đỡ người khác.

sents.t: Those who volunteered mainly to improve their own situation showed no difference compared with non-volunteers.
sents.vi: Những người tình nguyện chủ yếu để cải thiện tình cảnh bản thân không có khác biệt so với người không tình nguyện.

sents.t: The researchers caution that the study shows a correlation and cannot prove that volunteering itself caused the improvements.
sents.vi: Các nhà nghiên cứu lưu ý nghiên cứu chỉ cho thấy tương quan và không thể chứng minh chính việc tình nguyện gây ra sự cải thiện.

q.q: The health benefits were found among all volunteers, whatever their motivation.
The study cannot prove that volunteering caused the benefits.
Most of the volunteers in the study worked in hospitals.

gram.title: Advanced passive forms
gram.rule: modal + be + past participle · needs + to be + past participle · passive infinitive (to be done) · passive gerund (being done) · perfect passive (having been done) · get + past participle
gram.note: Beyond basic tenses, the passive appears with infinitives and gerunds. Use the passive gerund after verbs and prepositions: Nobody likes being told what to do. Use the perfect passive participle for an earlier completed action: Having been trained, the volunteers were sent to the villages. Get-passives are informal and often describe something unexpected: He got injured.

ex.t: More needs to be done to support young carers.
ex.vi: Cần làm nhiều hơn để hỗ trợ người chăm sóc trẻ tuổi.

ex.t: Many volunteers dislike being treated as free labour.
ex.vi: Nhiều tình nguyện viên không thích bị đối xử như lao động miễn phí.

ex.t: Having been trained, the volunteers were sent to the shelters.
ex.vi: Sau khi được đào tạo, tình nguyện viên được cử đến các điểm trú ẩn.

ex.t: The scheme is expected to be extended next year.
ex.vi: Chương trình dự kiến sẽ được mở rộng năm sau.

drill.t: The roof needs ___ before the rainy season.
drill.vi: Mái nhà cần được sửa trước mùa mưa.

drill.t: She hates ___ in front of others.
drill.vi: Cô ấy ghét bị chỉ trích trước mặt người khác.

drill.t: ___ selected, the students began their project.
drill.vi: Sau khi được chọn, các sinh viên bắt đầu dự án.

drill.t: The results are expected ___ next month.
drill.vi: Kết quả dự kiến được công bố tháng sau.

lines.t: Should volunteering be compulsory for students?
lines.vi: Có nên bắt buộc học sinh làm tình nguyện?

lines.t: I’m in two minds. Compulsory schemes introduce young people to causes they might never have discovered, and some go on to volunteer for life. But if it becomes just another box to tick, it can feel tokenistic, and organisations end up with unmotivated helpers. On balance, I’d make it available and well-supported rather than compulsory.
lines.vi: Tôi phân vân. Chương trình bắt buộc giới thiệu cho người trẻ những mục đích họ có thể không bao giờ tự khám phá, và một số người sau đó tình nguyện suốt đời. Nhưng nếu nó chỉ là một ô cần đánh dấu, nó có thể mang tính hình thức, và các tổ chức nhận về những người giúp thiếu động lực. Nhìn chung, tôi sẽ tạo cơ hội và hỗ trợ tốt hơn là bắt buộc.

lines.t: Why are some young people uninterested in politics?
lines.vi: Vì sao một số người trẻ không quan tâm chính trị?

lines.t: I’m not sure it’s really apathy. Many young people are very engaged with specific issues — climate, animal welfare — and they’ll sign petitions or join campaigns. What they’re less interested in is traditional party politics, partly because they feel it doesn’t represent them.
lines.vi: Tôi không chắc đó thực sự là thờ ơ. Nhiều người trẻ rất quan tâm đến những vấn đề cụ thể — khí hậu, phúc lợi động vật — và họ sẽ ký kiến nghị hay tham gia chiến dịch. Điều họ ít quan tâm là chính trị đảng phái truyền thống, một phần vì họ cảm thấy nó không đại diện cho họ.

lines.t: Can volunteers replace paid professionals?
lines.vi: Tình nguyện viên có thể thay thế người làm chuyên nghiệp được trả lương không?

lines.t: They shouldn’t. Volunteers can add a great deal — time, local knowledge, human contact — but services like nursing or disaster relief need trained, accountable staff. Relying on goodwill is also unreliable; people’s availability changes.
lines.vi: Không nên. Tình nguyện viên có thể đóng góp rất nhiều — thời gian, hiểu biết địa phương, sự gần gũi — nhưng các dịch vụ như điều dưỡng hay cứu trợ thảm hoạ cần nhân viên được đào tạo và chịu trách nhiệm. Dựa vào thiện chí cũng không ổn định; thời gian rảnh của người ta thay đổi.

gram2.title: Synthesising and concluding
gram2.rule: All things considered, … · On balance, … · Ultimately, … · Taking everything into account, … · The key issue is not X but Y · It follows that …
gram2.note: A strong conclusion does more than repeat the introduction: it weighs the arguments and shows which matters more. On balance and all things considered signal that you have compared both sides. The key issue is not … but … reframes the question at a higher level, which examiners reward. Avoid introducing new arguments in the conclusion.

ex.t: All things considered, the benefits clearly outweigh the costs.
ex.vi: Xét mọi mặt, lợi ích rõ ràng lớn hơn chi phí.

ex.t: On balance, voluntary schemes work better than compulsory ones.
ex.vi: Nhìn chung, chương trình tự nguyện hiệu quả hơn bắt buộc.

ex.t: The key issue is not whether people volunteer but how they are supported.
ex.vi: Vấn đề then chốt không phải là có tình nguyện hay không mà là được hỗ trợ ra sao.

ex.t: Ultimately, a healthy society depends on active citizens.
ex.vi: Suy cho cùng, một xã hội lành mạnh dựa vào công dân tích cực.

drill.t: ___ balance, I support the idea.
drill.vi: Nhìn chung, tôi ủng hộ ý tưởng.

drill.t: All things ___, it was a success.
drill.vi: Xét mọi mặt, đó là một thành công.

drill.t: The key issue is not cost ___ quality.
drill.vi: Vấn đề then chốt không phải chi phí mà là chất lượng.

drill.t: Taking everything into ___, the plan is sound.
drill.vi: Xét tổng thể, kế hoạch hợp lý.

cue.card: Describe a time when you helped someone in your community.
points: and explain how you felt about helping
model: I’d like to describe something that happened during the floods in central Vietnam in 2020, when I was working in Hue for a few months on a construction project.

The rain went on for almost two weeks, and the area around the old citadel flooded badly. An elderly couple who lived on the ground floor of the house next to my rented room couldn’t leave — the husband had difficulty walking, and their children lived in Ho Chi Minh City. On the third morning the water was up to my knees inside their house, and their electricity had been cut off.

Together with two colleagues, I helped them move their most important belongings — family photographs, the ancestral altar, their documents — up to the second floor of a neighbour’s house, and for about a week we brought them meals and drinking water, which had been delivered to our site by the company. It wasn’t heroic; it was just a matter of being physically close and able to help. How did I feel? Honestly, more uncomfortable than proud, because it made me realise how vulnerable older people living alone are when public services are overwhelmed. All things considered, it was one of the experiences that made me think seriously about volunteering in a more organised way, and it’s why I’d now like to use my engineering skills to help design flood-resilient housing.

write.prompt: Some people think that all young people should be required to do unpaid work in their communities, for example helping the elderly or protecting the environment. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase + position (disagree with compulsion; support strongly encouraged, flexible, recognised schemes)
Body 1: arguments for compulsion — civic awareness, social cohesion, practical benefits; acknowledge fully
Body 2: arguments against — undermines motivation, tokenism, burden on poor students, displaces paid jobs; evidence on motivation
Conclusion: synthesise — the key issue is engagement, not attendance
model: It has been suggested that every young person should be obliged to carry out unpaid work for their community, such as caring for older people or taking part in environmental projects. While I fully agree that young people benefit from such experiences, I disagree that participation should be compulsory, because enforced volunteering tends to undermine the very motivation that makes it valuable.

The case for a requirement is not without merit. Community work exposes young people to sections of society they might otherwise never encounter, which can build empathy and a sense of civic duty. It can also strengthen social cohesion, particularly in ageing societies where isolated elderly people would benefit from regular contact with younger generations. In addition, young people often gain practical skills, from teamwork to problem-solving, that make them more employable. Some schools that have introduced service requirements report that a proportion of students continue volunteering long after they are obliged to.

However, making such work mandatory raises significant problems. Research on volunteering suggests that its benefits, both for the volunteer and for the people helped, depend heavily on genuine motivation; when participation is enforced, it risks becoming a box-ticking exercise in which young people simply attend without engaging. A compulsory scheme would also place a disproportionate burden on students from low-income families, many of whom already work part-time to support themselves or their relatives. Moreover, if large numbers of unpaid young people are deployed in care or environmental work, there is a danger that they will be used to replace paid professionals, reducing both the quality of services and the number of jobs available.

All things considered, I believe the key issue is not whether young people are made to do community work but whether they are given real opportunities and reasons to do so. On balance, governments and schools should encourage participation through flexible programmes, academic credit and recognition by employers, rather than imposing a requirement that may produce attendance without commitment.

lines.t: Which do you find more productive?

lines.t: For focused tasks like writing reports, home is far better — there are fewer interruptions. But for anything that requires collaboration, I’d rather be in the room, because a two-minute chat often solves what would take ten emails.

lines.t: Is there anything you dislike about working from home?

sents.t: Fully remote work, however, produced more mixed results, particularly for newer employees who missed out on informal learning.

gram.title: Cleft sentences for emphasis
gram.rule: What + clause + is/was + focus · It is/was + focus + that/who + clause · The reason (why) … is that …
gram.note: Cleft sentences split one idea into two clauses to highlight the key information, a feature examiners associate with band 8 flexibility: What remote workers miss most is informal mentoring. It is junior staff who suffer most from isolation. Don’t overuse them — one or two per answer is enough.

lines.t: Why do some employers insist on staff being in the office?

lines.t: There are legitimate reasons — mentoring and spontaneous collaboration genuinely suffer online. But I suspect that in some cases it’s presenteeism: managers who were trained to judge people by visibility rather than outcomes feel uneasy when they can’t see their team.
lines.vi: Có những lý do chính đáng — kèm cặp và cộng tác ngẫu hứng thật sự bị ảnh hưởng khi làm trực tuyến. Nhưng tôi ngờ rằng đôi khi đó là văn hoá có mặt cho có: những quản lý quen đánh giá người khác qua sự hiện diện thay vì kết quả thấy bất an khi không nhìn thấy nhóm mình.

lines.t: How might remote work change cities?

lines.t: It could be transformative. If fewer people commute, city centres built around offices will need to reinvent themselves — perhaps converting office space into housing — while smaller towns could benefit as people move somewhere cheaper and greener.

lines.t: I’d support it. What technology has done is make work available everywhere and at all times, so some legal protection seems reasonable to prevent burnout, although it would need exceptions for genuine emergencies.

cue.card: Describe a place where you like to work or study, other than your home.
points: and explain why you work well there
model: I’d like to talk about a small co-working café near my office in District 3, which has become my favourite place to work on the days I’m not required in the office.

It’s on the first floor of an old French-style villa, so it has high ceilings, tall wooden shutters and a huge mango tree outside the windows. Downstairs is a normal café, but upstairs they’ve set up long shared tables with sockets every half metre, plus a few phone booths for calls.
I go there roughly once a week, usually on Fridays. It costs about the same as two coffees, and I can stay all day.

What makes me productive there is a combination of things. At home the boundaries between work and life are blurred — I end up doing the laundry or checking my phone in bed. In the office, on the other hand, I’m constantly interrupted. The café sits nicely in between: there’s a quiet hum of other people working, which somehow puts gentle pressure on me to focus, but nobody knows me, so nobody interrupts. It’s also where I’ve met a few freelancers and digital nomads, and those conversations have given me ideas I would never have come across in my own company.

write.prompt: Some people believe that working from home benefits both employees and employers, while others think it causes more problems than it solves. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
plan: Introduction: paraphrase; opinion — a hybrid model captures most benefits
Body 1: benefits — time and money saved, focus and autonomy, wider talent pool, lower costs
Body 2: problems — isolation and weaker mentoring, blurred boundaries and burnout, collaboration, city economies
Body 3 / own view: hybrid, outcome-based management, right to disconnect
Conclusion
model: The shift towards working from home, accelerated by the pandemic, has divided opinion. Some regard it as a clear improvement for both staff and organisations, whereas others believe its costs outweigh its advantages. In my view, while fully remote work does create significant problems, a well-managed hybrid arrangement offers the best of both worlds.

The case for remote work is persuasive. Employees save time and money by avoiding long commutes, which in congested cities can amount to two hours a day, and many report being able to concentrate better on demanding tasks away from the interruptions of an open-plan office. Greater autonomy over when and where they work is also strongly linked to job satisfaction. Employers, for their part, can recruit from a far wider talent pool, reduce spending on office space and, according to several studies, retain staff for longer.

Nevertheless, the drawbacks are real. It is junior employees who tend to lose out most, since much professional learning happens informally, through overheard conversations and spontaneous advice from experienced colleagues. Remote workers may also experience isolation, and when the kitchen table becomes the office, the boundaries between work and private life become blurred, increasing the risk of burnout. Some forms of creative collaboration are also harder to replicate on video calls. At a wider level, city-centre businesses that depend on office workers have suffered.

What these arguments suggest, in my opinion, is that the question is not whether people should work from home but how. A hybrid model, in which teams meet in person for collaboration and mentoring but work remotely for focused tasks, captures most of the benefits while limiting the harms. This works best when managers judge staff on outcomes rather than visibility and when firms respect employees’ right to disconnect outside working hours.

In conclusion, working from home brings substantial advantages but also genuine risks, particularly for newer staff and for wellbeing. A carefully designed hybrid approach is, I believe, the most sensible way forward.

read.title: The promise and limits of MOOCs

sents.t: When massive open online courses appeared around 2012, enthusiasts predicted that they would make traditional universities obsolete.
sents.vi: Khi khoá học trực tuyến mở đại trà xuất hiện khoảng năm 2012, những người hào hứng dự đoán chúng sẽ khiến đại học truyền thống lỗi thời.

sents.t: A decade later, average completion rates remain in single figures.
sents.vi: Một thập kỷ sau, tỉ lệ hoàn thành trung bình vẫn dưới mười phần trăm.

sents.t: Moreover, most learners who finish MOOCs already hold a degree, suggesting that online courses have so far benefited the educated more than the disadvantaged.
sents.vi: Hơn nữa, phần lớn người học hoàn thành đã có bằng đại học, cho thấy khoá trực tuyến đến nay có lợi cho người có học vấn hơn người thiệt thòi.

sents.t: Researchers have found that adding deadlines, small study groups and occasional contact with tutors significantly improves completion.
sents.vi: Nhà nghiên cứu phát hiện thêm hạn chót, nhóm học nhỏ và đôi lúc liên hệ với trợ giảng giúp cải thiện tỉ lệ hoàn thành đáng kể.

sents.t: Many universities now use online material as part of blended programmes rather than as a replacement for teaching.
sents.vi: Nhiều trường đại học nay dùng tài liệu trực tuyến như một phần chương trình kết hợp thay vì thay thế giảng dạy.

q.q: MOOCs have replaced most traditional universities.
Most people who complete MOOCs are already graduates.
MOOCs are more popular in Asia than in Europe.

gram.title: Negative inversion for emphasis
gram.rule: Not only + auxiliary + subject …, but … also · Rarely / Seldom / Never + auxiliary + subject · Only when / Only by … + auxiliary + subject
gram.note: After a negative or restrictive adverbial at the start of a sentence, invert the subject and auxiliary, as in a question. Use it sparingly in formal speaking and writing for emphasis: Not only is online learning cheaper, but it is also more flexible. Only when deadlines were added did completion rates improve.

ex.t: Not only is online study cheaper, but it is also more flexible.
ex.vi: Học trực tuyến không chỉ rẻ hơn mà còn linh hoạt hơn.

ex.t: Rarely do free courses have high completion rates.
ex.vi: Hiếm khi khoá học miễn phí có tỉ lệ hoàn thành cao.

ex.t: Only when tutors got involved did students stay motivated.
ex.vi: Chỉ khi có trợ giảng tham gia, học viên mới giữ được động lực.

ex.t: Never before has education been so accessible.
ex.vi: Chưa bao giờ giáo dục dễ tiếp cận đến vậy.

drill.vi: Học viên trực tuyến hiếm khi gặp nhau.

drill.t: Only by setting deadlines ___ improve completion.
drill.vi: Chỉ bằng cách đặt hạn chót, ta mới cải thiện được tỉ lệ hoàn thành.

lines.t: Will online learning replace traditional schools?
lines.vi: Học trực tuyến có thay thế trường học truyền thống không?

lines.t: I very much doubt it, at least for children. Schools don’t just transmit knowledge; they teach social skills, provide supervision so parents can work and, for poorer children, sometimes provide the only reliable meal of the day. Not only would remote schooling widen the digital divide, but it would also deprive children of those things.
lines.vi: Tôi rất nghi ngờ, ít nhất với trẻ em. Trường học không chỉ truyền kiến thức; nó dạy kỹ năng xã hội, trông nom để cha mẹ đi làm và với trẻ nghèo, đôi khi là bữa ăn ổn định duy nhất trong ngày. Học từ xa không chỉ nới rộng khoảng cách số mà còn tước đi những điều đó của trẻ.

lines.t: Who benefits most from online education?
lines.vi: Ai được lợi nhiều nhất từ giáo dục trực tuyến?

lines.t: Probably motivated adults who already have some education — people who want to upskill around a full-time job. Ironically, the groups it was supposed to help most, such as rural learners, often lack the devices, connection or quiet space that make it work.
lines.vi: Có lẽ là người lớn có động lực và đã có nền tảng học vấn — những người muốn nâng kỹ năng bên cạnh công việc toàn thời gian. Trớ trêu là những nhóm nó được kỳ vọng giúp nhiều nhất, như người học nông thôn, thường thiếu thiết bị, kết nối hay không gian yên tĩnh.

lines.t: Are online qualifications as valuable as traditional ones?
lines.vi: Bằng cấp trực tuyến có giá trị như bằng truyền thống không?

lines.t: Increasingly, yes, especially in fields like IT where employers care about what you can do. But for professions requiring hands-on training, such as medicine or nursing, an online credential alone would never be enough.
lines.vi: Ngày càng có, nhất là ngành như CNTT nơi nhà tuyển dụng quan tâm bạn làm được gì. Nhưng với nghề cần thực hành trực tiếp như y khoa hay điều dưỡng, chứng chỉ trực tuyến thôi sẽ không bao giờ đủ.

gram2.title: Adjective + preposition for evaluation
gram2.rule: conducive to · detrimental to · beneficial to/for · effective in + -ing · dependent on · accessible to
gram2.note: Precise adjective + preposition combinations are a hallmark of academic style and a common source of errors. Learn them as units: conducive to learning, detrimental to concentration, effective in improving results.

ex.t: A quiet room is conducive to concentration.
ex.vi: Phòng yên tĩnh thuận lợi cho sự tập trung.

ex.t: Long hours of video calls are detrimental to wellbeing.
ex.vi: Họp video nhiều giờ có hại cho sức khoẻ tinh thần.

ex.t: Deadlines are effective in reducing dropout.
ex.vi: Hạn chót hiệu quả trong việc giảm bỏ học.

ex.t: Success is heavily dependent on self-discipline.
ex.vi: Thành công phụ thuộc nhiều vào tính tự giác.

drill.t: Noise is detrimental ___ learning.

drill.t: Group work is effective ___ building confidence.
drill.vi: Làm việc nhóm hiệu quả trong việc xây dựng tự tin.

drill.t: The course is accessible ___ anyone with a phone.
drill.vi: Khoá học mở cho bất kỳ ai có điện thoại.

drill.t: A calm space is conducive ___ study.
drill.vi: Không gian yên tĩnh thuận lợi cho việc học.

cue.card: Describe an online course or video that taught you something useful.
points: and explain why it was useful to you
model: I’d like to talk about a free online course on personal finance that I took about two years ago, offered by a university through one of the big MOOC platforms.

I came across it almost by accident. I’d been watching videos about saving money, and the algorithm recommended it. It was self-paced, about six weeks long, with short video lectures, quizzes and a final project in which you had to draw up a realistic budget for yourself.

I learned a surprising amount. The most eye-opening part was about compound interest — the lecturer showed how a small amount invested in your twenties can grow to be worth more than much larger amounts invested in your forties. I also learned how to read the small print on loans and how to recognise investment scams, which, unfortunately, are very common in Vietnam at the moment.

It was useful in a very practical sense. Not only did I start saving a fixed percentage of my salary, but I also talked my parents out of putting money into a scheme that promised unrealistic returns. What I appreciated most was that the course was completely free and accessible to anyone with an internet connection — although, to be honest, I only finished it because a friend took it with me and we kept each other motivated.

write.prompt: Online courses are becoming increasingly popular. Some people think they will eventually replace traditional face-to-face education. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase; position — largely disagree; online will complement, not replace
Body 1: why online is growing — cost, flexibility, scale, lifelong learning
Body 2: why it will not replace — completion and motivation, social and practical skills, digital divide, role of schools
Body 3: likely future — blended learning
Conclusion
model: Over the past decade, online courses have expanded rapidly, offering everything from short professional certificates to full degrees. This has led some to predict that face-to-face education will eventually become obsolete. While I accept that online learning will continue to grow, I largely disagree that it will replace traditional teaching.

There are clear reasons for the popularity of online education. It is often considerably cheaper than campus-based study, since it removes the costs of accommodation and travel and allows institutions to teach thousands of students at once. It is also flexible: working adults can upskill in the evenings, and learners in remote areas can access lectures from leading universities. In an economy where skills quickly become outdated, this makes lifelong learning far more realistic.

Nevertheless, there are strong reasons to believe that online courses will complement rather than replace face-to-face education. Firstly, completion rates for many online courses are strikingly low, which suggests that most learners need the structure, deadlines and personal relationships that classrooms provide. Secondly, education involves more than transferring information; schools and universities develop teamwork, communication and other social skills, and many subjects, from chemistry to nursing, require hands-on practice. Finally, relying on online provision would widen the digital divide, since poorer students are less likely to have reliable devices, internet access or a space conducive to study.

The most likely future, therefore, is one of blended learning, in which recorded lectures and online exercises free up classroom time for discussion, practical work and individual support. Not only does this approach use technology’s strengths, but it also retains the human interaction that remains essential to effective learning.

In conclusion, although online courses offer real advantages in cost and flexibility, they are unlikely to replace traditional education entirely. Instead, the two are set to merge into more flexible blended models.

units.title: Celebrity culture
units.goal: Discuss fame, influencers and role models, using modal perfects to speculate about and criticise past actions.

words.exVi: Người nổi tiếng có ảnh hưởng lớn đến người hâm mộ trẻ.

words.vi: sự sùng bái người nổi tiếng

words.exVi: Cô ấy được phát hiện qua chương trình tìm kiếm tài năng.

lines.t: Is there a famous person you admire?
lines.vi: Có người nổi tiếng nào bạn ngưỡng mộ không?

lines.t: I admire Son Doong’s explorers more than pop stars, to be honest. But if I had to pick a celebrity, it would be a footballer like Quang Hai, because he’s worked incredibly hard and seems to handle the spotlight well.
lines.vi: Thật lòng tôi ngưỡng mộ những nhà thám hiểm Sơn Đoòng hơn ngôi sao nhạc pop. Nhưng nếu phải chọn một người nổi tiếng, đó sẽ là cầu thủ như Quang Hải, vì anh ấy rất chăm chỉ và có vẻ chịu được áp lực dư luận tốt.

lines.t: Do you follow celebrities on social media?
lines.vi: Bạn có theo dõi người nổi tiếng trên mạng xã hội không?

lines.t: A few, mostly musicians. I used to follow lots of influencers, but I unfollowed many because their content felt shallow — mainly endorsements disguised as daily life.
lines.vi: Một vài người, chủ yếu là nhạc sĩ. Trước đây tôi theo nhiều người có ảnh hưởng, nhưng bỏ theo dõi nhiều vì nội dung có vẻ nông cạn — chủ yếu là quảng cáo đội lốt đời thường.

lines.t: Would you like to be famous?
lines.vi: Bạn có muốn nổi tiếng không?

lines.t: Not at all. Constant public scrutiny sounds exhausting, and I value being able to have a bad day without it ending up online.
lines.vi: Hoàn toàn không. Bị công chúng soi xét liên tục nghe rất mệt, và tôi trân trọng việc có một ngày tệ mà không bị đưa lên mạng.

sents.t: A survey of young people in several countries found that “becoming famous” ranked among their top three career ambitions.
sents.vi: Một khảo sát người trẻ ở nhiều nước cho thấy “trở nên nổi tiếng” nằm trong ba mong ước nghề nghiệp hàng đầu.

sents.t: Psychologists link this partly to social media, which makes fame appear achievable for anyone with a phone.
sents.vi: Các nhà tâm lý học cho rằng một phần là do mạng xã hội, khiến danh tiếng có vẻ trong tầm tay bất kỳ ai có điện thoại.

sents.t: Yet studies of people who achieve sudden fame report high levels of anxiety, loss of privacy and difficulty forming trusting relationships.
sents.vi: Tuy nhiên nghiên cứu về những người nổi tiếng đột ngột ghi nhận mức lo âu cao, mất riêng tư và khó xây dựng quan hệ tin cậy.

sents.t: Child stars are considered particularly vulnerable, since they become famous before they have developed a stable sense of identity.
sents.vi: Ngôi sao nhí được xem là đặc biệt dễ tổn thương, vì họ nổi tiếng trước khi hình thành bản sắc ổn định.

sents.t: Some countries have introduced laws requiring that a share of child influencers’ earnings be held in trust until they turn eighteen.
sents.vi: Một số nước đã ban hành luật yêu cầu một phần thu nhập của người có ảnh hưởng nhí phải được giữ lại đến khi họ đủ mười tám tuổi.

q.q: Fame is one of the top career goals for young people in the survey.
People who become famous suddenly usually report lower anxiety.
All countries now protect child influencers’ earnings by law.

gram.title: Modal perfects for speculation and criticism
gram.rule: must have / can’t have + past participle (deduction) · might / could have + p.p. (possibility) · should / shouldn’t have + p.p. (criticism)
gram.note: Modal perfects let you speculate about the past and judge past actions with precision: He must have known the photos were edited. She could have refused the endorsement. The company should have checked his background. Note: can’t have (not mustn’t have) for negative deduction.

ex.t: The star must have known the product was harmful.
ex.vi: Ngôi sao hẳn đã biết sản phẩm có hại.

ex.t: She can’t have written that post herself.
ex.vi: Cô ấy không thể tự viết bài đăng đó.

ex.t: He might have avoided the scandal if he had apologised sooner.
ex.vi: Anh ấy có lẽ đã tránh được bê bối nếu xin lỗi sớm hơn.

ex.t: The brand should have done more research.
ex.vi: Nhãn hàng lẽ ra phải tìm hiểu kỹ hơn.

lines.t: Why are people so interested in celebrities’ private lives?
lines.vi: Vì sao người ta quan tâm đến đời tư người nổi tiếng?

lines.t: Partly curiosity and partly something quite old — gossip has always been a way of bonding and discussing social norms. What’s new is the scale: social media gives the impression of intimacy, so fans develop parasocial relationships and feel entitled to know everything.
lines.vi: Một phần là tò mò và một phần là điều rất cũ — chuyện phiếm luôn là cách gắn kết và bàn luận chuẩn mực xã hội. Điều mới là quy mô: mạng xã hội tạo cảm giác thân mật, nên người hâm mộ hình thành quan hệ một chiều và cảm thấy có quyền biết mọi thứ.

lines.t: Do celebrities have a responsibility to be role models?
lines.vi: Người nổi tiếng có trách nhiệm làm hình mẫu không?

lines.t: To a degree. Nobody should be expected to be perfect, but if you earn money from the attention of millions of young fans, you can’t really claim your behaviour is purely private. Promoting gambling sites or dangerous diets, for instance, is hard to defend.
lines.vi: Ở mức độ nào đó. Không ai nên bị kỳ vọng hoàn hảo, nhưng nếu bạn kiếm tiền từ sự chú ý của hàng triệu fan trẻ, bạn khó mà nói hành vi của mình hoàn toàn riêng tư. Ví dụ quảng bá trang cờ bạc hay chế độ ăn nguy hiểm thì khó bào chữa.

lines.t: Is cancel culture a fair way of holding famous people accountable?
lines.vi: Văn hoá tẩy chay có phải cách công bằng để buộc người nổi tiếng chịu trách nhiệm không?

lines.t: It can expose genuine misconduct that the authorities ignored. The danger is that online mobs rarely wait for evidence, and the punishment is often out of proportion to the offence — someone might lose their career over a clumsy joke made ten years ago.
lines.vi: Nó có thể phơi bày hành vi sai trái thật mà chính quyền bỏ qua. Mối nguy là đám đông trên mạng hiếm khi chờ bằng chứng, và hình phạt thường không tương xứng với lỗi — ai đó có thể mất sự nghiệp vì một câu đùa vụng về mười năm trước.

gram2.title: Passive reporting of perception: be seen as, be regarded as, be perceived as
gram2.rule: be seen / regarded / viewed / perceived as + noun or adjective · be considered (to be) + adjective
gram2.note: These structures express how people generally view something without saying who holds the view, which is useful in formal discussion: Influencers are increasingly seen as entrepreneurs. Fame is often regarded as a reward in itself.

ex.t: Influencers are increasingly seen as entrepreneurs.
ex.vi: Người có ảnh hưởng ngày càng được xem là doanh nhân.

ex.t: Fame is widely regarded as desirable.
ex.vi: Danh tiếng được nhiều người coi là đáng mơ ước.

ex.t: His apology was perceived as insincere.
ex.vi: Lời xin lỗi của anh ấy bị coi là thiếu chân thành.

ex.t: Child stars are considered especially vulnerable.
