lines.t: Do you have a pet?
lines.vi: Bạn có nuôi thú cưng không?

lines.t: Not at the moment, though I grew up with a dog. I’d like a cat eventually, but I travel too much for work, and it wouldn’t be fair to leave an animal alone for days.
lines.vi: Hiện tại thì không, dù tôi lớn lên cùng một chú chó. Cuối cùng tôi muốn nuôi mèo, nhưng tôi đi công tác quá nhiều, và để một con vật ở nhà một mình nhiều ngày thì không công bằng.

lines.t: Do you think about where your meat comes from?
lines.vi: Bạn có nghĩ về nguồn gốc thịt mình ăn không?

lines.t: More than I used to. I buy free-range chicken when I can, and I eat meat less often, partly for my health and partly because I’ve become uncomfortable with how factory farming treats animals.
lines.vi: Nhiều hơn trước. Tôi mua gà thả vườn khi có thể, và ăn thịt ít thường xuyên hơn, một phần vì sức khoẻ và một phần vì tôi bắt đầu thấy không thoải mái với cách chăn nuôi công nghiệp đối xử với động vật.

lines.t: Are people in your country kind to animals?
lines.vi: Người dân nước bạn có tử tế với động vật không?

lines.t: Attitudes are changing quickly, especially among young people in cities, where pets are treated almost like family. A number of animal welfare groups have emerged in the last decade, which would have been unusual before.
lines.vi: Thái độ đang thay đổi nhanh, nhất là ở người trẻ thành thị, nơi thú cưng được đối xử gần như thành viên gia đình. Một số nhóm bảo vệ phúc lợi động vật đã ra đời trong thập kỷ qua, điều trước đây hiếm thấy.

sents.t: The number of animals used in scientific procedures in the European Union has fallen gradually over the past two decades.
sents.vi: Số lượng động vật dùng trong các quy trình khoa học ở Liên minh châu Âu đã giảm dần trong hai thập kỷ qua.

sents.t: New methods, such as “organs-on-chips” that grow human cells in tiny devices, can sometimes predict drug toxicity more accurately than animal tests.
sents.vi: Các phương pháp mới như “cơ quan trên chip”, nuôi tế bào người trong thiết bị siêu nhỏ, đôi khi dự đoán độc tính thuốc chính xác hơn thử nghiệm trên động vật.

sents.t: In 2022, the United States removed a legal requirement that new drugs be tested on animals before human trials.
sents.vi: Năm 2022, Hoa Kỳ bỏ yêu cầu pháp lý rằng thuốc mới phải được thử trên động vật trước thử nghiệm trên người.

sents.t: However, most researchers agree that some complex studies, such as those on the whole immune system, cannot yet be replaced.
sents.vi: Tuy nhiên, phần lớn nhà nghiên cứu đồng ý rằng một số nghiên cứu phức tạp, như về toàn bộ hệ miễn dịch, chưa thể thay thế.

sents.t: The goal for most regulators is therefore reduction and refinement rather than an immediate ban.
sents.vi: Vì vậy mục tiêu của phần lớn cơ quan quản lý là giảm thiểu và cải tiến chứ không phải cấm ngay lập tức.

q.q: The US removed the legal requirement for animal testing of new drugs in 2022.
Organs-on-chips can now replace all animal studies.
The EU plans to ban all animal testing by 2030.

gram.title: Paraphrasing techniques
gram.rule: change word form (protect → protection) · use synonyms carefully (harmful → detrimental) · change structure (active ↔ passive; clause ↔ noun phrase) · change the order of ideas
gram.note: Paraphrasing the question is essential in the introduction, and paraphrasing sources is essential in Reading. Combine at least two techniques; a synonym alone often changes the meaning. Keep technical terms that have no true synonym (animal testing). Original: Many people think animals should not be used in experiments. Paraphrase: It is widely argued that the use of animals in scientific research is unjustifiable.

ex.t: Original: Zoos protect endangered species. → Endangered species are protected by zoos.
ex.vi: Đổi chủ động sang bị động.

ex.t: Original: Factory farming is cruel. → The cruelty of factory farming is widely recognised.
ex.vi: Đổi tính từ thành danh từ.

ex.t: Original: Should animals have rights? → Whether animals should be granted rights is debated.
ex.vi: Đổi câu hỏi thành mệnh đề danh ngữ.

ex.t: Original: Testing on animals is decreasing. → There has been a decline in animal testing.
ex.vi: Đổi động từ thành danh từ.

drill.t: Best paraphrase of “animals suffer in farms”:
opts: animals suffer in farms a lot
drill.vi: Diễn đạt lại chính xác và tự nhiên nhất.

drill.t: Noun form of “protect”:
drill.vi: Danh từ của protect là protection.

drill.t: Passive of “Governments regulate zoos”:
drill.vi: Câu bị động đúng.

drill.t: Which keeps the meaning of “harmful”?
drill.vi: “Detrimental” giữ nghĩa “có hại”.

lines.t: Is it acceptable to use animals for medical research?
lines.vi: Dùng động vật cho nghiên cứu y học có chấp nhận được không?

lines.t: For serious medical research, where there’s genuinely no alternative, I find it reluctantly acceptable — many vaccines and treatments depend on it. But the burden of proof should be on the researchers, and the number of animals used ought to keep falling as alternatives like organs-on-chips improve. Testing cosmetics on animals, by contrast, seems impossible to justify.
lines.vi: Với nghiên cứu y học nghiêm túc mà thật sự không có phương án khác, tôi miễn cưỡng chấp nhận — nhiều vắc-xin và phương pháp điều trị phụ thuộc vào nó. Nhưng trách nhiệm chứng minh nên thuộc về nhà nghiên cứu, và số lượng động vật được dùng nên tiếp tục giảm khi các phương án như cơ quan trên chip cải thiện. Ngược lại, thử nghiệm mỹ phẩm trên động vật thì có vẻ không thể biện minh.

lines.t: Why do people treat some animals as pets and eat others?
lines.vi: Vì sao người ta coi một số loài là thú cưng nhưng lại ăn những loài khác?

lines.t: Largely culture and habit rather than any consistent principle. Pigs are at least as intelligent as dogs, yet in most countries one is family and the other is food. Philosophers call this inconsistency speciesism; I think most people simply avoid thinking about it too carefully.
lines.vi: Phần lớn do văn hoá và thói quen chứ không phải nguyên tắc nhất quán nào. Lợn ít nhất cũng thông minh như chó, nhưng ở hầu hết các nước, một loài là gia đình còn loài kia là thức ăn. Các triết gia gọi sự thiếu nhất quán này là phân biệt giống loài; tôi nghĩ phần lớn người ta đơn giản là tránh suy nghĩ quá kỹ về nó.

lines.t: Will attitudes to animals change in the future?
lines.vi: Thái độ với động vật sẽ thay đổi trong tương lai không?

lines.t: I suspect they’ll change considerably, partly for ethical reasons and partly practical ones. Factory farming carries real public-health risks, including zoonotic diseases, and as plant-based and cultivated meat become cheaper, future generations may look back on industrial livestock farming the way we look back on practices we now find unthinkable.
lines.vi: Tôi đoán chúng sẽ thay đổi đáng kể, một phần vì lý do đạo đức và một phần vì lý do thực tế. Chăn nuôi công nghiệp mang rủi ro sức khoẻ cộng đồng thật sự, bao gồm bệnh lây từ động vật, và khi thịt thực vật và thịt nuôi cấy rẻ hơn, các thế hệ tương lai có thể nhìn lại chăn nuôi công nghiệp như cách ta nhìn lại những tập quán giờ đây không thể tưởng tượng nổi.

gram2.title: Subject–verb agreement traps
gram2.rule: the number of + plural noun → singular verb · a number of → plural verb · one of the + plural noun → singular verb · each / every → singular · neither … nor → verb agrees with nearer subject · collective nouns (the government, the public)
gram2.note: At band 8–9, the remaining errors are often small agreement slips in long sentences. Find the true head noun: The welfare of animals kept in small cages IS a concern (welfare, not cages). The number of zoos HAS fallen, but a number of zoos HAVE improved. In British English, collective nouns can take a plural verb when you mean the members, but be consistent.

ex.t: The number of animals used in research has fallen.
ex.vi: Số lượng động vật dùng trong nghiên cứu đã giảm.

ex.t: A number of countries have banned cosmetic testing.
ex.vi: Một số nước đã cấm thử nghiệm mỹ phẩm.

ex.t: One of the main concerns is the welfare of farm animals.
ex.vi: Một trong những mối lo chính là phúc lợi động vật trang trại.

ex.t: Neither the zoo nor the farmers were willing to comment.
ex.vi: Cả sở thú lẫn nông dân đều không muốn bình luận.

drill.vi: Phúc lợi của động vật trong sở thú đang được tranh luận.

drill.t: A number of species ___ recovered.
drill.vi: Một số loài đã phục hồi.

drill.t: One of the cages ___ empty.
drill.vi: Một trong những chiếc lồng trống.

drill.vi: Mỗi đề xuất đều có giá trị.

cue.card: Describe an animal that is important in your country.
points: and explain whether its importance has changed
model: I’d like to talk about the water buffalo, which has played a central role in Vietnamese life for thousands of years — so much so that it appears on ancient bronze drums and in countless folk songs.

Its importance was, first and foremost, practical. In a rice-growing civilisation, the buffalo ploughed the flooded fields, pulled carts and, for many poor families, represented by far their most valuable possession; there’s a saying that the buffalo is “the beginning of the family fortune”. Beyond that, it became a symbol of hard work, patience and the bond between farmers and the land. Many older Vietnamese people, including my father, have warm childhood memories of herding buffalo after school and lying on their backs in the fields.

Its importance has, however, changed dramatically. In most of the country, tractors have replaced buffalo for ploughing, and the number of buffalo has declined considerably over recent decades. Today the animal is more symbolic than economic — it appears in art, festivals and tourism. One of the more controversial changes is the growth of buffalo fighting festivals, which are defended as tradition but criticised by animal welfare groups. My own feeling is mixed: I’m glad farmers no longer depend on such exhausting labour, but I think something of the old relationship between people and animals has been lost, and I’d rather the buffalo were remembered for its partnership with farmers than for staged fights.

write.prompt: Some people think that keeping animals in zoos is cruel and should be stopped. Others believe that zoos play an important role in protecting animals. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
plan: Introduction: precise paraphrase + position (zoos as they commonly exist should be phased out; accredited conservation institutions justified)
Body 1: case against — welfare evidence (stereotypic behaviour), unsuitable species, entertainment motive, weak conservation in many zoos
Body 2: case for — captive breeding and reintroduction examples, research, education, funding for field conservation
Conclusion: distinguish good from bad; strict accreditation; focus on species that benefit
model: The question of whether animals should be kept in zoos continues to provoke strong disagreement. Some regard such institutions as inherently cruel, while others maintain that they make a vital contribution to conservation. In my view, many zoos, particularly those run primarily for entertainment, cannot be justified and should be closed; however, well-regulated institutions that focus on conservation still have an important role to play.

Critics of zoos have substantial evidence on their side. Many animals in captivity, especially wide-ranging species such as elephants, polar bears and large cats, display repetitive behaviours like pacing or swaying, which are widely recognised as signs of psychological distress. Small or poorly funded zoos often keep animals in enclosures that bear little resemblance to their natural habitats, and their primary purpose is to attract paying visitors rather than to protect species. Furthermore, only a minority of animals kept in zoos belong to endangered species, which weakens the claim that captivity is necessary for their survival.

Nevertheless, the best zoos have achieved results that would otherwise have been impossible. Captive breeding programmes have saved several species from extinction, including the Arabian oryx and the California condor, both of which have been successfully reintroduced into the wild. Accredited zoos also contribute to scientific research on animal health and reproduction, and many fund conservation projects in the animals’ native habitats. In addition, seeing living animals can foster a lasting concern for wildlife, particularly among children who have little contact with nature.

In conclusion, the debate is not so much about whether zoos should exist as about what kind of zoos should exist. Institutions that confine animals mainly for public entertainment, or that keep species known to suffer in captivity, should be phased out. By contrast, zoos that meet strict welfare standards, concentrate on species that genuinely benefit from captive breeding and support conservation in the wild deserve continued support.

units.title: Social mobility
units.goal: Analyse whether people can rise from their background, using multiples and proportions precisely and evidence verbs with care.

words.ex: Education helped her climb the social ladder.
words.exVi: Giáo dục giúp cô ấy leo lên nấc thang xã hội.

words.vi: sự đi lên về địa vị
words.ex: Upward mobility has slowed in many rich countries.
words.exVi: Sự đi lên về địa vị đã chậm lại ở nhiều nước giàu.

words.ex: Recruitment should be merit-based.
words.exVi: Tuyển dụng nên dựa trên năng lực.

words.vi: hoàn cảnh kinh tế – xã hội
words.ex: Results still correlate with socio-economic background.
words.exVi: Kết quả học vẫn tương quan với hoàn cảnh kinh tế – xã hội.

words.vi: sinh viên thế hệ đầu (đầu tiên trong nhà học ĐH)
words.ex: First-generation students often lack guidance.
words.exVi: Sinh viên thế hệ đầu thường thiếu định hướng.

words.ex: Unpaid internships favour those with privilege.
words.exVi: Thực tập không lương ưu ái người có đặc quyền.

words.vi: mạng lưới quan hệ đồng môn (đặc quyền)
words.ex: Jobs in finance were filled through the old boys’ network.
words.exVi: Việc làm trong ngành tài chính được lấp qua mạng lưới quan hệ.

words.vi: “sàn kính” (giữ con nhà khá giả không tụt xuống)
words.ex: Wealthy families create a glass floor for their children.
words.exVi: Gia đình giàu tạo “sàn kính” cho con cái.

words.vi: sự truyền lại qua các thế hệ
words.ex: There is strong intergenerational transmission of income.
words.exVi: Thu nhập được truyền lại mạnh qua các thế hệ.

words.ex: Cultural capital helps in job interviews.
words.exVi: Vốn văn hoá giúp ích trong phỏng vấn xin việc.

words.ex: Spending on private tutoring is enormous in East Asia.
words.exVi: Chi tiêu cho học thêm ở Đông Á rất lớn.

words.ex: Scholarships aim to create a level playing field.
words.exVi: Học bổng nhằm tạo sân chơi bình đẳng.

words.ex: Disadvantaged pupils start school behind.
words.exVi: Học sinh thiệt thòi bắt đầu đi học đã chậm hơn.

words.ex: The earnings gap persists even among graduates.
words.exVi: Khoảng cách thu nhập vẫn còn ngay cả giữa người có bằng.

words.vi: từ nghèo khó đến giàu sang
words.ex: Rags-to-riches stories are inspiring but rare.
words.exVi: Chuyện từ nghèo đến giàu truyền cảm hứng nhưng hiếm.

words.ex: Parental income correlates with children’s test scores.
words.exVi: Thu nhập cha mẹ tương quan với điểm thi của con.

words.ex: Wealthy children get a head start before school.
words.exVi: Trẻ nhà giàu có lợi thế xuất phát trước khi đi học.

words.vi: chính sách ưu tiên (nhóm thiệt thòi)
words.ex: Affirmative action remains highly controversial.
words.exVi: Chính sách ưu tiên vẫn gây tranh cãi lớn.

words.vi: đường cong Gatsby (bất bình đẳng cao → dịch chuyển thấp)
words.ex: The Great Gatsby curve links inequality with low mobility.
words.exVi: Đường cong Gatsby liên hệ bất bình đẳng với dịch chuyển thấp.

words.ex: Richer students are twice as likely to graduate.
words.exVi: Sinh viên khá giả có khả năng tốt nghiệp cao gấp đôi.

lines.t: Did your parents go to university?
lines.vi: Bố mẹ bạn có học đại học không?

lines.t: No, neither of them did — my father was a mechanic and my mother sold vegetables at the market — so I was a first-generation student. They were determined that I should have opportunities they never had.
lines.vi: Không, cả hai đều không — bố tôi là thợ máy và mẹ bán rau ở chợ — nên tôi là sinh viên thế hệ đầu. Họ quyết tâm để tôi có những cơ hội họ chưa từng có.

lines.t: Was it difficult for you?
lines.vi: Điều đó có khó khăn với bạn không?

lines.t: Academically, not especially, but socially it was. Many classmates had studied abroad or had parents in senior jobs, and they seemed to know unwritten rules — how to network, which internships to apply for — that nobody had taught me.
lines.vi: Về học thuật thì không quá khó, nhưng về xã hội thì có. Nhiều bạn từng du học hoặc có bố mẹ làm vị trí cao, và họ dường như biết những luật bất thành văn — cách kết nối, nên ứng tuyển thực tập nào — mà chẳng ai dạy tôi.

lines.t: Do you think anyone can succeed if they work hard?
lines.vi: Bạn có nghĩ ai chăm chỉ cũng có thể thành công không?

lines.t: Hard work matters enormously, but I’d be cautious about saying “anyone”. Background clearly shapes how far the same effort takes you.
lines.vi: Chăm chỉ rất quan trọng, nhưng tôi sẽ thận trọng khi nói “ai cũng”. Xuất thân rõ ràng quyết định cùng một nỗ lực đưa bạn đi xa đến đâu.

sents.t: Economists have observed that countries with higher income inequality tend to have lower intergenerational mobility, a relationship nicknamed the Great Gatsby curve.
sents.vi: Các nhà kinh tế nhận thấy nước có bất bình đẳng thu nhập cao hơn thường có dịch chuyển giữa các thế hệ thấp hơn, mối quan hệ được gọi là đường cong Gatsby.

sents.t: In Denmark, a child’s future earnings are only weakly linked to their parents’ income.
sents.vi: Ở Đan Mạch, thu nhập tương lai của trẻ chỉ liên hệ yếu với thu nhập cha mẹ.

sents.t: In the United States and the United Kingdom, the link is roughly two to three times as strong.
sents.vi: Ở Mỹ và Anh, mối liên hệ mạnh hơn khoảng hai đến ba lần.

sents.t: Researchers caution that the curve shows correlation rather than causation, and that measuring mobility across countries involves considerable uncertainty.
sents.vi: Nhà nghiên cứu lưu ý đường cong chỉ cho thấy tương quan chứ không phải nhân quả, và đo lường dịch chuyển giữa các nước có độ bất định đáng kể.

sents.t: Nevertheless, the pattern has been widely cited in debates about education and taxation.
sents.vi: Dù vậy, quy luật này được trích dẫn rộng rãi trong tranh luận về giáo dục và thuế.

q.q: Parental income strongly determines children’s earnings in Denmark.
The curve proves that inequality causes low mobility.
The pattern has been used in debates about taxation.

gram.title: Multiples and proportions
gram.rule: twice / three times as + adj + as · twice / three times the + noun (of) · X times more likely to · a fraction / a third of
gram.note: Precise quantification marks band 9 range. Note the patterns: twice as likely as, three times the rate of, half as many as. Avoid the ambiguous “three times less”; prefer “a third of”.

ex.t: Wealthier students are twice as likely to attend university.
ex.vi: Sinh viên khá giả có khả năng vào đại học cao gấp đôi.

ex.t: Private schools spend three times the amount per pupil.
ex.vi: Trường tư chi gấp ba lần mỗi học sinh.

ex.t: Poorer children receive a fraction of the tutoring.
ex.vi: Trẻ nghèo chỉ nhận được một phần nhỏ việc học thêm.

ex.t: Graduates earn about half as much again as non-graduates.
ex.vi: Người có bằng kiếm nhiều hơn khoảng một nửa so với người không có bằng.

drill.t: They are three times ___ likely to succeed.
drill.vi: Họ có khả năng thành công gấp ba lần.

drill.t: The rate is twice ___ of rural areas.
drill.vi: Tỉ lệ cao gấp đôi so với vùng nông thôn.

drill.t: They earn a ___ of what their bosses earn.
drill.vi: Họ chỉ kiếm một phần nhỏ so với sếp.

drill.t: Twice ___ many students applied this year.
drill.vi: Số sinh viên nộp đơn năm nay gấp đôi.

lines.t: Is education the best way to increase social mobility?
lines.vi: Giáo dục có phải cách tốt nhất để tăng dịch chuyển xã hội không?

lines.t: It’s necessary but not sufficient. If wealthier families can always buy an advantage — private tutoring, internships through contacts, help with a first home — then expanding education may simply raise the bar rather than level the playing field. Labour-market and housing policy matter just as much.
lines.vi: Nó cần thiết nhưng chưa đủ. Nếu gia đình khá giả luôn mua được lợi thế — học thêm, thực tập nhờ quan hệ, hỗ trợ mua nhà đầu tiên — thì mở rộng giáo dục có thể chỉ nâng ngưỡng chứ không tạo sân chơi bình đẳng. Chính sách lao động và nhà ở cũng quan trọng không kém.

lines.t: Is a perfect meritocracy desirable?
lines.vi: Một chế độ trọng dụng nhân tài hoàn hảo có đáng mong muốn không?

lines.t: Interestingly, some philosophers argue not. In a perfect meritocracy, those at the bottom would be told their position is deserved, which could be crushing, while those at the top might become arrogant. I think we should aim for fair opportunities and also a decent life regardless of outcome.
lines.vi: Thú vị là một số triết gia cho rằng không. Trong chế độ trọng dụng hoàn hảo, người ở đáy sẽ bị nói rằng vị trí của họ là xứng đáng, điều có thể rất nặng nề, còn người ở đỉnh có thể trở nên kiêu ngạo. Tôi nghĩ nên hướng tới cơ hội công bằng và đồng thời cuộc sống tử tế dù kết quả ra sao.

lines.t: How has social mobility changed in your country?
lines.vi: Dịch chuyển xã hội ở nước bạn thay đổi thế nào?

lines.t: My parents’ generation experienced enormous upward mobility because the whole economy was growing so fast. For my generation, the evidence suggests it’s becoming harder, partly because housing in cities has become so expensive that family wealth matters more.
lines.vi: Thế hệ bố mẹ tôi trải qua sự đi lên rất lớn vì cả nền kinh tế tăng trưởng nhanh. Với thế hệ tôi, bằng chứng cho thấy điều đó đang khó hơn, một phần vì nhà ở thành phố quá đắt nên tài sản gia đình quan trọng hơn.

gram2.title: Evidence verbs with precise strength
gram2.rule: prove / demonstrate (strong) · indicate / show (moderate) · suggest / point to (tentative) · imply (indirect)
gram2.note: Choosing the right reporting verb shows you understand the strength of evidence. Correlational studies rarely prove anything; they suggest or point to relationships. Overclaiming with “prove” is a common band 7 error.

ex.t: The data suggest a link between inequality and mobility.
ex.vi: Dữ liệu cho thấy có mối liên hệ giữa bất bình đẳng và dịch chuyển.

ex.t: These findings point to the importance of early years.
ex.vi: Những phát hiện này chỉ ra tầm quan trọng của những năm đầu đời.

ex.t: The trial demonstrated that tutoring improves results.
ex.vi: Thử nghiệm chứng minh học thêm cải thiện kết quả.

ex.t: This implies that schools alone cannot close the gap.

cue.card: Describe someone who achieved success despite a difficult start in life.
points: and explain what you have learned from them
model: I’d like to talk about one of my former lecturers, Dr Thao, who grew up in a remote commune in Ha Giang and is now an associate professor of public health.

Her start in life was difficult in almost every respect. Her family were subsistence farmers, the nearest secondary school was a two-hour walk away, and as a girl from an ethnic minority she was expected to leave school early to marry. She has told us that she studied by an oil lamp because the village had no reliable electricity, and that she had only one textbook, shared between three students.

Despite this, she won a place at a boarding school for ethnic minority students, then a scholarship to university in Hanoi and eventually a PhD in Australia. She now leads research on maternal health in mountainous provinces and has helped set up a mentoring programme for first-generation students.

What I’ve learned from her is twofold. Obviously, her persistence is inspiring. But she’s also very honest that her story is exceptional and shouldn’t be used to imply that anyone could do the same. She always emphasises the specific policies that helped her — the boarding school, the scholarship, a teacher who lent her books — and argues that social mobility depends far more on such structures than on individual heroism. That changed how I think about success.

write.prompt: Some people believe that in today’s society, anyone can succeed through hard work regardless of their background. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase; position — disagree to a considerable extent
Body 1: concession — effort matters; examples of mobility; expanded education and technology
Body 2: main argument — background shapes starting points, accumulated advantages, networks and wealth, Great Gatsby curve
Body 3: implication — policy to equalise opportunity
Conclusion
model: It is often claimed that modern societies are meritocracies in which anyone who works hard enough can succeed, whatever their origins. While I accept that effort remains important and that opportunities have expanded, I disagree to a considerable extent, since a person’s background continues to shape both their starting point and the rewards their effort brings.

There is some truth in the meritocratic view. Mass education, scholarships and the internet have given millions of people access to knowledge and careers that were unavailable to their parents, and many individuals from modest backgrounds have risen to prominent positions. In rapidly growing economies such as Vietnam’s, an entire generation has experienced substantial upward mobility. Hard work is clearly a necessary condition for most forms of success.

However, it is far from a sufficient condition. Children from wealthier families typically benefit from better nutrition, more educated parents, private tutoring and quieter places to study, so that differences in attainment are visible before they even start school. These advantages accumulate: affluent students are several times as likely to attend elite universities, can afford unpaid internships, and draw on family networks and cultural capital when seeking employment. Inherited wealth, particularly in the form of housing, further widens the gap. International comparisons suggest that countries with greater inequality tend to have lower mobility, which indicates that the influence of background is not inevitable but depends on social structures.

This has important implications. If success depended solely on effort, the poor could reasonably be blamed for their situation. Recognising the role of background, by contrast, justifies policies such as high-quality early-years education, targeted support for disadvantaged pupils, transparent recruitment and fairer taxation of inheritance, which together can make opportunities more equal.

In conclusion, although hard work is essential, it does not guarantee success regardless of background. Genuine equality of opportunity remains an aspiration rather than a reality, and achieving it requires deliberate public policy.

lines.t: What is the strongest argument for universal basic income?
lines.vi: Lập luận mạnh nhất ủng hộ thu nhập cơ bản phổ quát là gì?

lines.t: For me, it’s simplicity and dignity. Means-tested systems are complicated, intrusive and full of welfare traps, where taking a low-paid job can leave you worse off. An unconditional payment avoids that and would also cover people the current system misses, like informal workers and unpaid carers.
lines.vi: Với tôi, đó là sự đơn giản và phẩm giá. Hệ thống xét theo thu nhập phức tạp, xâm phạm và đầy bẫy phúc lợi, nơi nhận một việc lương thấp có thể khiến bạn thiệt hơn. Khoản chi vô điều kiện tránh điều đó và bao phủ những người hệ thống hiện tại bỏ sót, như lao động phi chính thức và người chăm sóc không lương.

lines.t: And the strongest argument against it?
lines.vi: Còn lập luận mạnh nhất phản đối?

lines.t: Cost. Paying everyone a meaningful amount would require very large tax increases, and giving the same sum to millionaires seems an odd use of scarce public money. Targeted support might achieve more for the poorest at a fraction of the price.
lines.vi: Chi phí. Trả mọi người một khoản đáng kể đòi hỏi tăng thuế rất lớn, và trả cùng một khoản cho triệu phú có vẻ là cách dùng tiền công khan hiếm kỳ lạ. Hỗ trợ có mục tiêu có thể làm được nhiều hơn cho người nghèo nhất với chi phí chỉ bằng một phần nhỏ.

lines.t: Will automation make UBI necessary in the future?

lines.t: Possibly, but predictions of mass unemployment have been wrong before; new technologies have tended to create new jobs. If AI were to displace workers faster than they could retrain, though, some form of guaranteed income might become politically unavoidable.
lines.vi: Có thể, nhưng dự báo thất nghiệp hàng loạt từng sai trước đây; công nghệ mới thường tạo việc làm mới. Tuy vậy, nếu AI thay thế người lao động nhanh hơn tốc độ họ đào tạo lại, một dạng thu nhập đảm bảo có thể trở nên không tránh khỏi về chính trị.

cue.card: Describe something you would do if you did not have to work for money.
points: how you would organise your time
who you would do it with
and explain why this activity matters to you
model: If I didn’t have to work for money, I think I’d spend most of my time setting up and running a small community library and learning centre in my home town in Thanh Hoa.

At the moment there’s nowhere in the town where children can borrow books or get help with homework, and many parents work in factories until late. I’d rent a ground-floor space near the primary school, fill it with donated books and run free afternoon sessions — reading clubs for younger children and English or maths support for older ones.

In terms of time, I’d probably keep a fairly disciplined routine — mornings for planning, fundraising and my own reading, afternoons and early evenings with the children. Assuming the basic income covered my living costs, I could afford to do this full-time rather than squeezing it into weekends.

I’d do it with my cousin, who’s a primary teacher, and I’d hope to recruit retired teachers and university students home for the holidays. It matters to me because I benefited enormously from a teacher who lent me books when I was young, and I know how much difference that can make. Honestly, it’s the kind of work that has huge social value but no market value, which is precisely why so few people can afford to do it now.

write.prompt: Some people argue that governments should pay every citizen a basic income, regardless of whether they work. Do the advantages of this policy outweigh the disadvantages?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase; position — not yet, as universal; but partial or targeted versions promising
Body 1: advantages — security and dignity, removes welfare traps, covers informal/unpaid work, automation hedge, evidence on wellbeing
Body 2: disadvantages — fiscal cost and taxes, poor targeting, inflation risk, political sustainability, limited evidence
Body 3: evaluation — outweigh? Not at present; gradual, targeted cash transfers
Conclusion
model: Universal basic income, an unconditional payment made to every citizen, has moved from the margins of political debate into the mainstream, partly in response to fears about automation. While the idea has considerable merits, I believe that, at least in its fully universal form, its disadvantages currently outweigh its advantages.

The case for a basic income is compelling in several respects. By guaranteeing everyone a minimum level of security, it would protect people against sudden loss of income and give them greater bargaining power to refuse exploitative work. Because it is unconditional, it would avoid the complex, intrusive and often humiliating assessments of means-tested systems, as well as the welfare traps in which taking a low-paid job leaves claimants worse off. It would also reach groups that conventional welfare overlooks, such as informal workers and those providing unpaid care. Pilot schemes, notably in Finland, suggest that recipients experience improved mental health without significantly reducing their efforts to find work.

Nevertheless, the drawbacks are substantial. The most obvious is cost: a payment large enough to live on, given to every adult, would require tax increases on a scale few electorates would accept. Paying the same amount to wealthy and poor citizens alike is also an inefficient way to reduce poverty, since targeted support can achieve more for the most vulnerable at a fraction of the price. Some economists further warn that large unconditional payments could push up prices, particularly rents, eroding their value. Finally, the existing evidence comes from small, temporary trials, which cannot show how a permanent, nationwide scheme would affect work, migration or public finances.

Weighing these factors, I would argue that a fully universal basic income is not yet justified. However, many of its benefits could be captured through more modest measures, such as simplifying benefits, extending unconditional cash transfers to children or the poorest households, and gradually broadening coverage if evidence proves positive.

In conclusion, although basic income offers security, simplicity and dignity, its cost and poor targeting mean that its disadvantages currently outweigh its advantages. A cautious, incremental approach seems wiser than an immediate universal scheme.

lines.t: Has your neighbourhood changed in recent years?
lines.vi: Khu bạn sống gần đây có thay đổi không?

lines.t: Dramatically. Ten years ago it was a fairly run-down area with workshops and cheap rice stalls. Now there are artisan coffee shops, co-working spaces and a craft beer bar, and rents have roughly tripled.
lines.vi: Thay đổi rất nhiều. Mười năm trước đó là khu khá xuống cấp với xưởng sửa chữa và quán cơm bình dân. Giờ có quán cà phê thủ công, không gian làm việc chung và quán bia thủ công, và tiền thuê tăng gần gấp ba.

lines.t: Do you think those changes are positive?

lines.t: Mixed. The streets are cleaner and safer, which I appreciate. But many of the families I grew up with have been priced out, and the area feels less like a community.
lines.vi: Lẫn lộn. Đường phố sạch và an toàn hơn, điều tôi trân trọng. Nhưng nhiều gia đình tôi lớn lên cùng đã bị giá cả đẩy đi, và khu này ít còn cảm giác cộng đồng.

lines.t: Would you like to live somewhere else?
lines.vi: Bạn có muốn sống ở nơi khác không?

lines.t: Not really, though I may have no choice if my landlord raises the rent again.
lines.vi: Không hẳn, dù tôi có thể không có lựa chọn nếu chủ nhà lại tăng tiền thuê.

sents.t: The term “gentrification” was coined in 1964 by the sociologist Ruth Glass to describe middle-class families moving into working-class areas of London.
sents.vi: Thuật ngữ “gentrification” được nhà xã hội học Ruth Glass đặt ra năm 1964 để mô tả gia đình trung lưu chuyển vào khu lao động ở London.

sents.t: Some recent studies in American cities have found that original residents are not displaced as often as commonly assumed.
sents.vi: Một số nghiên cứu gần đây ở các thành phố Mỹ cho thấy cư dân cũ không bị đẩy đi thường xuyên như vẫn nghĩ.

sents.t: Residents who stay may even benefit from lower crime and better services, though they face higher living costs.
sents.vi: Cư dân ở lại thậm chí có thể hưởng lợi từ tội phạm giảm và dịch vụ tốt hơn, dù chịu chi phí sinh hoạt cao hơn.

sents.t: Other researchers argue that these studies underestimate the problem, because people who are forced out are hard to track.
sents.vi: Các nhà nghiên cứu khác cho rằng những nghiên cứu này đánh giá thấp vấn đề, vì những người bị buộc rời đi rất khó theo dõi.

sents.t: There is broad agreement, however, that the cultural character of gentrified areas often changes significantly.
sents.vi: Tuy nhiên, có sự đồng thuận rộng rãi rằng nét văn hoá của khu bị quý tộc hoá thường thay đổi đáng kể.

q.q: Ruth Glass first used the term to describe changes in London.
All studies agree that most original residents are forced to leave.
Ruth Glass lived in a gentrified area herself.

gram.title: Participle clauses of result and cause
gram.rule: …, + -ing (result: leading to, resulting in, forcing, making) · Having + p.p., … (cause) · -ing / p.p. clause at the start (cause)
gram.note: A participle clause after a comma can express the consequence of the main clause concisely: Rents tripled, forcing many families to leave. At the start of a sentence, it can express cause: Priced out of the centre, young families moved to the suburbs. The implied subject must match.

ex.t: Land values soared, pricing out local businesses.
ex.vi: Giá đất tăng vọt, đẩy doanh nghiệp địa phương ra ngoài.

ex.t: Developers bought the houses, leaving tenants with nowhere to go.
ex.vi: Nhà phát triển mua nhà, khiến người thuê không còn chỗ đi.

ex.t: Having lost their customers, the stalls closed.
ex.vi: Mất hết khách, các quán đã đóng cửa.

ex.t: Attracted by low rents, artists moved in first.
ex.vi: Bị thu hút bởi giá thuê rẻ, giới nghệ sĩ chuyển đến trước.

lines.t: Is gentrification always negative?
lines.vi: Quý tộc hoá có luôn tiêu cực không?

lines.t: No, and I think the word itself is something of a loaded term. Investment can bring safer streets, better schools and new jobs. The problem arises when the benefits go mainly to newcomers and property owners while long-standing tenants bear the costs.
lines.vi: Không, và tôi nghĩ bản thân từ này mang hàm ý. Đầu tư có thể mang lại đường phố an toàn hơn, trường tốt hơn và việc làm mới. Vấn đề nảy sinh khi lợi ích chủ yếu thuộc về người mới đến và chủ nhà, còn người thuê lâu năm gánh chi phí.

lines.t: How can cities improve neighbourhoods without displacing residents?
lines.vi: Thành phố có thể cải thiện khu phố mà không đẩy cư dân đi như thế nào?

lines.t: A combination of tools: inclusionary zoning so new developments include affordable units, some protection for tenants against sudden rent hikes, and giving residents a real voice in planning. Building more housing overall also helps, because scarcity is what drives prices up.
lines.vi: Kết hợp nhiều công cụ: quy hoạch bắt buộc để dự án mới có căn hộ giá rẻ, bảo vệ người thuê khỏi tăng giá đột ngột, và cho cư dân tiếng nói thực sự trong quy hoạch. Xây thêm nhà nói chung cũng giúp ích, vì khan hiếm là thứ đẩy giá lên.

lines.t: Does gentrification threaten local culture?
lines.vi: Quý tộc hoá có đe doạ văn hoá địa phương không?

lines.t: It can. When street vendors and family workshops disappear, an area may become indistinguishable from any other trendy district in the world. Ironically, the character that attracted newcomers in the first place is often what gets lost.
lines.vi: Có thể. Khi người bán hàng rong và xưởng gia đình biến mất, khu phố có thể trở nên giống hệt mọi khu sành điệu khác trên thế giới. Trớ trêu là chính nét đặc trưng thu hút người mới đến lại thường là thứ bị mất đi.

gram2.title: Connotation: neutral, positive and loaded words
gram2.rule: regeneration / renewal (positive) · change / redevelopment (neutral) · gentrification / displacement (critical)
gram2.note: At band 9, word choice reflects stance. Officials speak of “regeneration”; critics speak of “gentrification” and “displacement”. Recognising connotation helps you describe others’ views accurately and present your own precisely.

ex.t: The council calls it regeneration; residents call it displacement.
ex.vi: Chính quyền gọi đó là tái thiết; cư dân gọi là bị đẩy đi.

ex.t: “Redevelopment” sounds more neutral than “gentrification”.
ex.vi: “Tái phát triển” nghe trung tính hơn “quý tộc hoá”.

ex.t: Describing the area as a “slum” justified demolition.
ex.vi: Gọi khu đó là “khu ổ chuột” đã biện minh cho việc phá dỡ.

ex.t: Supporters frame it as urban renewal.
ex.vi: Người ủng hộ mô tả đó là sự đổi mới đô thị.

cue.card: Describe a neighbourhood that has changed a lot.
points: what it used to be like
and explain how you feel about these changes
model: I’d like to describe Thao Dien in Thu Duc, on the edge of Ho Chi Minh City, an area I’ve known since I was a child because my aunt lived there.

Twenty years ago, it was largely rural — a riverside area of fruit gardens, small fishing households and narrow dirt lanes, with only a handful of foreign families in large villas. My aunt sold drinks from her front room, and the main entertainment was watching boats on the Saigon River.

Since then, it has been transformed almost beyond recognition. Land values soared after the new bridges and later the metro line, attracting property developers, international schools and an influx of expatriates and wealthy young professionals. The lanes are now lined with upmarket restaurants, artisan bakeries and boutique hotels. Most of the original households have sold their land, some becoming quite rich, while tenants like my aunt’s neighbours were simply priced out.

My feelings are genuinely mixed. On the one hand, the area is cleaner, the roads are better and it’s full of life. On the other, it now feels like a district designed for outsiders; my aunt says she can’t afford a coffee on her own street. What saddens me most is that the riverside character that originally attracted people has largely disappeared. I think it shows that regeneration can benefit some groups enormously, but without planning, those who were there first rarely share in the gains.

write.prompt: In many cities, older working-class neighbourhoods are being redeveloped and becoming more expensive, forcing some original residents to move away. Is this a positive or negative development?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase; position — mixed, but negative as currently managed
Body 1: positives — investment, safety, services, jobs, owners’ gains
Body 2: negatives — displacement of tenants, loss of community and character, inequality
Body 3: what makes it positive — planning tools
Conclusion
model: Across the world, neighbourhoods that were once home to working-class communities are attracting investment and wealthier residents, a process often described as gentrification. As property prices and rents rise, some original residents are forced to leave. In my view, while this process brings genuine benefits, it is, as it is currently managed in most cities, a negative development.

It would be misleading to portray such change as wholly harmful. Investment frequently brings improved infrastructure, renovated buildings, safer streets and new businesses, creating employment and generating tax revenue that can fund public services. Residents who own their homes may benefit substantially from rising property values, and some studies suggest that those who manage to stay enjoy lower crime and better amenities.

Nevertheless, the costs fall disproportionately on the most vulnerable. Tenants, who typically make up a large share of working-class populations, have no stake in rising property values; instead they face rent increases, leaving many with no option but to move to distant suburbs, often far from their jobs, schools and support networks. Displacement thus breaks long-established community ties and may increase commuting time and costs. Moreover, as independent shops, street vendors and workshops are replaced by upmarket cafés and chain stores, neighbourhoods lose the distinctive character that made them attractive in the first place. The overall effect is often to deepen spatial inequality, concentrating wealth in city centres and pushing poverty to the periphery.

These outcomes, however, are not inevitable. Cities can capture the benefits of investment while limiting displacement by requiring new developments to include social housing, protecting tenants from sudden rent hikes, supporting local businesses and involving existing residents meaningfully in planning decisions.

In conclusion, the redevelopment of working-class neighbourhoods offers real improvements, but because its costs are borne mainly by low-income tenants and its benefits accrue largely to owners and newcomers, it is currently a negative trend. With deliberate and inclusive planning, however, it could become a positive one.

units.title: Philanthropy & charitable giving
units.goal: Evaluate charity, effective giving and billionaire philanthropy, using “however/whatever/no matter how” and finely graded evaluative adjectives.

words.exVi: Một nhà bảo trợ giấu tên tài trợ thư viện.

lines.t: Do you ever give money to charity?
lines.vi: Bạn có bao giờ quyên góp cho từ thiện không?

lines.t: Regularly, though not large amounts. I donate monthly to a children’s heart surgery fund, and during the floods in the central provinces I gave through a group I trusted because they publish detailed accounts.
lines.vi: Thường xuyên, dù không nhiều. Tôi quyên góp hằng tháng cho quỹ phẫu thuật tim trẻ em, và đợt lũ miền Trung tôi góp qua một nhóm tin cậy vì họ công bố sao kê chi tiết.

lines.t: Why is transparency important to you?
lines.vi: Vì sao sự minh bạch quan trọng với bạn?

lines.t: Because there have been several scandals in which online fundraisers kept a large share of donations. However generous people are, that kind of story causes donor fatigue.
lines.vi: Vì đã có nhiều bê bối khi người kêu gọi trên mạng giữ lại phần lớn tiền quyên góp. Dù người ta hào phóng đến đâu, những chuyện như vậy gây mệt mỏi cho người góp.

lines.t: Do you prefer giving money or volunteering time?
lines.vi: Bạn thích góp tiền hay góp thời gian tình nguyện?

lines.t: Money is usually more useful to professional organisations, but volunteering gives me a connection to the cause, so I try to do a bit of both.
lines.vi: Tiền thường hữu ích hơn cho tổ chức chuyên nghiệp, nhưng tình nguyện cho tôi sự gắn bó với mục tiêu, nên tôi cố làm cả hai.

sents.t: The effective altruism movement argues that donors should give where their money will do the most measurable good.
sents.vi: Phong trào vị tha hiệu quả cho rằng nhà tài trợ nên cho đi nơi đồng tiền tạo nhiều lợi ích đo lường được nhất.

sents.t: Charity evaluators estimate that some health programmes, such as distributing insecticide-treated bed nets, save a life for a few thousand dollars.
sents.vi: Các tổ chức đánh giá từ thiện ước tính một số chương trình y tế, như phát màn tẩm thuốc chống muỗi, cứu một mạng người với vài nghìn đô la.

sents.t: By contrast, many popular causes in wealthy countries achieve far less per dollar.
sents.vi: Ngược lại, nhiều mục tiêu phổ biến ở nước giàu đạt được ít hơn nhiều trên mỗi đô la.

sents.t: Critics argue that focusing only on what can be measured ignores causes such as human rights or the arts, whose benefits are harder to quantify.
sents.vi: Người phê phán cho rằng chỉ tập trung vào điều đo lường được sẽ bỏ qua các mục tiêu như nhân quyền hay nghệ thuật, vốn khó định lượng lợi ích.

sents.t: They also point out that the movement’s reputation was damaged when one of its best-known backers was convicted of fraud.
sents.vi: Họ cũng chỉ ra uy tín phong trào bị tổn hại khi một trong những người ủng hộ nổi tiếng nhất bị kết tội lừa đảo.

q.q: Some bed net programmes are estimated to save a life for a few thousand dollars.
Critics believe the arts should receive no donations.
Effective altruism originated in Vietnam.

gram.title: However / whatever / no matter how: concession with emphasis
gram.rule: however + adjective / adverb + subject + verb · whatever / whoever + clause · no matter how / what / who + clause
gram.note: These structures concede that something is true to any degree, yet the main point still holds: However generous a donation is, it cannot replace public services. Whatever their motives, billionaires’ donations save lives. No matter how much you give, transparency matters.

ex.t: Whatever their motives, the donations have saved lives.

ex.t: No matter how small, every donation counts.

lines.t: Do the very rich have a moral obligation to give away their wealth?
lines.vi: Người siêu giàu có nghĩa vụ đạo đức phải cho đi tài sản không?

lines.t: I’d say they have an obligation to contribute, but the most important contribution is paying fair taxes. Voluntary giving is commendable, yet it allows individuals to choose which causes matter, and those choices aren’t democratically accountable.
lines.vi: Tôi cho rằng họ có nghĩa vụ đóng góp, nhưng đóng góp quan trọng nhất là đóng thuế công bằng. Cho đi tự nguyện đáng khen, nhưng nó cho phép cá nhân tự chọn mục tiêu nào quan trọng, và những lựa chọn đó không chịu trách nhiệm giải trình dân chủ.

lines.t: Is large-scale philanthropy sometimes self-serving?
lines.vi: Từ thiện quy mô lớn có đôi khi vụ lợi không?

lines.t: Sometimes, undoubtedly. Companies may fund environmental projects while continuing to pollute, which amounts to reputation laundering. But whatever the motives, a vaccine programme that saves children’s lives is still valuable, so I try to judge outcomes as well as intentions.
lines.vi: Đôi khi, chắc chắn. Công ty có thể tài trợ dự án môi trường trong khi vẫn gây ô nhiễm, thực chất là tẩy trắng danh tiếng. Nhưng dù động cơ là gì, một chương trình vắc-xin cứu sống trẻ em vẫn có giá trị, nên tôi cố đánh giá cả kết quả lẫn ý định.

lines.t: Should charities or governments be responsible for helping the poor?
lines.vi: Tổ chức từ thiện hay chính phủ nên chịu trách nhiệm giúp người nghèo?

lines.t: Primarily governments, because they can provide reliable, universal support. Charities are excellent at reaching groups the state overlooks and at innovating, but they depend on donors’ moods and can’t guarantee continuity.
lines.vi: Chủ yếu là chính phủ, vì họ có thể cung cấp hỗ trợ ổn định, phổ quát. Tổ chức từ thiện rất giỏi tiếp cận nhóm nhà nước bỏ sót và đổi mới, nhưng phụ thuộc tâm trạng nhà tài trợ và không đảm bảo được tính liên tục.

gram2.title: Graded evaluative adjectives
gram2.rule: positive: commendable, laudable, admirable · neutral: well-intentioned, pragmatic · critical: self-serving, misguided, counterproductive
gram2.note: Nuanced evaluation distinguishes intention from effect: a well-intentioned but misguided project; a laudable aim pursued in a counterproductive way. Pair adjectives with “but” or “if” to show balanced judgement.

ex.t: Her commitment to the cause is admirable.
ex.vi: Sự tận tâm của cô ấy với mục tiêu thật đáng ngưỡng mộ.

ex.t: Sending used clothes can be counterproductive.
ex.vi: Gửi quần áo cũ có thể phản tác dụng.

ex.t: It is a laudable, if ambitious, goal.
ex.vi: Đó là mục tiêu đáng ca ngợi, dù đầy tham vọng.

cue.card: Describe a charity or organisation that helps people.
points: and explain why you think its work is valuable
model: I’d like to talk about a small Vietnamese charity that runs “zero-dong” bread and rice shops in several cities, where workers on low incomes can get a free or very cheap meal.

It mainly helps manual labourers, street vendors, motorbike taxi drivers and elderly people living alone — people who often skip meals to save money. In the shop near my office, you can see construction workers queuing at lunchtime alongside students and lottery ticket sellers.

The model is simple. Restaurants and individual donors contribute food or money, and volunteers distribute meals at fixed times. It’s run with very low overheads because the space is often donated and most staff are volunteers, and they post the daily accounts on their Facebook page, which I think explains why donors trust them.

I find its work valuable for a couple of reasons. Firstly, it is extremely cost-effective: a small donation translates directly into a hot meal for someone who needs it. Secondly, and perhaps more importantly, it’s done with dignity — there’s no form to fill in and nobody asks people to prove they’re poor. Of course, no matter how admirable it is, it can’t solve the underlying problem of low wages and weak social insurance, which is ultimately the government’s responsibility. But as a way of filling the gaps, I think it’s a model worth copying.

write.prompt: Some extremely wealthy people donate large sums of money to charity. Some people think this is the best way to solve social problems, while others believe it is the responsibility of governments. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
plan: Introduction: paraphrase; opinion — governments primary; philanthropy valuable complement
Body 1: case for philanthropy — speed, innovation, risk-taking, global causes, efficiency
Body 2: case for government — scale and continuity, democratic accountability, tax avoidance and self-interest, systemic causes
Body 3: own view — complementary roles; transparency
Conclusion
model: In recent decades, a number of billionaires have pledged vast fortunes to charitable causes, from global health to education. This has prompted debate about whether such philanthropy is the most effective way to address social problems or whether this responsibility belongs primarily to governments. In my view, while philanthropy plays a valuable role, governments must remain the main actors.

Supporters of large-scale philanthropy highlight its distinctive strengths. Private foundations can act quickly, without the delays of political processes, and can fund risky or innovative projects, such as new vaccines, that governments may avoid. Because they are not bound by national borders, they can also address global problems, including diseases that mainly affect poorer countries. Furthermore, some donors bring business expertise, insisting on measurable results and cost-effective programmes, which can make aid more efficient.

However, there are strong reasons to regard governments as primarily responsible. Social problems such as poverty, healthcare and education require permanent, large-scale and universal provision, which only states can guarantee; philanthropic funding, however generous, depends on the priorities and fortunes of individuals and may be withdrawn at any time. More fundamentally, democratic governments are accountable to citizens, whereas wealthy donors decide privately which causes deserve support, giving a small number of people disproportionate influence over public life. Critics also note that philanthropy can coexist with aggressive tax avoidance, so that the public loses more in revenue than it gains in donations, and that some giving serves to improve the reputation of companies whose activities contribute to the problems being addressed.

In my opinion, therefore, philanthropy and government action should be seen as complementary rather than alternatives. Governments, funded by fair and effectively collected taxes, should provide the essential foundations of welfare, while philanthropists can usefully support innovation, research and neglected causes, provided they operate transparently and do not seek to replace democratic decision-making.

In conclusion, although large donations from the wealthy can achieve impressive results, they cannot substitute for the sustained, accountable action of governments. The ideal is a partnership in which each does what it does best.

gram.title: Emphatic structures: do / did, by no means, far from, the very
gram.rule: auxiliary do / does / did + base verb · by no means · far from + -ing / adjective · the very + noun
gram.note: Emphatic do contradicts an expectation or stresses a contrast: I do enjoy shopping, but I try to resist. By no means and far from are formal negatives: Minimalism is far from new. The very marks something as precise or extreme: the very thing that attracted us.

lines.t: Why do people buy things they don’t need?
lines.vi: Vì sao người ta mua những thứ không cần?

lines.t: Partly because shopping is designed to be effortless and exciting — one-click payment, flash sales, countdown timers. But there’s also a social dimension: possessions signal status, so people feel pressure to keep up with the Joneses, and the comparison group is now everyone on social media.
lines.vi: Một phần vì mua sắm được thiết kế để dễ dàng và hấp dẫn — thanh toán một chạm, flash sale, đồng hồ đếm ngược. Nhưng còn khía cạnh xã hội: đồ đạc thể hiện địa vị, nên người ta chịu áp lực không thua kém người khác, và nhóm để so sánh giờ là tất cả mọi người trên mạng xã hội.

lines.t: Is minimalism a realistic alternative for most people?
lines.vi: Tối giản có phải lựa chọn thực tế cho đa số không?

lines.t: In its fashionable form, I’m sceptical. Owning only a few beautiful, expensive items is a privileged choice — poorer families often keep things because they can’t afford to replace them. But the underlying principle, buying less and valuing experiences, is by no means only for the rich.
lines.vi: Ở dạng thời thượng, tôi hoài nghi. Chỉ sở hữu vài món đẹp, đắt tiền là lựa chọn của người có điều kiện — gia đình nghèo thường giữ đồ vì không đủ tiền thay. Nhưng nguyên tắc cốt lõi, mua ít đi và coi trọng trải nghiệm, hoàn toàn không chỉ dành cho người giàu.

lines.t: Would the economy suffer if people bought less?
lines.vi: Kinh tế có bị ảnh hưởng nếu người ta mua ít đi không?

lines.t: In the short term, certainly — consumer spending supports millions of jobs. But an economy dependent on ever-increasing consumption of disposable goods isn’t sustainable environmentally. Shifting spending towards services, repairs and experiences could maintain employment with far less waste.
lines.vi: Ngắn hạn thì chắc chắn — chi tiêu tiêu dùng nuôi hàng triệu việc làm. Nhưng một nền kinh tế dựa vào tiêu thụ ngày càng nhiều hàng dùng một lần không bền vững về môi trường. Chuyển chi tiêu sang dịch vụ, sửa chữa và trải nghiệm có thể duy trì việc làm với ít rác thải hơn nhiều.

cue.card: Describe something you bought that you later regretted.
points: and explain why you regretted buying it
model: I’d like to talk about an expensive smartwatch that I bought about two years ago during a huge online sale on the eleventh of November.

To be honest, I didn’t really need it. A few colleagues had just bought the same model and kept talking about their step counts and sleep scores, and the advertising was very persuasive — it promised to make me healthier and more productive. The sale price, with a countdown timer ticking away on the screen, made it feel like an opportunity I’d regret missing. Looking back, it was a textbook impulse buy.

For the first month or so, I used it constantly, checking my steps and heart rate several times an hour. But the novelty wore off remarkably quickly. Charging it every day became a chore, the notifications were distracting, and I realised that knowing my step count didn’t actually make me exercise more. Within six months it was sitting in a drawer.

I regret it partly because of the money — it cost almost half a month’s rent — but mainly because it taught me something uncomfortable about myself. Far from being a rational decision, the purchase was about keeping up with my colleagues and the brief excitement of buying something new. Since then I’ve tried to apply a simple rule: if I still want something after thirty days, I can buy it. Most of the time, I don’t.

write.prompt: In many countries, people are buying more goods than ever before, yet surveys suggest they are not becoming happier. Why might this be the case? What could individuals and society do about it?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase paradox; preview
Body 1: causes — adaptation/hedonic treadmill, relative status and social comparison, debt and stress, time and environment costs
Body 2: solutions — individual (experiences, relationships, deliberate buying), societal (advertising limits, repair, public goods, work-time)
Conclusion
model: Over recent decades, rising incomes and online shopping have enabled people in many countries to buy unprecedented quantities of goods. Paradoxically, however, measures of happiness have in many cases remained stagnant. This essay will suggest reasons for this apparent contradiction and propose measures that individuals and society could take.

One explanation lies in human psychology. People adapt quickly to new possessions, so the pleasure of a purchase fades and is replaced by the desire for the next, a cycle sometimes described as the hedonic treadmill. Moreover, much consumption is driven by comparison with others: if satisfaction depends on having as much as one’s peers, then rising consumption across society brings little gain for anyone, particularly when social media expands the comparison group to include celebrities and influencers. Consumption can also undermine wellbeing directly, through debt incurred to finance purchases, the long working hours needed to pay for them and the time spent acquiring and maintaining possessions. Finally, growing awareness of the environmental damage caused by overconsumption may itself create unease.

Individuals can respond by spending more deliberately. Research suggests that money spent on experiences, on other people and on time-saving services tends to produce more lasting satisfaction than material goods. Simple habits, such as waiting before non-essential purchases or joining secondhand and sharing networks, can reduce impulse buying. Society, too, has a role. Governments could restrict manipulative advertising techniques, particularly those aimed at children, and support a culture of repair by requiring products to be durable and repairable. Investing in public goods, such as parks, libraries and community spaces, provides sources of wellbeing that do not depend on private consumption, while policies that allow shorter working hours give people more time for the relationships that matter most to happiness.

In conclusion, buying more does not make people happier largely because of adaptation, social comparison and the hidden costs of consumption. By spending more wisely and by building societies that value time, relationships and shared spaces, it is possible to pursue wellbeing more effectively than through ever-increasing consumption.

sents.vi: Phần lớn điều này phản ánh giá nhà tăng, có lợi cho người đã sở hữu trong khi khiến người trẻ khó bước vào thị trường hơn.

sents.t: At the same time, ageing populations mean that a shrinking number of workers must support a growing number of pensioners.
sents.vi: Đồng thời, dân số già nghĩa là số người lao động ngày càng ít phải nuôi số người hưởng lương hưu ngày càng nhiều.

sents.t: Some economists warn that framing this as a conflict between generations is misleading, since inequality within each generation is often greater than inequality between them.
sents.vi: Một số nhà kinh tế cảnh báo việc mô tả đây là xung đột giữa các thế hệ là sai lệch, vì bất bình đẳng trong mỗi thế hệ thường lớn hơn giữa các thế hệ.

sents.t: Many older people, for example, live on small pensions and own little property.
sents.vi: Ví dụ, nhiều người lớn tuổi sống bằng lương hưu ít ỏi và sở hữu ít tài sản.

q.q: Older people’s share of wealth has fallen over forty years.
Inequality within a generation can exceed inequality between generations.
Most pensioners in developed countries own several properties.

gram.title: Future perfect and future continuous for projections
gram.rule: will have + p.p. (completed before a future point) · will be + -ing (in progress at a future time) · by + time / by the time + present simple
gram.note: These forms are useful for projections in Part 3 and essays: By 2050, the population will have aged considerably. In twenty years, today’s students will be supporting a much larger elderly population. Note: by the time + present simple (not will).

ex.t: By 2040, the dependency ratio will have doubled.
ex.vi: Đến năm 2040, tỉ lệ phụ thuộc sẽ đã tăng gấp đôi.

ex.t: Today’s young workers will be paying for these pensions for decades.
ex.vi: Người lao động trẻ hôm nay sẽ đang trả cho những khoản lương hưu này trong nhiều thập kỷ.

ex.t: By the time I retire, the rules will have changed.
ex.vi: Đến khi tôi nghỉ hưu, quy định sẽ đã thay đổi.

ex.t: This time next year, I’ll be living in my own flat.
ex.vi: Giờ này năm sau, tôi sẽ đang sống trong căn hộ của mình.

drill.t: By 2050, sea levels ___ significantly.
drill.vi: Đến 2050, mực nước biển sẽ đã dâng đáng kể.

drill.t: By the time she ___, the debt will be repaid.
drill.vi: Đến khi bà nghỉ hưu, khoản nợ sẽ được trả.

drill.t: In 2040, more people ___ alone.
drill.vi: Năm 2040, nhiều người hơn sẽ đang sống một mình.

drill.t: By then, prices ___ again.
drill.vi: Đến lúc đó, giá sẽ đã tăng gấp đôi lần nữa.

lines.t: Do older generations have responsibilities to younger ones?
lines.vi: Thế hệ trước có trách nhiệm với thế hệ sau không?

lines.t: I think every generation has a duty of stewardship — to pass on institutions, a healthy environment and public finances in at least as good a state as they found them. The difficulty is that democratic politics encourages short-termism, because future generations can’t vote.
lines.vi: Tôi nghĩ mỗi thế hệ có nghĩa vụ gìn giữ — trao lại thể chế, môi trường lành mạnh và tài chính công ít nhất tốt như khi họ nhận. Khó khăn là chính trị dân chủ khuyến khích tư duy ngắn hạn, vì thế hệ tương lai không thể bỏ phiếu.

lines.t: Is it fair to blame older people for problems like expensive housing?
lines.vi: Đổ lỗi cho người lớn tuổi về những vấn đề như nhà đắt có công bằng không?

lines.t: Not really. Scapegoating a whole generation ignores the fact that most older people simply bought homes when they were affordable. The causes lie in policy — too little housing built, low interest rates, tax advantages for owners — and these can be changed.
lines.vi: Không hẳn. Đổ lỗi cho cả một thế hệ bỏ qua thực tế là phần lớn người lớn tuổi chỉ mua nhà khi giá còn phải chăng. Nguyên nhân nằm ở chính sách — xây quá ít nhà, lãi suất thấp, ưu đãi thuế cho người sở hữu — và những điều này có thể thay đổi.

lines.t: How can societies make sure future generations are considered?
lines.vi: Xã hội có thể làm gì để đảm bảo thế hệ tương lai được tính đến?

lines.t: Some countries have created institutions for this. Wales, for instance, has a commissioner for future generations who reviews major decisions. Long-term targets written into law, such as climate commitments, are another way of constraining short-termism.
lines.vi: Một số nước đã lập thể chế cho việc này. Ví dụ xứ Wales có uỷ viên phụ trách các thế hệ tương lai xem xét các quyết định lớn. Mục tiêu dài hạn được luật hoá, như cam kết khí hậu, là một cách khác để hạn chế tư duy ngắn hạn.

gram2.title: Cohesion through reference: this trend, such policies, the former / the latter
gram2.rule: this / these + summary noun · such + noun · the former … the latter … · both / neither of these
gram2.note: Band 9 cohesion depends on referring back precisely without repetition. Use a summary noun after this (this trend, this imbalance) rather than a bare “this”. Use the former / the latter only for two items.

ex.t: House prices have tripled; this trend has excluded many young buyers.
ex.vi: Giá nhà tăng gấp ba; xu hướng này loại nhiều người mua trẻ ra ngoài.

ex.t: Such policies favour existing owners.
ex.vi: Những chính sách như vậy ưu ái người đã sở hữu.

ex.t: Pensions and housing both matter, but the latter is more urgent.
ex.vi: Lương hưu và nhà ở đều quan trọng, nhưng cái sau cấp bách hơn.

ex.t: Neither of these measures is sufficient alone.
ex.vi: Không biện pháp nào trong số này tự nó là đủ.

drill.t: Prices rose sharply. ___ trend worries economists.
drill.vi: Giá tăng mạnh. Xu hướng này khiến các nhà kinh tế lo ngại.

drill.t: Of rent and debt, ___ is the bigger problem for students.
drill.vi: Giữa tiền thuê và nợ, cái sau là vấn đề lớn hơn với sinh viên.

drill.t: ___ measures are unpopular with voters.
drill.vi: Những biện pháp như vậy không được cử tri ưa.

drill.t: ___ of these solutions is perfect.
drill.vi: Không giải pháp nào trong hai cái là hoàn hảo.

cue.card: Describe a conversation you had with an older person that changed your opinion.
points: and explain how and why your opinion changed
model: I’d like to talk about a long conversation I had with my grandmother last Tết, when the two of us were left to wrap bánh chưng while everyone else went to the market.

We ended up talking about money and housing. I was complaining, rather bitterly, that her generation had it easy: land was cheap, everyone could build a house, and now my generation can’t afford even a small flat in the city.

Before that conversation, I genuinely believed that older people had simply been lucky and didn’t understand how hard things are for young people today. I’d absorbed quite a lot of that “boomers versus millennials” narrative from social media.

What changed my mind was hearing the details of her life. She described the post-war years when the family had almost nothing, when she worked in the fields and sold vegetables before dawn, and when the land they now own was considered almost worthless. She didn’t deny that my generation faces real difficulties — she was surprisingly sympathetic about housing — but she pointed out that every generation has its own hardships. I came away still thinking that housing policy is unfair to young people, but I realised that the problem lies in policy rather than in older people themselves, and that scapegoating a whole generation is both inaccurate and unkind.

write.prompt: Some people think that the current older generation has benefited at the expense of young people, for example through cheaper housing and generous pensions. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase; position — partly agree on outcomes, disagree with framing
Body 1: evidence of advantage — housing wealth, pensions, public debt and climate
Body 2: limits of the claim — inequality within generations, hardships older people faced, policy not people, families transfer wealth
Body 3: implications — policy reforms for intergenerational fairness
Conclusion
model: It is increasingly argued that today’s older generation has enjoyed advantages, such as affordable housing and generous pensions, that have come at the cost of young people. While I agree that economic outcomes have shifted in favour of older age groups in many countries, I disagree with the suggestion that one generation has deliberately benefited at the expense of another.

There is considerable evidence of a generational imbalance. In many economies, people who bought homes decades ago have seen their value multiply, whereas young adults now face prices many times their annual income, leaving them renting for longer and accumulating less wealth. Pension systems funded on a pay-as-you-go basis often promise current retirees benefits that will be difficult to sustain as the dependency ratio rises, meaning that today’s workers will be paying higher contributions for less generous future entitlements. Younger generations will also bear the long-term costs of public debt and, perhaps most significantly, of climate change caused largely by past emissions.

Nevertheless, the claim that older people benefited “at the expense of” the young oversimplifies the situation. Firstly, inequality within each generation is frequently greater than inequality between them: many pensioners live on modest incomes and own no property, while some young people stand to inherit substantial wealth. Secondly, older generations faced serious hardships of their own, including war, poverty and limited access to education. Thirdly, these imbalances are largely the result of policy decisions, such as insufficient house building and tax advantages for property owners, rather than the actions of individuals who simply bought homes when they were affordable. Indeed, within families, wealth often flows from older to younger members.

Such an analysis suggests that the solution lies in reforming policies rather than blaming a generation. Governments could increase housing supply, reform pensions gradually so that costs are shared fairly, and adopt long-term commitments, for example on climate, that protect the interests of future generations.

In conclusion, although economic trends have favoured older people in important respects, I do not accept that they have benefited deliberately at the expense of the young. Framing the issue as a conflict between generations obscures its policy causes and the inequalities that exist within every age group.
